name: He Who Fights With Monsters | Compendium Lorebook (spoiler level 3)
description: Derived from the HWFWM compendium (not a source). Spoiler level 3: Books 1-13. Book text takes precedence over the fan wiki; this file is regenerated by src/tools/lorebook.py.

1.comment: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.content: This primer is the foundation of the compendium. It explains the setting in plain language and summarises the facts that come up again and again. Later documents expand every section. Where a fact only becomes true later in the story it is marked (Later: Book N). The series follows Jason Asano, an ordinary Australian who is pulled out of his world by an accident and arrives, hairless and alone, in Pallimustus: a world very like Earth in size and shape, but soaked in magic. There, people absorb essences (crystallised magic), which give them supernatural abilities, and grow through ranks by hunting monsters and training. Adventurers, guilds, gods and rulers all depend on this system. Pallimustus has a twin, Earth, which was made from the same template but has much less magic, so its people do not know magic exists (at first). The two worlds are linked, and the link matters more and more as the story proceeds. Above both worlds sits a larger cosmos of great astral beings, gods, astral kings and other powers who rarely interact directly with mortals but shape their lives. In a roleplay you can set a story anywhere from the beginning (a rural iron-rank adventurer in Greenstone) to the end (a gold-rank world-defender at the edge of a cosmic war). The chief factors that change from period to period are: who knows what, how powerful the leading characters are, and what the dangers are (a Builder cult, a monster surge, messengers, vampires, Knowledge's plan).
keys: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.name: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*

2.content: Astral kings rule their own universes. Most are messengers' masters: the messengers are their servants, invaders of worlds, and carry the astral king's message. In Book 8 Jason discovers that he himself is an astral king, which makes him both a political danger among the messengers and an unusual ally to them.
2.name: Astral Kings and Messengers

3.content: Authority is what great astral beings and gods are made of, and the thing that lets them shape the cosmos. It cannot be taken by force and must be traded, it comes in a safe set state and a dangerous potential state, and it is guided by will. Sanctioning is how transcendent beings change one another: their authority is turned against them, or they change themselves with it. The books treat it as the cosmos's only real punishment, because an immortal cannot be killed. What it is: great astral beings are the most powerful entities in the cosmos, and "the nature of both themselves and their power was known as authority". Authority is "the fundamental power of the cosmos", and everything in physical reality is underpinned by it to some degree. Two states: set-state authority has been put to a purpose, which makes it fixed, defined and safe ("clay turned into a bowl"); potential-state authority is the unworked clay, "except the clay is actually enriched uranium". Jason's domains: his spirit domains are made of set-state authority, which he calls "the treehouse that I'm allowed to play in". His spirit realm is also an aspect of his authority. He thinks that if his domains broke down into potential-state authority it would kill him. Transformation zones: they are "areas of set-state authority breaking down into potential-state authority", the domes being the world sealing them like scabs.
3.name: Authority and Sanctioning

key: The Cosmic Throne and the Sundering
4.comment: The Cosmic Throne and the Sundering
4.content: The Cosmic Throne was the ultimate authority that regulated the great astral beings. They broke it long ago, replaced it with a web of pacts, and in time regretted it. Jason is asked to repair it during his transition to astral king, and to leave it empty. He does so at the end of Book 11, which sets a new status quo for the cosmos and, as a side effect, makes his interface the System. What it was: "the power that regulated cosmic forces, keeping the great astral beings adherent to their respective purposes". Transcendent entities have effectively infinite power, and authority is "the right for a transcendent being to employ their infinite power in a specific way", which keeps the cosmos in balance; the throne was "the ultimate authority". A neutral arbiter: the throne must be left empty, "a neutral arbiter without will, only purpose", as it was before the sundering. Raythe and Velius want someone who will claim the ultimate authority and then give it up without ever exercising it. The rules it enforces: "The rules of the cosmos are enforced by something called the Cosmic Throne. It was damaged long ago, but the throne has been restored and the rules are more dangerous to bend, let alone break". Knowledge says the rules "have been put back in place. By you, no less".
keys: The Cosmic Throne and the Sundering
4.name: The Cosmic Throne and the Sundering

5.content: Gods are transcendent beings outside physical reality, each focused on a single concept (Dominion, Healer, Knowledge, Death and more). They manifest avatars, speak with Akashic Speech, give followers essences and awakening stones that they can take back, and work miracles. In Jason's words in Book 8, "gods are like regional managers of full-blown universes". Churches are their institutions.
5.name: Gods and Churches

6.content: A great astral being (GAB) is a cosmic-scale transcendent: an aspect of the cosmos that embodies a concept such as construction, finality of death, time, entropy or dimensional integrity. They are not gods and are not bound by gods. Clive describes them in Book 1 as similar to gods but belonging to no world: they exist between worlds in the deep astral, "gods to the gods, although you wouldn't catch any gods saying that". They do not rule worlds directly. They act through vessels: mortals chosen to host them, and prime vessels, who carry the fullest part of their power. GABs cannot interact with physical reality directly; they recruit others to act for them. Authority: they generate it intrinsically. See 00_Cosmology_Overview.md. Mortal form: great astral beings enjoy mortal bodies. A vessel can be possessed; Clive notes it is possible, if far from ethical. Diamond-rank vessels of the great astral beings can withstand the strain and keep their selves, unlike the disposable vessels the Builder uses; eventually the soul can no longer cope and the vessel passes on the role, with no lingering effects and a stronger soul as a result. No fear of gods: Clive says a GAB is one of the few beings that need not fear a god's retribution, since the gods of Pallimustus cannot see into an astral space that is not part of their world. Sanctioning: see section 4.
6.name: Great Astral Beings

7.content: The Council of Kings is the nearest thing the messengers have to central leadership: a loose body of the strongest astral kings, the heirs of the side that won the old war against free messengers. It guides but does not rule, many astral kings stand outside it, and its members are rivals who cooperate. Its de facto leader is Jamis Fran Muskar. What it is: "the closest thing the messengers had to central leadership", represented in Book 10 by a collection of prime avatars, each belonging to a different member. Membership: it "ostensibly represents the strongest of the astral kings", with many others outside it, "even a few powerful eccentrics who have declined to be part of our little group". The council does not know how many astral kings stand outside it. Authority: "The Council of Kings may guide us, but you do not rule us". Jamis says he is a member and that some consider him its leader, "although it has no such thing". Tera Jun Casta calls him "the closest thing we have to a true, singular leader". Not absolute: the council's power is not absolute, as what happened in Boko already shows, and controlling it is "a delicate affair". Rivalry: "Every person here is an enemy to everyone else in this room, yet we work together regardless". Messenger structure: astral kings rarely mix their forces, to protect the culture of hierarchy. Large operations are coordinated by meetings of Voices of the Will, the commanders of each king's local forces.
7.name: The Council of Kings

8.content: The astral is the space between worlds, the source of all magic, and the home of the beings who govern the cosmos. Clive explains it to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup in which worlds float. The deep astral has no geography, time or space of its own, and gold-rankers rarely travel in it without a patron. Interstice, the universe-city, is the capital of the part of it that anyone knows. The dumpling soup: Clive says the cosmos is "a bowl of dumpling soup". Each physical reality is a dumpling, and "the astral is the soup through which we are all the dumplings... floating". The astral is also the source of all magic, "pure, unadulterated; the most fundamental building blocks of reality". Why worlds differ: some worlds soak up a lot of the soup and others very little, which is why Pallimustus has essences, awakening stones, quintessence and monsters and Earth did not. Astral spaces: "think of the soup kind of congealing around a dumpling", giving a magical dimension attached to a world. Congealed magic can drift away, especially if someone pokes a hole in the world's side, and can touch another world to form a brief unstable link. What the deep astral is: "just magic. Only magic." Physical substance cannot exist there, which is why Jason's body "ceased to exist" when he was pulled through it. Only his soul, being magical, survived.
8.name: The Deep Astral and Interstice

9.content: The Rules (or Laws) of Intrusion govern who may invade a world and on what terms. They began as the rules for holy wars, where one faith invades the domain of another, and they also govern dimensional invasion. Since the Cosmic Throne was restored they are strict. Invaders need a pretext or an invitation, and until they meet the terms they are cut off from outside help. What they cover: "The Rules of Intrusion have always been in place. On my world, they mostly apply to holy wars, where one faith invades the domain of another. But, as it turns out, they also govern dimensional invasion". Jason describes them as a body of rules about "who can invade a world", including how one god can invade another's territory to conduct a holy war. Closed worlds: there are rules about intruding on worlds that have not declared themselves open to the cosmic community. Earth was opened to the wider cosmos, which let outside forces in. Bending them: the Jakaar pirate fleet makes its living on rules that "could be nudged" and others "pushed". The lower the rank, the less strenuous the rules, so a gold-rank crew can go places the admiral's main force cannot, and a thin pretence is enough to satisfy the rules for a low-to-mid magic world.
9.name: The Rules of Intrusion

10.content: The System is the interface of windows, ranks and messages that Jason carried alone from Book 1. When he restored the Cosmic Throne, an echo of him was imprinted on it, and his interface became available to everyone in the cosmos with essences or the potential to get them. He administers it through the System Administrator gift, with limits, and in Book 12 withdraws it from regions that keep slavery or indenture. Before: in Books 1 to 10 the interface is one of Jason's outworlder gifts, a private window, inventory and quest log; see../03_Magic_and_Adventuring/Unusual_and_Unique_Magic.md. The announcement: on every world with magic, every person who has essences or the potential for them sees a screen saying "Don't Panic. Everything is going to be fine. Welcome to the System", in whatever medium the species uses to communicate. Why: "The throne could never be restored to what it was. Part of you was imprinted upon it. An echo of you, spread across the cosmos", and "You made your interface available to everyone with essences or the potential to get them". What it does by default: it lets people view their own information and nothing more, but species gift evolutions and essence abilities are expanding the base effects, as they did for Jason.
10.name: The System

11.content: The Unorthodoxy is the messenger resistance: the descendants of the free messengers who lost the old war, who live in hiding without the brand and the indoctrination. They are few, scattered and short of allies, but they have astral kings of their own and hidden birthing planets, and a secret way of drawing extra power at their rank. Boris Ket Lundi is their agent on Earth and Pallimustus. Origin: Boris says that originally astral kings guided newborn messengers to form their own marks, and there was no rank limit because limits are a function of the brand. When messengers who had transcended became astral kings they instituted the brand and enslaved their own kind. There was war, the free lost, and the defeated went into hiding. "In time, the leaders of the enemy became the Council of Kings. We became the Unorthodoxy". The orthodox view: messenger society teaches that the Unorthodoxy is a scant few in the hidden crevices of society. Boris says most of that is inaccurate. Orthodox messengers hunt them diligently, and an orthodox commander worries that talk of a traitor astral king is the thinking that leads to the Unorthodoxy and a purge. Numbers and hiding: "the Unorthodoxy is scattered and lacking in allies. We hide because we lack the strength to fight, and nothing ever changes". They use different methods in each place so that losing one site does not expose them all.
11.name: The Unorthodoxy

12.content: The god of Death on Pallimustus governs the passage of souls into the astral, and is distinct from the Reaper, the great astral being who is "very big on the finality of death". The church certifies deaths and returns, opposes Undeath, and is dryly protective of the order of things. The deity changes guise, and the books speak of both a goddess and a lord. Domain: the Reaper is "very big on the finality of death. Some consider it the true god of death, as all our god of death governs is the passage of the soul into the astral". Where there is no god of death to guide the soul into the astral, it drifts into the Reaper's grasp on its own.
12.name: Death

13.content: Destruction is a god of the hidden kind, worshipped by those who want to destroy rather than rule. His church is small, secretive and well hidden, and its allies include the Church of Undeath. In Book 10 he takes an interest in the natural array under Yaresh, whose catastrophe or whose tree-turned-apocalypse-beast would serve him, and he speaks to Amos Pensinata through a prisoner priest. The hidden kind: Carlos explains that many gods fall into two camps: those with temples anywhere there are people, and "the gods whose priests dwell in the hidden places. Gods who you pray to not because of something you want, but something you want to avoid. Pain, Discord, Deceit". Destruction is not on his list, but the Book 10 priests work in the tunnels and the temples are hidden; the wiki also counts Destruction among the hidden gods. The priests under Yaresh: captured priests are found with a messenger communication orb in the tunnels of the natural array. The voice of the god: when Amos Pensinata presses a captured priest, "a new aura shrouded the prisoners, unmistakable in its divinity", and Destruction's voice rumbles "like an avalanche": "The souls of my priests are mine to toy with, not yours". Jason, as a nascent astral king, is unaffected by the god's will.
13.name: Destruction

14.content: Dominion is the god of rulership, the god "of deciding who gets to be king". He is young, handsome, sneering, charming and frank, he is the god most interested in Jason, and he turns up in person more often than any other. His church is the outlier among churches in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. For all his menace he gives Jason surprisingly honest advice. The temple and the creed: a believer in the Divine Square calls it the temple of Dominion and says "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves". First appearance: at Jory's clinic he comes to take the Healer's cast-out clergy, "young and handsome, but with a look of disdain and faint cruelty", with an aura like a wave of fire. He tells those who join: "There is no service in my church... under me, you will obey or suffer. Or both, as I choose, because you will not enter my service. You will belong to me". Jason and Gary: "I love that guy," Dominion says of Jason, because "the ones who won't kneel are always the most fun". He tests Gary with his gaze, laughs when Gary stands, and says "That is where monarchs come from. I love them most of all. I'll be keeping an eye on you, Gareth Xandier". He asked after Jason by name.
14.name: Dominion

15.content: Fertility is the god of growth and birth, and his church is far more practical than its murals suggest. It grows children in vats, bridges races so that mixed couples can have children, supplies food in surges, and in Book 12 is the thing the brighthearts most need to rebuild their people. Its temples are covered in murals of people being fertile, which Jason notes with some alarm. The murals: Jason avoids pairing with "the god of fertility? The one with all the provocative murals?", and Farrah describes the temples as covered "in murals of people... being fertile".
15.name: Fertility

16.content: Hearth is a god of home and shelter. The books show only its church at work: its priests organise people who have lost their homes, alongside the church of Refuge. This file records what the text says. The Healer's Hearth ritual: Neil asks whether a procedure is "the Healer's Hearth ritual", suggesting a ritual named for Hearth is used by the Church of the Healer. Organising refugees: after Boko's destruction, Jason says "The priests of Hearth and of Refuge will be organising the people. Who wants to settle permanently, who wants to find a new home, and who wants to wait for the reconstruction of Boko". In Jason's kingdom: the clergy in his astral kingdom stay for his journey to Earth. The first contingent came from the churches of Hearth, Refuge and Dominion, and others joined as the work expanded, mostly for the logistics of a population in the tens of thousands.
16.name: Hearth

17.content: Hero is the god of heroes, the only core deity without subordinate gods. He appears in the books almost only through the Cup of Heroes, a miracle that makes a dying hero a demigod at a terrible price. Hero is regretful about it, and by Book 11 plans to sanction himself to give mortals a gentler option. Name and rank: Jason notes "the god of heroes is called Hero. They really stick to that straightforwards naming convention". Hero is "the only core deity not to have subordinate gods". Appearance: a leonid larger than Gary's demigod form, with a divine aura. The Cup of Heroes: when Gary goes out to die against the undead, Hero appears and tells him his choice, not his life, was the sacrifice: "You believed that you came here to die. People keep thinking that what the gods want in sacrifice is their lives, but that is not the case". He conjures a goblet, a dewdrop falls into it, and Gary snatches it, saying "I know what it is". Hero calls his choice the reason both are there. What it does: Gary drinks, and the window says he has absorbed divine power belonging to the god of heroes, which will leave his soul unless he is isolated from the god's influence, and reforges his body into a gestalt. His hammer, fire and iron essences become Divine versions at Gold 0 and his forge confluence is replaced by a Demigod essence. The aftermath: Hero acts "like a proud but sad father". Jason, learning of it, speaks in a flat voice, and Farrah warns him not to do anything crazy.
17.name: Hero

18.content: The goddess of Knowledge is the god Jason meets first and speaks to most. She is detached, polite, honest in form and a planner at heart, and she knows everything anyone in her world knows. Her church is scholarly and wealthy and funds research, and from Book 6 on it is shown mustering armies. By Book 13 the books reveal she has worked for centuries to invade Earth. Appearance: in the Divine Square a glorious light appears in front of a temple and the people fall to their knees. In her temple she takes the form of a woman with colourful clothes and Mediterranean features, "beautiful, yet there was something detached and untouchable about her". She says "I am Knowledge. Everything that is, or ever was known in this world". Omniscience, limited: she knows what anyone in her world knows, including what Jason brought with him. Jason says in a recording that deities are gender fluid, "heard from the goddess of knowledge herself", and jokes that she knows his Mario Kart shortcuts. The church: acolytes of the church check Adventure Society assessments, "don't try to slip anything past them, because there isn't any point". Gabrielle Pellin introduces herself as an acolyte. Danielle Geller will send her scholarly relatives to the temple's library, as "the goddess always welcomes seekers of truth". Gifts to Jason: a token the goddess claimed would send him home and books on dimensional transgression, which Clive annotates.
18.name: Knowledge

19.content: Pain and Discord belong to the "hidden" gods, the gods people pray to for what they want to avoid. The books mention them only in passing. This file records every thing the text says, so that a story using them knows how much is open. The hidden gods: Carlos says many gods fall into two camps: those whose temples are anywhere there are people, and "the gods whose priests dwell in the hidden places. Gods who you pray to not because of something you want, but something you want to avoid. Pain, Discord, Deceit". These are the "dark gods" who "will do very well" if the Purity deception becomes public, and Carlos does not like "the idea of my actions serving the God of Discord". Pain, a god or a goddess: a soldier thinks of Pain as a god, but Kerr answers, "Where I come from, they know that Pain is a woman", and refers to "the Goddess of Pain's firstborn daughter". Gods are gender-fluid in the books. A byword for fear: Trenchant says that against an affliction skirmisher he would "run like the God of Pain was chasing me". Discord: it is called out as "in particular" the god the deception benefits.
19.name: Pain and Discord

20.content: Purity is the god of cleanliness, with both gentle and extreme aspects; his church is rich, strict and prominent in Greenstone. For centuries the god in the Church of Purity was not Purity but Disguise, who masqueraded in his place with Knowledge's help. The church's collusion with the cult of the Builder, Disguise's role in the Order of Redeeming Light, and the real Purity's relic are the revelations behind the Book 3, 8 and 10 plots. The church: Anisa Lasalle is a priestess of the God of Purity, and a priest of Purity in clean robes attends the Adventure Society inquiry team. The temple has church militants who guard its interests. Collusion with the Builder cult: when the church's involvement with the cult comes to light, a number of its key members vanish on "previously scheduled sabbaticals", including the archbishop Nicolas Hedron. The people from the church are detained under the authority of the ecumenical council. Hendren: the archbishop calls out, "You think afflictions can take down a priest of Purity?" in the fight.
20.name: Purity and Disguise

21.content: The god of medicine and healing, the Healer is kind, modest in manner and strict with those who exploit the sick. His church runs clinics, hospitals and research. In Book 1 he casts out the corrupt clergy of the Greenstone temple in person, and in later books his priests, among them Neil, Carlos and Arabelle, are central members of Jason's team. Corruption in Greenstone: Neil Davone makes a stand in the Greenstone Temple of the Healer, saying "This isn't about serving the Healer", and is told he is no longer welcome in the church. The god arrives: the Healer appears at Jory's clinic, tells his clergy that merely not being shunned from his temples is "mercy enough", and refuses to restore their essences: "For that, I shall give you no salve. But you may turn to another". He says the power-seekers are of no use to him and hands them to Dominion, who takes those willing. A blessing: he declares the clinic a sanctuary for healing, accepts that Jory's alchemy includes "togetherness jelly" ("I'm not going to begrudge people a little... togetherness"), and promises rituals of sanctification and a healer to staff it. Those who repent: he answers a plea from a priest with "You blame others for your failings?", and gives a slight nod of assent to those who accept responsibility.
21.name: The Healer

22.content: Undeath is the god of the unliving, the dark counterpart of Death. His church lies dormant for generations and strikes when it has saved up the god's chances to intervene. In Book 10 it nearly destroys the Cardinas expedition, and in Book 11 Jason sanctions the echo of Undeath's authority left in an avatar. Undeath is a menacing but brisk god who compromises with other gods, including the high priestess of Destruction whose grandson serves in his church. Early notice: Gary says "Undeath is bad". A character recalls a zombie plague with a Temple of Undeath at its heart, whose high priest was the local mayor. How the church acts: Hana Shavar says the Church of Undeath "does not act frequently. We don't give them the chance", so it lies dormant for generations and strikes when it gets one. "It's like their god has been saving up his chances to intervene in the world. Expect to see some dark miracles". Garth and Jameela: Garth, a zemravore, leads the church's priests in Cardinas, and with Jameela commands the undead. Garth's tactic: "The harder-fought the battle, the more we have to work with when it's done", and every battle that does not crush them makes the church stronger. Claiming territory: Jason sees the god seeping into the ground and making it his domain, marked by purple light. Death says "Undeath has been liberally spending his influence in this place".
22.name: Undeath

23.content: The All-Devouring Eye is the great astral being of annihilation. It does not communicate with the others, gives no blessings, and stands apart from the pacts. Its realm in the deep astral is where Gordon and the apocalypse beasts come from, and the great astral beings believe it created Gordon for the purpose of repairing the Cosmic Throne. Among those interested: it is one of the handful of great astral beings that take an interest in physical realities.
23.name: The All-Devouring Eye

24.content: The Celestial Book is the great astral being of the understanding of magic, venerated by researchers and ritualists. It gives blessings, is friendlier than the Reaper and more cheerful than most of its peers, and in the Book 11 battle it is the one great astral being who enjoys being mortal. It locked essence combinations after the sundering. Veneration: "I venerate the Celestial Book," Clive says, describing a blessing that triggered a racial gift evolution, changing the human special-attack affinity to a spell affinity, like the elves. It is "fairly common for those of us heavily involved in magical theory". Not a god of books: Jason first asks if it is "the god of books, or something". It is named among the great astral beings interested in physical realities. Approachable: its stones are described as "a lot more approachable than the Reaper". A word on proportionality: the World-Phoenix reminds the Builder, "The Celestial Book wanted me to remind you about proportionality... The ritualist is one of his", meaning Clive, and the book will not tolerate a gold-ranker sent to kill the boy out of spite.
24.name: The Celestial Book

25.content: The Keeper of Moments, also called the Keeper of the Sands, is the great astral being that governs time. It opposed the sundering from the beginning and refused to join the pacts, and it polices attempts at time travel. Its prime vessel is Raythe, who in Book 13 bargains with Jason over what he may try to do with time. Domain: "Even the Keeper of Moments, the great astral being that governs time, cannot [affect the past]". Policing time: it "comes down hard" on anyone who comes close to time travel, "in terms of bad ideas, even on a cosmic scale, time travel is the worst". Names: a speaker confesses "a soft spot for the name 'Keeper of the Sands'. I like the hourglass imagery", and Jason says he once heard the master called "the Underclock". Vessel: Lady Raythe is the prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments. She says her master "opposed the sundering from the beginning and refused to participate in any of it", which gives her freedoms others lack. The Keeper stands apart with the All-Devouring Eye and the Word in the Silence. Interventions: Raythe's master took an interest in Jason, and its prime vessel killed Mah Go Schaat to protect him. Velius warns that the Keeper and the All-Devouring Eye waging war in Jason's soul would be bad even if they were on his side. Why the link was left: Clive reasons that the Builder's synchronising of two universes' timelines can't have pleased the Keeper.
25.name: The Keeper of Moments

26.content: Legion is the great astral being that administers the cosmic rules governing life itself. It is one of the beings that joined the pacts after the sundering, then came to think the sundering a mistake. In the Book 11 battle it appears in a mortal body as a deep-voiced man with antlers and a beard. No blessings: Legion and the All-Devouring Eye are not known to hand out blessings. Domain and realm: Legion "administers the cosmic rules that govern life itself", and its realm abuts the All-Devouring Eye's region, a place "where life and annihilation are neighbours". A sanguine horror was summoned from a "nightmare realm where the Limitless Legion met the Final Domain". Position on the sundering: Legion is among those who "have come around and will fight". In a mortal body: "the man with the antlers". It speaks in a "deep, rumbling voice" and objects to vessels that Jason provided: "There are rules". It looks impassive behind its beard. Its view of the plan: it tells Jason that he could have given them far more advantages, and says "We do not get 'used in turn'". Fighting beside him, it says "You are throwing away a chance we have waited eons for". Against the World-Phoenix: it says Jason agreed to help and that "we exploited that to come here", and explains that it is easier to make an immoral choice when you are not doing so alone.
26.name: Legion

27.content: The Seeker of Songs is a great astral being whose domain the books never state. It was against the sundering from the start. It appears in Book 11 in a mortal vessel as a woman with blue eyes, and likes music from Jason's world. Position on the sundering: Raythe says the Celestial Book and the Seeker of Songs "were both against the sundering from the start". Appearance: "the woman with blue eyes" among the great astral beings in mortal bodies. Manner: it identifies a phrase as "a song from Asano's world: 'Rumble in the Jungle' by Fugees, featuring A Tribe Called Quest, Busta Rhymes and John Forté". When the others complain at being used as a training tool it says "this man is hosting the largest gathering of great astral beings since the sundering, and he's using us as a training tool?". Against the World-Phoenix: it calls hijacking Jason's soul while his willpower is diminished "unconscionable", and in the throne room, when the Reaper calls ceremonies pointless, says "I rather like them".
27.name: The Seeker of Songs

28.content: The Builder is the great astral being of construction, whose work is forging universes. There have been two. The first built the twin universes of Earth and Pallimustus and was sanctioned for it. The second, the Builder of the present, is a mortal messenger who was raised to the office and whose authority is held on conditions. He is obsessed with physical reality, runs the cults that hunt astral spaces, and is building a universe of his own. Obsession and method: "obsessed with physical reality while, by its very nature, being unable to co-exist with it", the Builder recruits people to carve off the astral spaces connected to their world, then steps in and claims them. He gathers followers rather than crossing the World-Phoenix. Tools: star seeds, tokens, cults, constructs and clockwork animals. The three-way meeting: the Builder meets the Reaper and the World-Phoenix, grandly says "I will be worshipped by an entire universe... A god beyond gods", and is told that "we are the rules". The Reaper's terms bar him from interfering with Jason's birth world or producing new star seeds, tokens or vessels. In return the World-Phoenix will offer Jason a power at the cost of no further resurrections. Observers: the Builder's observer constructs accompany a group at a test, and Shade reads this as the Builder testing them.
28.name: The Builder

29.content: The Reaper is the great astral being of the finality of death. It is distinct from the god of Death of Pallimustus, who only guides souls into the astral. Cold, dry and a lover of rules, the Reaper is the mediator among the great astral beings, the father of the shadows that serve as familiars, and in Book 11 the reluctant opponent of Jason's plan to restore the throne. Its vessel is Velius. Domain: "The Reaper is very big on the finality of death. Some consider it the true god of death, as all our god of death governs is the passage of the soul into the astral". Items and orders: the Way of the Reaper is a set of skill books, and the Order of the Reaper's teachings are collected in its legacy. The Order of the Reaper used ancient knowledge of how to anchor such realms, "provided by the Reaper itself". Reaper awakening stones give mostly aggressive utility and conjuration powers. Speaking through Velius: when the Reaper takes over its vessel, the warm voice becomes "cold and bleak". It tells the Builder that Jason "carried the World-Phoenix's token. Those pacts are older than you and I will not violate them". The rules: "We are the rules. To deny them is to deny ourselves". It arranges the compromise between the Builder and the World-Phoenix and makes its own concession, because it fears being made a farce if Jason is resurrected over and over. Shade: "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path", the Reaper says, with a brief fatherly smile.
29.name: The Reaper

30.content: The Whisper in Corners is a great astral being Jason had never heard of before meeting Raythe and Velius. It joined the fight against the consequences of the sundering and appears in Book 11 as a veiled woman in lace whose voice comes from every direction. Position on the sundering: it is among those who "have come around and will fight". Appearance: "the woman in lace", laced and veiled, "not a great astral being Jason had heard of" before. Voice: "Her mouth did not move, her voice instead a susurrus of whispers all around them". On forcing souls: it warns the World-Phoenix that there are lines even great astral beings should not cross, and asks "Will you become like the Builder, World-Phoenix? Forcing your way into unwilling souls". It later asks why she would entice others to stand against her.
30.name: The Whisper in Corners

31.content: The Word in the Silence is a great astral being named only once. The text lists it among the beings that "stood apart" from the rest, even before the sundering. Apart from the pacts: Velius says of those who stood aside from the sundering, "They have ever stood apart from the rest, even before the sundering. The Keeper, the All-Devouring Eye, the Word in the Silence".
31.name: The Word in the Silence

32.content: The World-Phoenix is the great astral being of dimensional integrity: it keeps universes from tearing, and it set Jason's journey in motion. It prefers to plant seeds rather than act, has a sense of humour, and fought Jason in his own soul in Book 11. Its prime vessels are called First Servant or First Sister, and Dawn, a former vessel, is its hierophant. The mark on Jason: his first status screens carry a symbol of a fire bird, and an ability labelled "Authority of the World Phoenix". Jason says the World-Phoenix gave him "a gift as his soul passed through the astral", and that he is an outworlder through "happenstance". Its role: "the integrity of dimensions is mine. It is only with my permission that you can conduct your little game". The Builder will not cross it. The meeting of three: the World-Phoenix attends in a celestine vessel with alabaster skin and ruby hair, "a teasing smile and an amused twinkle in her red, gemstone eyes". She calls Jason "a pleasantly effective little seedling", and negotiates with the Reaper over terms that forbid the Builder from interfering with Jason's world.
32.name: The World-Phoenix

33.content: An essence ability is a power an essence user has from an essence. Each essence gives five; one is awakened at absorption and the rest are awakened later by stones. Each ability has a type, a cost, a cooldown and a rank, and gains a new effect at each rank. Four attributes, Power, Speed, Spirit and Recovery, each bond to one of the four essences and rise in rank as that essence's abilities are mastered. Abilities and attributes together decide when a person can move up a rank. Special attack (melee, drain, wounding, blood): Leech Bite. Spell (drain): Blood Harvest. Special ability (dimension, teleport): Path of Shadows. Aura (holy, unholy): Hegemony. Conjuration (darkness, light, dimension): Cloak of Night. Familiar (ritual, summon): Sanguine Horror.
33.name: Abilities and Attributes

34.content: Adventuring is the work of killing monsters and clearing hazards for pay. In practice an adventurer is a licensed contractor: they take posted notices and contracts from a jobs hall, work in a team, and are paid in spirit coins and loot. Most are not heroes in the story sense, and the profession is as much about judgement and bookkeeping as combat. This file describes how the work runs. The organisation is described in 05_Organisations/Adventure_Society.md.
34.name: The Adventuring Profession

35.content: An affliction is a condition that harms its target for a time; a boon is a condition that helps. Both are named in brackets in System messages, carry tags (poison, disease, curse, holy, unholy, magic and others) and can stack. Defence against afflictions is a game of resisting, cleansing and negating: a cleanse removes an affliction, resistance reduces the chance or strength of one landing, and some afflictions are built to defeat both. In this world a character who understands which tool beats which condition has a large tactical advantage, and Jason's power set is built around that interplay.
35.name: Afflictions, Boons and Damage

36.content: Alongside essences and stones the world has a layer of working magic that does not need an essence: quintessence gems, spirit coins, potions, ointments, enchanted tools and growth items that rise in rank. This file describes what these materials are and how they are used. It does not list individual named items; those are in 09_Items_and_Artefacts/.
36.name: Alchemy, Artifice and Magical Materials

key: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
37.comment: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
37.content: Three kinds of event reshape territory in the series. Astral spaces are pocket worlds attached to a physical world through apertures. Proto-astral spaces are short-lived, unstable versions of them that Earth suffers from. Transformation zones are sealed events that rewrite a place and the people in it. Monster surges are periodic increases in monster numbers across a world. All four are driven by the same source: raw magic leaking through from the astral.
keys: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
37.name: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges

38.content: An aura is the projection of a ranked person's soul. It grows with rank, is read by other ranked people as a sense of danger, strength and mood, and is how adventurers judge each other before words are spoken. Controlling the aura is a skill with three basic parts: projecting it, restraining it and suppressing other people's. Auras can be hidden, masked, aimed at normal people to intimidate them, and, at silver rank, begin to lift the body off the ground.
38.name: Auras

39.content: An awakening stone is a consumable crystal that awakens one essence ability the user has not yet awakened. It is the third kind of non-living magic Rufus lists, after essences and quintessence. The stone does not choose the ability; it steers toward a theme, and what comes out depends mostly on the essences the user holds. Stones are how a new essence user fills out the twenty abilities that a full set carries, and they are bought, auctioned, given as rewards and kept as family wealth.
39.name: Awakening Stones

40.content: A confluence is the fourth essence a person receives. It is not picked, bought or found. It is produced by the three essences already absorbed, and it arrives the moment the third is used. In the main run of the series a given trio of essences always gives the same confluence, and the Magic Society keeps a list of the known trios. Confluences are rated and talked about as if they were essences in their own right, and many of the best-known power sets belong to a confluence.
40.name: Confluences

41.content: Earth has the same magic as Pallimustus in a much thinner form. Through most of its history essences and monsters did not exist there at all; magic leaked in through short-lived proto-astral spaces, and a small number of secret societies used the powers that people could earn from them. When Jason returns in Book 4, Earth's magic is low and rising, with a planetary Grid of rituals monitoring and containing the leaks. The monster waves of Book 5 and the transformation zones that follow end that system. By Book 11 the rules have changed.
41.name: Magic on Earth

42.content: The books name far more essences than the wiki lists give with evidence. This file collects those the text actually shows, with who holds them and what the text says of their behaviour. Rarity statements come from the text; where the text gives none, none is invented. It is intended as a quick reference for building a character's power set, not as a mechanical list. The full set of essences the Magic Society knows is in its living document. The wiki's fuller lists of essences, confluences and combinations are in../Appendices/Wiki_Reference_Lists.md, with a cross-reference to the first book line for each entry found in the text. Where the wiki gives a rarity, it agrees with the text so far: sin is Legendary, renewal is Epic and rune and vast are among the highest.
42.name: Essence Catalogue

43.content: An essence is the most powerful and rarest of the forms in which magic condenses into something that is not alive. It is absorbed into a person's soul and gives that person a set of five abilities tied to its concept. Four essences make a full set. A person with a full set becomes iron rank and is changed by it. Essences are how Pallimustus makes essence users: the people who fight monsters, serve in the churches and run most of the world's institutions.
43.name: Essences

44.content: A familiar is a creature made or called to serve one person for life. A summoned familiar is built by ritual from magical materials and a being drawn from the deep astral; a bonded familiar is a creature that answers a call. Familiars are different from the short-lived summons many essence users can conjure in the middle of a fight, and from conjurations, which are things drawn out of mana. All three are essence abilities and come from awakening stones or from the essences themselves; none can be used by anyone who lacks the necessary ritual knowledge.
44.name: Familiars, Summons and Conjurations

45.content: The appendices of Book 12 are the only complete statement of one character's essence abilities across all ranks. They are used here as a worked example of how abilities are built: each ability gains one new effect at each rank, and many effects add an affliction or a boon that other abilities then use. The author notes that the list "is written for brevity (believe it or not) rather than accuracy or comprehensiveness". This file records the facts and adds no numbers.
45.name: Jason's Power Set at Gold

46.content: An essence user can grow in power in two ways. One is to consume monster cores, which is easy and can be bought. The other is to train, fight real danger and meditate. Rufus's teaching in Book 1 is that the first method eats into the potential of the second. The setting's politics, from the aristocratic families of Greenstone to the Network on Earth, turn on which method a group has used, and on what it costs them later.
46.name: Monster Cores and Training

47.content: Monsters are the most common way magic manifests in a magic-rich world. They appear from nothing, usually in the wild, live for a time that depends on their rank, and then dissolve back into raw magic if not killed first. They have ranks like essence users; the ranks are not given by essences but by the density of the magic that makes them. Hunting them before they reach their aggressive final stage is the bulk of an adventurer's work, and what they leave behind funds much of the economy.
47.name: Monsters

key: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
48.comment: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
48.content: This file records, for Jason and a few teammates, the first chapter where each rank, essence and ability appears. Jason's lines come from the system messages that announce them. For Jason's full gold-rank power set, see Jason_Power_Set_Reference.md. "First shown" means the first line the compendium found, which may come a chapter after an unreported awakening.
keys: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained
48.name: Progression Tracks: When Rank, Essence and Ability Were Gained

49.content: Rank is the world's measure of power. It runs from normal people through iron, bronze, silver, gold and diamond; beyond diamond are gods and great astral beings, who are not part of the ladder. Essence users and monsters share the ladder, and each rank "has a suppressive effect on lower ranks". Rank changes the body, the length of life, what a person can do with their aura and the way other people treat them. It is the setting's class system.
49.name: Ranks and Advancement

50.content: Ritual magic is the practice of drawing a diagram, a circle with lines and glyphs, and powering it with external magic to do something an essence ability cannot. It is used for absorbing essences, awakening stones, summoning familiars, spreading wards and tracking, and, in permanent form, as formations and arrays. Ritual magic is learned, not given by an essence, and a competent ritualist is a valuable member of any team. Anyone can learn external magic; only essence users can combine it with essence powers.
50.name: Rituals, Arrays and Formations

51.content: A skill book is a consumable magical book that implants knowledge directly into the reader. It can teach a language, a martial art, the basics of ritual magic or a branch of astral magic. A skill book gives technique and information, not understanding or practice, and the people who use them well prepare beforehand and consolidate afterwards. They are the fast, flawed route to ability in a skill, in the same way that cores are the fast, flawed route to rank.
51.name: Skill Books and Learning

52.content: A soul is the part of a person that essences and ranks change. It shapes the body, projects the aura, leaves marks when wounded and, on death, lingers briefly before drifting into the astral. Healing magic can reverse a death only in that grace period and only with powerful magic. Everyday healing is done by the Healer's church, by alchemists and by healing abilities, and it is in short supply compared to demand.
52.name: Souls, Death and Healing

53.content: A title is how the System writes down a change to the soul: it appears as a window after a soul has been scarred or tested and usually changes the owner's aura. A blessing is a gift from a god or great astral being that evolves a racial gift. Titles come from what happens to a person, blessings from what a transcendent being chooses to give. The two meet in Jason's story because the same events scar his soul and attract the blessings of the World-Phoenix and the Reaper.
53.name: Titles and Blessings

54.content: Most magic in the setting follows the essence-and-rank structure described elsewhere in this folder. A smaller body of magic does not: the gifts a person is born with or earns as a race, the outworlder abilities that give Jason a game-like interface, titles drawn from soul damage, time magic, and the powers of great astral beings and gods. This file collects them so a storyteller knows what exists and who has what. It does not attempt to explain the cosmology; see 02_Cosmology_and_Powers/. Interface: the screens and System messages; "interpret reality through a recognisable medium". Quest System: quests with rewards, including a "racial gift transfiguration". Inventory: a grid of forty slots with a currency counter; items are plucked from and pushed into the screen. Astral Affinity: "Increased resistance to dimension effects and astral forces. Dimension abilities have increased effect and transcendent damage is increased". Mysterious Stranger: "Language adaptation. Essence, awakening stone and skill-book absorption. Immunity to identification and tracking effects".
54.name: Unusual and Unique Magic

55.content: Belinda is the team's trickster and utility caster: Magic, Trap and Adept, producing the Charlatan confluence. Her set borrows other people's powers, shapes herself into other roles, sets traps and teleports allies. She is delighted by her own power: "I was looking through the abilities it's known to give and they sound fantastic".
55.name: Belinda Callahan's Power Set

56.content: Clive is the team's battlemage and ritualist: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. His set is built on one big spell, retributive karma effects that punish attackers, ritual circles and mana support. Spells are his focus; he uses magical weapons like staves and wands and works with his familiar.
56.name: Clive Standish's Power Set

57.content: Emi is a ritual specialist: a teenager who masters ritual magic before she has essences, then takes Vast, Myriad and Harmonic, whose Resonant confluence feeds a set of stacked ritual-circle shields and mana recycling. She is Jason's niece.
57.name: Emi Evans-Asano's Power Set

58.content: Farrah is a volcano-themed battlemage and ritualist: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence. She fights in glossy obsidian armour with a sword that becomes a lava whip, burning orbs and lava spells, and her ritual magic underlies the team's summons and later the Grid repairs. Obsidian armour: heavy obsidian armour that glows with internal heat; a full set of glossy obsidian shards swept into wing shapes with a red glow between the segments. Sword: a huge obsidian sword whose blade is "a pillar of jagged segments" that can break up and whip around on a cord of glowing magma. Unextended it is a jagged-edge greatsword; as a whip-sword the teeth are strung on a flexible cord of red-hot lava. Lava cannon: a showstopping power that "devoured mana like pigs with a fresh corpse"; she uses it to devastate a team of silver-rankers. Orbs: three flaming orbs manifest over her head and shoot fiery beams; at the Network fight they are "searing flame" orbs. Magma and obsidian terrain: a glowing sigil on the ground produces a magma geyser, a curtain of obsidian shards from a stomp, an obsidian wall that explodes into shards, and a spike that impales. Finisher: she turns the obsidian fragments left in an enemy into lava. Magma elemental summon: a pile of black and red magma with arms, summoned from a ritual circle like Gary's golem. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and teaches Emi, Hiro and others magical theory.
58.name: Farrah Hurin's Power Set

59.content: Gary is a leonid smith-warrior: hammer, fire, iron and the forge confluence. His set is a conjured suit of armour, a heavy hammer and shield, a forge golem he summons from iron filings, and forge powers for repair and alloys. The Book 10 change replaces the set with divine essences and a demigod confluence. Armour and weapons: conjured full-body armour of dark steel plates held together with large bolts, engraved with runes; he fights with a huge hammer and a shield. He forges a hammer himself to fight constructs. Forge golem: he pours iron filings into a circle, his hand bursts into flame, and a three-metre golem of ugly black iron rises with molten metal between the joints. The text calls it a foundry golem when he names it and a forge golem later. It is a temporary summon, unlike a familiar. Summoning powers need ritual understanding, as for Farrah. Forge powers: he uses a forge essence power to repair a wagon wheel, and creates "alloys heavier and stronger than steel" for the academy annex. Smithing: he forges Jason's Dread Salvation. Rescue work: in the Book 9 surge he and other craftspeople shape stone and reinforce structures, and his golem's chest plate opens to carry survivors.
59.name: Gary's Power Set

60.content: Humphrey is the team's heavy hitter: "simple, reliable power". His dragon, wing and might essences give him a dragon-winged flyer with fire, a weapon-heavy attack set and racial gifts that scale with risk. His familiar is the mirage dragon Stash.
60.name: Humphrey Geller's Power Set

61.content: Neil is the team's healer and shield-caster: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence. His set is built around timed, short-lived shields, buffs on allies and ritual healing, and Prosperity luck effects. Rufus is struck by the shielding: the shields "lasted only moments and would end after absorbing only a single attack", so they need good judgement and timing.
61.name: Neil Davone's Power Set

62.content: Rufus is a swordsman-teleporter built on the sun and moon: a skilled fighter whose powers blend movement, teleportation, illusory after-images and attacks. In the Greenstone years he fights as a bronze-ranker with a golden and a silver sword; by Book 9 his essence is described as the eclipse confluence, and his combat shifts between sun, moon and eclipse states. Conjured swords: a golden sword and a silver sword that appear in his hand. The swords leave marks: those cut by the golden sword have a small orb of fire, "a miniature golden sun", floating around them and scorching them; those touched by the silver sword have a tiny moon that soaks up heat instead. Speed of light: when he activates it "the world seemed to freeze in time around him", giving "only two seconds of accelerated time"; the text calls it "one of his strongest trump cards". Movement chain: unlike Jason, he does not have one teleport he can use over and over; "he had a slew of powers that blended movement, teleportation, illusionary after-images and attacks" and chaining them takes skill and practice. Water-walking boots are noted in his character file. Kingdom of Eclipse: his incantation-driven power, whose chant ends "bring forth the kingdom of eclipse"; it fires an eclipse orb that kills dozens.
62.name: Rufus Remore's Power Set

63.content: Sophie is a skill-based speed fighter: a celestine whose Swift, Balance and Wind essences form the Mystic confluence. Her set stacks movement, perception and unarmed techniques around one idea, acting faster and more precisely than the enemy. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years.
63.name: Sophie Wexler's Power Set

64.content: Taika is a bird-shifter and flyer: a garuda-confluence adventurer whose set is built on speed, momentum and a giant-bird form. By Book 9 his power set is in line with Humphrey's, sharing the might and wing essences, where Humphrey's confluence is dragon and Taika's is garuda. Taika's first plan for the garuda confluence began with a bird essence.
64.name: Taika's Power Set

key: Boko: Culture of a City of Scholars and Artists
65.comment: Boko: Culture of a City of Scholars and Artists
65.content: Boko is an old desert city north of Greenstone with a native population, known for its scholars and artists. The Adventure Society has a branch there, but it is not a strong adventuring city. Its fate in Book 12 is in Boko.md. Older than Greenstone: "A lot older than Greenstone, with a population native to the area". The arts: "Scholars of the arts. Painting, poetry, sculpture, dance", with people travelling from across the continent to see its theatres. It has beautiful architecture and gardens and universities. Look and dress: desert stone like Old City with drier air; the people are almost entirely human and very dark-skinned, with loose, breathable fashion calmer than the Ustei's. Not a port: a coastal city that was never a port like Greenstone, with no natural harbour. Adventuring: the Adventure Society has a branch but Boko "was not a strong adventuring city". Boko has a mirage chamber that Clive helped rebuild. Return of the Ustei: the Society returns Ustei captives to Boko. Politics: its Duke is a silver-ranker through cores, as is normal for political leaders, and noble houses exist. A movement against intellectuals among low-rankers began in Boko. Temples: floating temples shielded by their gods survive the city's destruction.
keys: Boko: Culture of a City of Scholars and Artists
65.name: Boko: Culture of a City of Scholars and Artists

key: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
66.comment: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
66.content: The Pallimustus calendar is close to Earth's but not the same: twelve months of thirty days, five extra days and a six-day week with simple day names. Naming customs and forms of address mark rank, family and role, and Rimaros has a distinctive palindrome custom for prominent adults.
keys: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address
66.name: Calendar, Holidays, Naming Customs and Forms of Address

67.content: Metallic-haired, metallic-eyed people with an astral affinity, produced when two outworlders have a child. Appearance: Sophie has chocolate skin and shining silver hair, her eyes matching it exactly, "the matching metallics a giveaway trait of the celestine race". In Kurdansk many celestines have dark skin and silver hair. Astral affinity: astral affinity is a celestine racial gift; celestines are similar to elves and humans. The rare Child of the Celestial Wind appears only in races with astral affinity, on Pallimustus meaning celestines, or potentially outworlders. Origin: Dawn says two outworlders who have a child produce a celestine, and celestines propagate with their own kind; she is herself a child of two outworlders. Gift evolutions: Sophie's Mana Integrity becomes Mana Wellspring, her Astral Affinity becomes Boundary Breaker and her Celestial Swiftness becomes Princess of the Firmament. Communities: Zartos is a subterranean city largely populated by celestines. Messengers: messengers are about half again as tall as a celestine, and their servants take care never to imply the resemblance. Dawn's true form: a celestine with ruby eyes and hair.
67.name: Celestines

key: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
68.comment: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
68.content: A regional table of how people dress, eat, celebrate and travel. Daily_Life.md covers Greenstone and the delta in detail; this file adds Rimaros and the Storm Kingdom, Yaresh, Kurdansk, Pranay, Vitesse and smaller places, and gathers the festivals the text names.
keys: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region
68.name: Clothing, Food, Festivals and Transport by Region

key: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
69.comment: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
69.content: The practical texture of life in Greenstone and the delta: the calendar, what people wear and eat, how they travel and what runs on spirit coins. Calendar: "twelve months of thirty days, divided up into early, mid and late stages of each season", five extra days for the solstices, equinoxes and the new year, which falls at the beginning of spring. The week has six days. Clothing: "Most people, whether in Greenstone or the delta, wore loose-fitting, breathable clothes because of the heat"; adventurers on a job wear fitted outfits, often with protective properties. Elf fashion has flowing, tapered lines. Food: preparation is often familiar, with bread, soup, sandwiches and cake, but the ingredients are mostly different because farms raise different animals and trees bear different fruit. Jason lists local sauce ingredients with a village cook. Housing: Leust, one of the delta's largest towns, has paved roads and stone buildings "instead of mud-brick"; in the Island, green stone appears everywhere. Transport: heidels are "the size and shape of a horse, but with scales instead of hair and two heads, each with a horn"; the Island's districts are linked by a subterranean, submarine transit line called the loop, with terminals laid out like train stations. Devices: lamps, showers and most household magic run on lesser spirit coins. Communication: the Magic Society's water link projects a lifelike image of a speaker; by Book 12 Travis Noble's sky link service carries calls.
keys: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
69.name: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport

70.content: Large, scaled humanoids who claim descent from dragons and whose homeland is the Dragon Lands. Appearance: "a member of the rare draconian race, larger even than male leonids and covered in glossy scales", the colour of dark leaves, green moving into purple; Maximilian is the tallest person in Greenstone, with a long hairless head and glossy scales. A draconian skull is distinctive enough to identify skeletons. Pride in descent: draconians "took pride in their claimed dragon ancestry and often had issues with other races wielding the dragon essence". Homeland: the Dragon Lands, Pallimustus's version of Antarctica, "the native land of the large, scaled humanoids known as draconians", with active volcanoes, hot springs and "dragon mouth" geysers from subterranean apertures to a realm of fire. Rarity: draconians are rare in Greenstone, where Maximilian is the only one present at a gathering.
70.name: Draconians

key: The Dragon Lands: Culture of the Draconian Homeland
71.comment: The Dragon Lands: Culture of the Draconian Homeland
71.content: The Dragon Lands are the volcanic island continent that is the native land of the draconians, a largely isolationist people who export agricultural produce through proxies. The text shows them only from the air in Book 12. The people: large, scaled humanoids who "took pride in their claimed dragon ancestry" and have issues with other races wielding the dragon essence. They are rare outside their land. Closed society: they "aren't very welcoming to strangers" and use proxies outside their lands. Farming and trade: the land is famously rich farmland and the best place for gold-rank cooking ingredients, because the leaking magic has earth as well as fire affinity. Agricultural products from the Dragon Lands are the second-largest trade through Greenstone's port, after low-rank spirit coins. Most nations tariff the goods heavily over political issues, making them a luxury food. The land: dark stone mountains rising from green lowlands of forest and farmland laid out like a map, with a climate like Scotland or Ireland, volcanoes, hot springs and flame geysers called dragon mouths.
keys: The Dragon Lands: Culture of the Draconian Homeland
71.name: The Dragon Lands: Culture of the Draconian Homeland

72.content: Dreisil is the nation of Kurdansk, Sophie's birthplace. The text names it once and gives its full title. Kurdansk_Culture.md covers the life of the city and is the main file for what is known of the nation's people. Name: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil". Humphrey's view: "The more they try to make a nation sound free and righteous, the more tyrannical and corrupt it is". Prisons: Kurdansk uses prisons rather than indenture as punishment.
72.name: Dreisil: The People's Holy Federation

73.content: How money works on Pallimustus: spirit coins in six denominations that also power devices and sustain essence users, farms that make them, and who controls them. Denominations: "The basic coin of the realm was the lesser spirit coin. Iron spirit coins were worth a hundred lesser coins, used by bulk traders, adventurers and other members of the wealthy elite. After that, it was ten iron to the bronze, ten bronze to the silver and ten silver to the gold"; three gold coins are "worth three hundred thousand units of the basic currency". Why the lesser coin is the basic unit: higher-rank coins are "not very useful for everyday life"; almost all home and business magic devices, such as lamps and showers, run on lesser coins and higher ranks would burn them out, while larger infrastructure such as the loop line uses more powerful coins. Sustenance: ranked people can live on spirit coins; Rufus says a bronze coin will sustain bronze-rank adventurers without stressing their bodies, so it is about not going over your limit. Farms: spirit coins are made on farms using special moulds that cause magic to crystallise, in delicate, very stable ambient magic.
73.name: Economy and Money

key: Education: Academies, Training Programmes and Universities
74.comment: Education: Academies, Training Programmes and Universities
74.content: How people are taught: family academies for adventurers (Remore, Geller), Magic Society research wings, universities (Kazlahk's medical school) and, on Earth, the Asano Academy. The text shows education mostly through what it produces: skilled adventurers, researchers and healers.
keys: Education: Academies, Training Programmes and Universities
74.name: Education: Academies, Training Programmes and Universities

75.content: Elves are powerful spellcasters whose healing magic is unparalleled. Reputation: "Elves are powerful spell casters and their skill with healing magic is unparalleled". Aptitude: the elven aptitude is for spells rather than the special attacks humans favour. Racial gift: Neil's elf racial ability, Life Affinity, evolves into Life Guard. Local families: Greenstone has local elf families; Lucian Lamprey is an elf banished there who is not one of them, and Pochard Finn is an elf and a local. Elf fashion: "flowing, tapered lines". Notable elves: Allayeth and Charist, Yaresh's two diamond-rank elves; Hana Shavar, High Priestess of the Healer; Elspeth Arella, director of the Greenstone Adventure Society. Predation: cannibals in Book 1 discuss elves as food.
75.name: Elves

key: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
76.comment: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
76.content: A large, densely populated kingdom of old noble houses, garden towers and high-magic farmland, and the homeland from which Greenstone was colonised. Standing: "One of the most prominent kingdoms in the world" with a royal family; the Queen of Estercost and other members of its elite ask Jason to arbitrate over the System's withdrawal. Population: a "large and densely populated kingdom" and the land from which Greenstone was colonised centuries earlier; the region is "filled with towns, villages and smaller cities, due to the idyllic climate and rich natural resources". Capital and councils: Cyrion is the capital, yet the Adventure Society's continental council sits in Vitesse, where the royal family keeps a tower as a palace; in Book 7 the Cyrion branch takes over the site of the operation from Vitesse. Vitesse: the city of flowers, on what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that house the wealthy elite and key organisations. Adventurers think of it as the continent's adventuring capital, because its high magic spawns powerful, frequent monster manifestations. Aristocracy: the Remore family has no title, while the Gellers hold only the title from their small provincial city of origin and refuse all others; neither is begrudged a premier tower. Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". House Headingway is "one of Estercost's pre-eminent families".
keys: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
76.name: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats

key: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
77.comment: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
77.content: Girlano is an inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom, ostensibly a kingdom but controlled by cartels that produce banned or heavily controlled substances. It has a reputation, and the text shows it only through reputation and a border city. Rule: "ostensibly a kingdom", it is "famously controlled by cartels known for producing substances that ranged from heavily controlled to outright banned"; the cartels keep power through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up a puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression. Economy: the cartels exploit the region's rare plants and minerals, and the nation is surrounded by strong public sanctions and border controls. Smuggling culture: the border with the Storm Kingdom is jungle-covered hills with many semi-hidden smuggling paths to the shore. The border city Casallini is a small city where the Adventure Society keeps a large force because it is a border city. Neutral Society: the Adventure Society ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with. Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers". Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" with "all the opportunities it offered to an enterprising and open-minded young lady". Hired muscle: the men who attack Sophie's delivery are local hires from Casallini.
keys: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom
77.name: Girlano: Culture of a Cartel Kingdom

78.content: Goblins and fairies appear as monsters and as people of Earth transformed by the zones; fairies are also a small hovering manifestation. Goblins as monsters: Jason jokes about killing ten goblins for an uncommon spear in the cannibals' cave. Transformed humans: in West Canfield, Detroit, people were "turned into goblins and their homes into underground warrens", which became a lawless combat zone. Cabal beings: the Cabal's mythological beings include centaurs, ogres, fairies and more. Elves, goblins and fairies: people in a magic city were "turned into elves and goblins and fairies". Fairy manifestation: a small hovering fairy-like figure with an androgynous body bites Clive in Book 2. Earth beings in the open: as the Cabal operated in the open, "centaurs, ogres, fairies, and more" were spotted by the media and revealed to the world. A Network operative expects the Cabal to be "myths and fairy tale creatures". Zone-turned people: Emi says people in a magic city "were all turned into elves and goblins and fairies", so they were let live there. Jason's cloud city is described as a fairy tale kingdom, but that is a style, not a people.
78.name: Goblins and Fairies: Zone-Transformed Peoples

79.content: The most common people of Pallimustus and Earth's native people, with gifts that favour special attacks and fast essence advancement. Racial gifts: an affinity for special attacks, essences that advance more rapidly than others', and latent powers that adapt to the essences. The latent gifts are dormant until awakened and then take a form based on the person's essences. Evolution: Clive's blessing from the Celestial Book changes his human special attack affinity into a spell affinity; his Human Ambition becomes Thirst for Knowledge and Humphrey's Special Attack Affinity becomes Attack of the Mirage Dragon. Taika's human abilities have been replaced with outworlder ones. Distribution: the Greenstone region is human-dominated. Humans and outworlders: an outworlder who has a child with another species produces offspring of that species, so a human and an outworlder have a human child. Lifespan: essence users age slower; bronze-rankers can live well past a hundred, silvers double that and gold-rankers live for centuries.
79.name: Humans

key: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
80.comment: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
80.content: Jayapura is a northern-coast sea-trade port of Pranay and the birthplace of Hester. Pranay_Culture.md covers the land; this file gives Jayapura's own life: the mirage arenas as entertainment, floating discs, markets and the Mystic Quarter. Trade port: one of the important sea-trade ports on Pranay's northern coast. Arena culture: its mirage chamber complex is the city's premier entertainment venue, with essence users facing each other or illusion challenges before a paying audience. "There are whole essence user teams who never become adventurers"; they earn money in the arena and use monster cores to rank. Two leagues a year in silver, bronze and iron divisions lead to grand championships. See Mirage_Chamber_Association.md. Retirement: arena professionals stop using cores before gold, retire when silver longevity runs out and become gold-rank managers of the arena. Layout: a flat circular arena building at the edge of the Mystic Quarter, spilling into the theatre district. Transport: those who can afford them ride platter-sized floating discs; floating discs are sold in the Mystic Quarter. Markets and food: the team visits its markets and finds new customs and food. A nondescript tattoo parlour run by Tilly is where Jason gets his crest. Ice cream: Jason remembers kulfi-like ice cream from there.
keys: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port
80.name: Jayapura: Culture of a Pranay Trade Port

key: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
81.comment: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
81.content: A river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil, where celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common, entertainment and crime share the old docks, and prisons rather than indenture punish crime. Nation: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil". Celestines: "Like many of Kurdansk's celestines, she had dark skin and silver hair", and the rowhouses are narrow and wedged together. Entertainment quarter: a former warehouse district near the Kurdan River docks, now the most viable site for large theatre halls, "a heady mix of pleasure, criminality and money". Skyport: it has a busy skyport with towers where airships dock. Law: Kurdansk locks criminals up for years in prisons, which a Book 12 speaker calls costly to run. The Reaper link: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk around twenty-five years before Book 9.
keys: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
81.name: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil

82.content: Greenstone and Estercost have no slaves, only indentured servants, and indenture is both a sentence and a business; in Book 12 the question of indenture drives the System's withdrawal. Indenture, not slavery: "We don't have slaves. We have indentured servants. A lot of criminals are sentenced to indenture, then their indenture is sold or auctioned to recoup the cost of their crimes". Jason finds the system disturbing and says both his world and this one need better systems. Captured enemies: the Ustei do not accept slavery; "their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". The Adventure Society agreement: a clause in the Adventure Society's agreement with Greenstone gives anyone who completes a contract the right of refusal on anyone sentenced to indenture as a result of it. Hearings: indenture hearings are a normal legal event; the Greenstone court "was less like an American legal p[roceeding]". House guards: in Cyrion, house guards are "technically a form of indentured servitude" and the laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". Jason's argument: if a family used "draconian measures" to hold people to cheap work, nothing would stop them.
82.name: Law and Indenture

83.content: The Lehenik are a people that exist only as a name and a promise: Jason's word for the people he intends to make from his own soul realm, of whom Nik is the first. Nik is the only one in the text. The name: Jason names Nik from the word "Lehenik", "in a language from the world where I was born, it roughly translates first or firstly. The first instance", and says that is what he wants to call Nik's people "once you're a species and not a unique being: Lehenik. The first people to belong in this place". Belonging: he explains that everything else in his soul realm "either doesn't belong or is an extension of me. Except for you. You came from me, but you belong to no one but yourself". A promise: Nik asks "You're going to make more like me?" and Jason answers "Yes. I believe I know how". Not yet a species: in Book 12 Jason says he cannot "make more of your kind, turn you into a species proper, until I reach the fullness of my power". He jokes about making a female lehenik and Nik rejects the idea. Others like them: Raythe tells Jason that astral kings cannot ordinarily use planets in their astral realms to birth messengers, "but you are not the first original to do so. Or to birth more than messengers. There are others like your lehenik to be found amongst the countless worlds".
83.name: The Lehenik

84.content: Lion-headed, furred, strong and fast people; Gary is the best-known leonid. Strength and stamina: "Members of his leonid race are stronger and faster than us, and that's only the beginning of what leonids can do"; a leonid needs far more exertion than others to tire, another racial gift. Appearance: a huge "lion man" whose voice is growly by default; Gary is "so huge he made bodybuilders look like they w[ere small]". He is covered in fur. Size: draconians are larger even than male leonids. Mixed company: a leonid, an elf and a celestine are among the eleven people who emerge from Dawn's cottage in Book 7. Notable leonids: Gary Xandier, a Vitesse adventurer, and Gary Sharpton in Book 12, who designs the flying vehicle the group travels in and has spent most of his life in an astral space.
84.name: Leonids

85.content: Merfolk are named once in the books as people, not fish; no detail beyond that is established here. Only reference: Emir answers a joke about someone's partner ("Man, woman or fish?") with "Merfolk are not fish. They happen to be very sensual people".
