Open gap: no chapter text found so far gives merfolk appearance, homeland or gifts. A joke, not a sighting: in Book 12 Travis asks "Is that some kind of merman?" of a passer-by with webbed hands and feet, and Jason answers that he is the actor Patrick Duffy. The line is an Earth joke, not a merfolk sighting. Searched: a scan of the chapter files for merfolk, mermaid, merman and merrow finds no other mention.
85.name: Merfolk

86.content: Messengers are the gestalt people who serve astral kings: long-lived, patient and hierarchical, with a master-and-servant social order. This file collects what they are as a society; their powers and their place in the cosmos are in Astral_Kings_and_Messengers.md. Origin: messengers are "budded, not born", and Jason says they are "actually plants, which is kind of crazy". They are gestalt beings whose body and soul are one. Appearance: a messenger in Book 9 "looked like a celestine with alabaster skin and long hair of spun gold", with solid gold eyes, standing some eight feet high with a pair of wings. A messenger's alabaster skin dulls when drained of mana. Hierarchy: masters hold servant races, and a master "was free to treat the servant races however he pleased, so long as it did not impinge upon the interests of other messengers". Fal Vin Garath, a silver-rank messenger, is Benella's abusive master. Names: the messenger names in the text are three-part names with a middle particle: Fal Vin Garath, Jes Fin Kaal, Vesta Carmis Zell, Jamis Fran Muskar, Erigo Fin Desca, Cas Vin Baral and Relia Vin Vala. Boris Ket Lundi is also named in this pattern. The text gives no meaning for the middle particles; this note records the pattern only. Belief: Dawn tells Jason that astral kings rule through messengers, whose message is "Kneel" (see Astral_Kings_and_Messengers.md. Hess confesses to feeling the instinct to kneel.
86.name: The Messengers as a People

key: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
87.comment: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
87.content: The Mirror Kingdom, also called the Kingdom of Mirrors, is a small, affluent kingdom founded and ruled for more than eight centuries by a diamond-ranker, the Mirror King. Its princes and princesses are many, and its prince Valdis leads an adventuring team in Greenstone. Nature: "the diminutive but influential Kingdom of Mirrors. Small, affluent and geographically blessed, it had neither expanded its borders nor been had its borders encroached upon in more than eight centuries". The king: the diamond-ranker known as the Mirror King founded the kingdom and rules it still; he has had "a series of queens, reportedly doting on each, even as they grew old and died beside him", and Valdis is one of the current queen consort's sons. Court manners: kneeling is expected before the king; his protocol officer Hastor tells Jason "You should kneel", and the king says Hastor "starts getting snippy" without a seating chart by rank. Valdis's team drops to one knee on the king's arrival. The king is amused, warm and teasing with his son. Teams built around princes: Valdis's team was built around him, "the shaft to his spearhead". The kingdom has its own battles with the Builder cult. The king's aura: Jason, an iron-ranker, finds the king's aura felt like part of the world, "in perfect symbiosis with the world", and it later inspires his own aura control. Portals: the king has his own portal specialist, Hastor, who calls up a glass-like portal.
keys: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker
87.name: The Mirror Kingdom: Culture of a Kingdom Ruled by a Diamond-Ranker

88.content: People whose souls re-entered a physical reality, manifesting a new body; they carry unusual gifts and cannot be easily tracked. Definition: Clive: "An outworlder is someone whose soul has re-entered a physical reality, reflexively manifesting a body for itself"; the body is "akin to that of a monster, or a summoned familiar", physical substance forged from raw magic, between the astral and the physical. How it happens: natural magical phenomena connecting two realities drag someone through; their body is annihilated in the astral and their soul reconstitutes one. Advantages: Farrah says outworlders "might have their advantages", and Jason's abilities (map, interface, astral affinity) are outworlder abilities. Children: an outworlder with another species produces offspring of that species; two outworlders produce a celestine. Arrivals: a hundred and nineteen outworlders arrive at once in Book 7; two outworlders among the eleven people in Dawn's cottage are bronze rank. Jason: his character screen lists him as a formerly human outworlder until Book 12.
88.name: Outworlders

key: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
89.comment: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
89.content: The large southern land corresponding to Sri Lanka, where portal stopovers and isolated city-states form a trading hub, and where Jayapura is the port Hester calls home. Geography: Pranay is this world's equivalent of Sri Lanka, "larger and further south", a huge landmass in the Indian Ocean. Its northern coast has several important sea-trade connections in a world without the Arabian Peninsula. Jayapura: Hester's birth city; personal transport for those who can afford it is a platter-sized floating disc ridden by shifting weight. Mirage chambers: Jayapura has a vast mirage chamber complex, more sophisticated than the Gellers' private chamber in Greenstone because the higher magic allows potent dimensional magic and concurrent chambers. Massive city: Jason's team visited Pranay's urban centre after their first Reaper astral space and saw only familiars as magical beasts. Portal stopover: in Book 11 it is a portal stopover on the way to Estercost, "the last of the isolated city-states they would visit for a while".
keys: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
89.name: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States

90.content: How faith appears day to day: crowded temple districts with hierarchies of their own, churches that serve as hospitals and archives, and gods whose rules limit what they can do. Temple districts: temples line the road to the Island's Divine Square and "gods had hierarchies of their own": the Temple of Roads sits behind the larger Temple of Journeys. The square is crowded with booths selling religious paraphernalia and people proselytising. Dominion: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves". The Healer: Neil makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer; ex-clergy who offended their gods and were stripped of divinely gifted essences suffer a debilitating imbalance in body and soul; the notes make the Healer the god who does this. Knowledge's temple: in Rimaros it is "an important resource for the many magical researchers" with a symbiotic relationship with the Magic Society branch; the temple is mostly a vast library covering multiple wings. Churches and research: churches, especially Knowledge's, help fund the Magical Research Association. Death's paperwork: the Church of Death issues certification of how many times a person has died. Limits on gods: a god's favour does not mean intervention; a goddess says she cannot see into the astral space where Jason holds prisoners; the gods are "bound by convoluted limitations".
90.name: Religion in Practice

91.content: Short, stocky, hairless people with deep-blue skin and naturally glowing runes. Appearance: "short and stocky, with skin of such a deep blue it was almost black", no hair and covered in faintly glowing, tattoo-like markings that are natural to the race. Rarity: they are "a rarity in Greenstone"; a runic barman in Old City is stocky and hairless with blue-black skin and glowing runes. Bones: the runes show faintly on their bones; a short, broad skeleton in the desert astral space is identified as a runic by them. Notable: Arash, a runic Jason meets in the temple district, explains Dominion's role: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles". Part of the civilisation-building species: the list of species that build civilisations is "humans, elves and leonids, celestines, runic, smoulder and draconians". Common in Old City: a runic works as a barman, and a runic man appears at Jory's clinic. Inherent markings: the glowing runes "looked like magic tattoos but were an inherent trait". Spellcasters: "Elves and runics were the most common affliction wielders, as their predilection for spells made a ranged power set much more likely". Earth zones: when zones turn Earth people into other species, Jason, Farrah and Dawn spot elves and "the dark-skinned runic people". A runic woman appears with Rick Mercer's team. Kinship with smoulders: "Smoulders and the runic were quite similar, with their dark skin and glowing features".
91.name: Runics

key: Sadi Andali: Culture of a Lawless Desert Country
92.comment: Sadi Andali: Culture of a Lawless Desert Country
92.content: Sadi Andali is "a little dirtball country" in or near an eastern desert, famously almost lawless, with slave markets and no Adventure Society branch. It appears in Book 12 when noble heirs are taken there. Setting: a captive's guess of "Eastern desert?" is answered "Obviously, ever hear of a little dirtball country called Sadi Andali?". Its cells are mud brick. Law: "famous for being almost lawless"; the Adventure Society has no branch there and only sends people in to sweep for illegal research and restricted essences, finding plenty of both. Slave markets: unusual products move through them; Ben asks whether destroying its slave trade is Jason's price. Reach: events "all across Sadi Andali" are set against the great houses of Cyrion. Effect on visitors: Percival Headingway thinks Garret's time there may have "knocked some sense" into him.
keys: Sadi Andali: Culture of a Lawless Desert Country
92.name: Sadi Andali: Culture of a Lawless Desert Country

93.content: Dark-skinned people with glowing red eyes and affinities for earth and fire; the brighthearts are the smoulder of the deep underground realm of Cardinas. Smoulder: "They have natural affinities for earth and fire"; a smoulder friend of Humphrey's parents has the wind essence and his earth affinity evolved into an air affinity. Niko, a member of Beth's team, has dark skin, glowing red eyes and jet-black hair. Brighthearts: in Book 10 fewer than ten thousand of the brightheart smoulder survive, crammed in the citadel cavern. Marla is a fire aspect with skin markings, eyes and hair the yellow-orange of steel in a forge; Lorenn, an ash aspect, has smoky greys. War form: Beaufort prefers his fifteen-foot metal skeleton "war form" but must meet the brightheart smoulders in a form they will accept. Home: the largest chamber of the underground realm was home to most brightheart smoulders.
93.name: Smoulder and Brighthearts

key: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
94.comment: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
94.content: A sea kingdom ruled from Rimaros, where a gold-rank monarch rules, heirs prove themselves as adventurers, and sky islands house the cream of society. Extent: "It rules the Sea of Storms, all the islands on it and all the coastal regions that surround it"; the capital is Rimaros. Sky islands: reserved for "the cream of society": big-name adventurers, long-standing adventuring families and aristocrats; a family known for producing good adventurers is mostly inducted into the nobility, and a house without good adventurers sinks into obscurity. Monarchy: the Storm King is a gold-ranker, which one must be to take the throne; royals are not raised on cores as in most nations, since that disqualifies them here, and potential heirs from every branch are adventurers proving themselves in monster fighting and statecraft in a decades-long contest until the monarch chooses an heir. Titles: the firstborn daughter of the Storm King, if competing, is the Hurricane Princess and the firstborn son the Storm Prince; many royals bow out, often adopting into their non-royal parent's family. Palindromic names: first and last names that are palindromes are assigned in adulthood and mark important family members; the more prominent the family, the rarer the practice, and the royal family shares a name with the capital. Royal looks: the royal family's iconic feature is sapphire hair and eyes.
keys: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
94.name: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms

95.content: A nomad tribe from a region to the north that raids spirit coin convoys in the Greenstone desert and will not accept captured warriors as slaves. Who they are: the "sand pirates" are actually the Ustei Tribe, nomads from a region to the north; Humphrey identifies them as northerners from their hair and clothes. The raids: an expedition is formed to find out why they are so far south and stop them raiding spirit coin shipments. The response: the best outcome is a peaceful return north or an agreement not to attack convoys; failing that, they are to be captured and interrogated. Vincent expects them to talk if shown strength. Captives: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". Later: by Book 12 the Ustei who came south are said to predate the Earth arrivals by about three years.
95.name: The Ustei: Northern Nomad Tribe

key: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
96.comment: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
96.content: The Ustei are nomads from a region to the north of Greenstone, living on oases connected to an astral space and moving with their war barge. Ustei.md covers who they are; this file collects what the text says of their homeland and customs. The homeland: a region to the north of the Greenstone desert, whose oases are connected to the astral space that supplies the desert. When the astral space's water supply failed, the oases "were no longer able to support all the nomad tribes". Travel: the entire tribe lives on a war barge, "easily the equal of a passenger liner", built on giant bones with multiple decks. See Desert_Transport_Skimmers_and_Barges.md. Warriors and ranks: only a fraction of the warriors are iron-rankers, most have one or two essences; bronze-rank captains lead them, and a silver-rank tribal chief commands the tribe. Dress: Humphrey identifies them as northerners "from the hair and clothes". Women, children and slaves: the tribe's women and children were locked away in conditions like slaves, and actual slaves were found in the same conditions. Someone floated the idea of taking the Ustei men as slaves, "which would at least be something they understood". Law of surrender: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". After defeat, they claim the barge and everything in it, including the women, children and slaves, belongs to the victor; "the idea is that now they have to go raiding for more women".
keys: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life
96.name: The Ustei Homeland and the Ustei Way of Life

97.content: A skinny, chihuahua-headed species that is not native to Pallimustus; humans are turned into valash by Earth's transformation zones. Origin: Jason had only seen valash when Earth's transformation zones turned humans into them; they are "a skinny sapient species not native to Pallimustus". Appearance: "skinny bodies and Chihuahua-like heads", shorter than Jason. Outworlders: the valash Jason meets in Yaresh is an outworlder with a silver-rank aura and no sign of core use. Fashion: his fitted white suit is not in the local style and "would have been more at home in a Miami nightclub in the eighties". Zolit Kreen: the valash outworlder introduces himself as "Zolit. Zolit Kreen". He was originally a valash, "attention-grabbing" for being an outworlder and a chihuahua-headed species, and "had spent years working very hard to undo that damage". A niche: he ranked to silver while staying as unremarkable as possible, then retired to be a fight promoter, where "everyone was a little bit strange" and "being a valash outworlder was his" gimmick. Prison: Adventure Society enforcers lock him up after he meets another outworlder, asking about his assistant Benella and messengers. Social standing: despite his small stature he is "not pushed, shoved, or disrespected" in a crowd, with a silver-rank aura.
97.name: Valash

key: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
98.comment: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
98.content: Vitesse is the garden-tower city of Estercost: wealthy, prosperous and full of powerful adventurers, with the Remore Academy and the continent's adventuring elite. This file covers how its people live; the geography is in../06_Places/Vitesse.md. The city of flowers: it is "known as the city of flowers", in what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that have every third or fourth floor given to gardens "using water, light and plant magic to create lush refuges of peace". The towers house the wealthy elite, aristocrats and adventurers, and the headquarters of key organisations. Standing of the great families: the Remore family has no aristocratic title and the Gellers only a small provincial one, and neither is begrudged residences in premier towers. Adventuring: iron-rankers there may not hunt alone, because of the high magic. Adventuring capital: many consider it the adventuring capital of the continent; high magic makes monster manifestations powerful and frequent across the region, which matters because Estercost is full of towns, villages and smaller cities. Detection: the local Adventure Society intercepts monster appearances with a network of towers, something like the Earth grid, instead of leaving notes for wandering adventurers.
keys: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers
98.name: Vitesse: Culture of the City of Flowers

key: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
99.comment: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
99.content: A small-population city that grows around its trees, whose civic government is weaker than its churches and societies, and whose two elf diamond-rankers dominate its adventuring scene. Size and design: only a few tens of thousands live there, but the design accommodates the environment so that the city has the footprint of a much larger centre. Walls and gates: its walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone filling the gaps, tunnels pass through the trunks, and vehicles queue at a gate for inspection. Streets: alleys are nicer than the norm and resemble gardens, with gravel paths through long grass. Government: "In Yaresh, the civic administration is considerably weaker than the churches and the major societies", because one group undermines the Duke for its own ends. The Aristocratic Faction: wealthy aristocrats and a few merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, and who use that power to shape their tenants' ideology. They have no adventurers or researchers behind them, just money and political influence. Diamond-rankers: Allayeth and Charist, both elves; Yaresh has "not just one but two resident diamond-rankers", with Charist the more social and Allayeth the more reclusive, who raised the all-woman team Moon's Edge, led by Miriam Vance. Reunion: in Book 12 much of the reunion group has already left Yaresh to make preparations for the expedition to Earth.
keys: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
99.name: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City

key: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
100.comment: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
100.content: Zartos is a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines and home to the diamond-ranker Virid, Gary's mentor. The text shows it only as a place to work and rest. Setting: "a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines". Celestine community: Gary says "Zartos has a large celestine community"; Rufus has not been, though his brother recommended it. See Celestines.md for the people. Craft: Virid keeps a personal smithy there, "the best place to forge a great work". Gary and Virid forge while the team rests.
keys: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth
100.name: Zartos: Culture of a Celestine City Under the Earth

101.content: The Adventure Society is one of the three great organisations of Pallimustus. Its main purpose is monster extermination: it posts notices, issues contracts, assesses and registers adventurers, and keeps records of their kills. Its insignia is a sword and rod crossed over a shield, stitched on its staff's clothing and embossed on its badges. Restricted essences: Rufus says Death is restricted by itself, and the Magic Society's living document shows one restricted combination, the Succubus essence, which takes two insanely rare essences. A corrupt essence is on the list: a Magic-Society-bound adventurer hands one looted from an elemental to the Adventure Society "since it was on the restricted list"; the Society offers good trades for restricted essences. The wiki's fuller list and its Sacrifice-confluence pit fighter were not found in the text. Neutrality: the Society is described as neutral in disputes between nations. Corruption and reform: Rufus says there "may be some level of corruption in this branch" in Book 1; a later corruption enquiry at the Greenstone branch led to blanket demotions of two- and three-star members, who were bumped back up afterwards.
101.name: The Adventure Society

102.content: The Alchemy Association is the guild of Pallimustus' alchemists. It lends its name to the potions and salves sold in a city, sits just behind the Adventure Society and the Magic Society in a city's guild district, and wants anything that advances alchemy, from Neil's miracle potion recipe to research in Yaresh. The text never describes its ranks or leadership. Branding: a tin of salve Jason buys in Book 1 is labelled "Greenstone Alchemy Association". Membership: Jory is "a member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association". Belinda says the same of another person, "in the Alchemy Association and the Adventure Society". Dual membership is ordinary. Standing: in Greenstone's guild district the Forge Society and the Alchemist Association are "clearly second to the Adventure and Magic Societies, but still occupied impressive chunks of real estate". Assistants: Jason is told he could get assistants from the Association. Interest in recipes: the Association has been "hounding" Neil for the miracle potion recipe. Benefits: organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society, Alchemy Association "and the like" are what the top guilds care about, not material rewards. Brokered supply: a lord brokered the sale of a crate of potions through the Association, and stock runs short until people get their next batches from the vats.
102.name: The Alchemy Association

103.content: Four hidden organisations run through the books. The Order of the Reaper is an ancient order of assassins that churches destroyed. The Builder cult serves a great astral being and uses star seeds and clockwork cores. The Order of Redeeming Light is a Purity zealot order that is in fact the work of Disguise. The Church of Undeath serves the corruption of the cycle itself.
103.name: Cults and Orders

key: The EDJI and the Post-Reveal Institutions
104.comment: The EDJI and the Post-Reveal Institutions
104.content: After magic goes public, Earth gains a layer of governmental and joint institutions on top of the old factions: national departments of Supernatural Affairs, a United Nations office, a multinational taskforce at Asano Village, a joint magitech weapons institute, and the Earth Defence Joint Initiative (EDJI) that Jason forces into being. The Asano clan acts as a faction in its own right and supplies the knowledge on which most of this depends.
keys: The EDJI and the Post-Reveal Institutions
104.name: The EDJI and the Post-Reveal Institutions

key: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
105.comment: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
105.content: Earth has three old magical powers and, from Book 5 on, a fourth. The Network uses essence magic, the Cabal is older and tied to vampires and "old magic", and the Engineers of Ascension (EOA) is a radical group with a secret agenda. The Asano clan is Jason's family turned into a faction. Governments and the United Nations become players when magic is made public.
keys: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan
105.name: Earth's Powers: the Network, the Cabal, the EOA and the Asano Clan

106.content: The Engineers of Ascension (EOA, also written EoA) is the youngest and weakest of Earth's three old powers: a union of outsider groups that tried to engineer a higher form of humanity and prepare for the day magic became public. Four "cardinals" ran it under Mr North, and its sabotage of the Grid ended the secrecy of magic and ended the organisation. Earth_Powers.md covers it briefly; this file is the full account.
106.name: The Engineers of Ascension

107.content: A guild is an adventuring organisation that recruits, trains and backs its members and takes on a share of the Adventure Society's work. Guilds carry weight in the Society's surge quotas and in politics. Great families have their own guilds or schools; some local powers (the Aristocratic Faction) deliberately avoid personal power.
107.name: Guilds, Houses and Local Powers

key: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
108.comment: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
108.content: The Magic Society records and regulates magic: it keeps the register of essences and their combinations, oversees spirit coin farms, runs communication networks and hoards research. The Alchemy Association and the Artifice Association are the guilds of the potion-makers and of the item-makers. In Book 11 onward a rival, the Magical Research Association (MRA), challenges the Magic Society with open access to knowledge. The living document: a marble-and-gold tablet, connected to a central record, that updates as the record changes and holds the full list of every essence and essence combination known to the Society. It is how Farrah and Rufus look up what a combination will produce. Water link: the Society's chambers allow conversation at a distance. See../03_Magic_and_Adventuring/Alchemy_Artifice_and_Magical_Materials.md (communication). Spirit coin farms: registered farms exist. The Adventure Society treats anything touching the farms as three-star work. Greenstone branch: directed by Lucian Lamprey, who uses the Fortress as his office; his deputy director Pochard Finn is an elf and a local who runs the city campus and is "the de facto director of Greenstone's Magic Society". Pochard is Clive's boss. By Book 11 Pochard has become director: "It's Director now, Standish. I haven't been deputy director for several years".
keys: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
108.name: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA

109.content: The MRA is Clive Standish's rival to the Magic Society: an open-access research body that grew from nothing to prominence in a handful of years, drew patronage away from the older society, and was shielded by the Adventure Society, governments and churches. The Magic Society tries to crush it, and is later shown to have been behind vandalism of the Vitesse campus. Founding and growth: "In just a handful of years since its inception, the Magical Research Association had exploded into prominence". Clive has gone from silver-rank team member to the head of "a rival to the Magic Society". Open access: where the Magic Society "leveraged its research and secrets for political power", the MRA gave open access to records and research libraries. Many prominent academics stayed with the Society for personal gain; the MRA is "a bastion for young, bold and innovative researchers". Funding and shield: organisations fund the MRA knowing the results will be freely available. Government authorities, the Adventure Society and several churches, especially Knowledge, contribute, and also act as a shield against the Magic Society's attempts to crush it. Projects: it is closely associated with the new sky communication network, and rumoured to be researching a transportation network, from years of study into the network Clive tracked earlier. Satellites solved the problem of monsters attacking relay towers. Its portal network project is reported to Clive by Vice Chancellor Grantham.
109.name: The Magical Research Association (MRA)

110.content: The Mirage Chamber Association is the body that owns and runs the mirage chamber complex in Jayapura, the biggest such facility the books show. A mirage chamber projects illusions that feel real to those inside; the Association turns that into a training service and a league sport, and it is powerful in its city for it. It is the only named body for mirage chambers; the Geller family's private chamber in Greenstone is not part of it.
110.name: The Mirage Chamber Association

key: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
111.comment: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
111.content: Two different bodies carry the Reaper's name. The Cult of the Reaper is the old body of worshippers of the great astral being called the Reaper, who venerate "the finality of death" and work alongside the Church of Death. The Order of the Reaper is a faction that split from the cult to become assassins and political power-brokers, was "destroyed" by a coalition of churches, and has quietly returned. Cults_and_Orders.md holds the short entries; this file is the full account.
keys: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper
111.name: The Order and the Cult of the Reaper

112.content: The Cabal is the oldest of Earth's three dominant magical forces: a loose collection of factions of vampires, fae and other creatures older than recorded history, with old money and old habits. It split when ancient vampires were woken and the vampire lords rose. Part of it sides with humanity and, in the end, is openly led by Boris Ket Lundi. Earth_Powers.md covers it briefly; this file is the full account.
112.name: The Cabal

113.content: The Network is Earth's largest magical organisation: a federation of old secret societies, now national and city branches, that uses essence magic, controls most of the world's spirit coin supply, and maintains the Grid that finds and contains incursions. It went public as the Global Defense Network when the monster waves began, and later fractured into four blocs. Earth_Powers.md covers it beside the other factions; this file is the full account.
113.name: The Network

114.content: The church of Death is the Pallimustus institution for the passage of the dead: it certifies who has died and returned, helps with registration, and has long watched against necromancy. It works alongside the Cult of the Reaper, which serves as its hidden dagger.
114.name: The Church of Death

115.content: The church of Dominion is the church of rulership and the exercise of authority. It is the outlier among churches in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. The god is often seen; his priests rarely are. Temple: in Greenstone it is "the strange temple" on the Divine Square, called the temple of Dominion. Control of clergy: other churches make little call on adventuring clergy; Dominion's is the most prominent outlier in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb. Absent priests: a character thought power and control were the church's remit, but has "never even met a priest of Dominion". The god's description: Dominion tells Jason he is "oppression-friendly", not an oppressor. A priest's account: Brian, a priest of Dominion, says, "The irony of our church... is that those most favoured by our god will never be in it. We guide them, and sometimes we serve them." The church does not venerate power itself, "but the establishment of power over others. Rulership. The exercising of authority". He calls slavery "a petty tyranny" compared to what the god looks to.
115.name: The Church of Dominion

116.content: The church of Hero is the church of the god of heroes. The books show it through its priest Gwydion Remore, its temple in the Worship Ring in Outer Rexion, and its long collection of demigod relics. Priests: Gwydion Remore, Rufus's older brother, is a priest of Hero. Relics: the church has collected the relics of dead demigods for millennia. The temple: a sculpture of a leonid in bronze, silver and gold with dark iron stands in the middle of the boulevard before the temple of Hero in the Worship Ring of Outer Rexion.
116.name: The Church of Hero

117.content: The church of Knowledge keeps the libraries, checks the assessments and has its acolytes at hand where information matters. From Book 7 it is also quietly building a fighting force across the world, which at the end of Book 9 stops hiding.
117.name: The Church of Knowledge

key: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
118.comment: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
118.content: The church of Purity is the church of cleansing: it supplies the healers who treat curses and taint, and it first developed the techniques for removing star seeds. In Book 3 its leadership vanishes when its involvement with the Builder cult comes to light, and the churches later learn it has been operating outside its dictates for some time.
keys: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family
118.name: The Church of Purity and the Lasalle Family

119.content: The church of Undeath serves the god of undeath and raises the unliving. It is stamped out wherever it is found, lies dormant for generations, and strikes only when given a chance. Its priests are unliving things led by Garth Larosse. A past plague: a zombie plague had "a Temple of Undeath at the heart of it all", with the local mayor as high priest. Why it is stamped out: those who fall to the undead become undead servants, allies and enemies alike, "why they are so thoroughly stamped out whenever and wherever they are found". Dormancy: "The Church of Undeath does not act frequently. We don't give them the chance". It is one of the few reliable allies of the Church of Destruction. Opportunity: a place of magic gone wrong and a hidden location is "a veritable wish list" for it. Priests: dozens of priests of Undeath, gold and silver rank, lead the army. They use their god's power to feed on elemental magic and make more powerful undead. Leadership: Garth Larosse is the High Priest, himself an unliving thing nine feet tall, in a dark green cloak. He leads the priests. Claiming: the high priest "could not himself" hold claim over the unliving's unified territories, which an avatar then does. A holy war: an undead army led by priests of Undeath is raised as a question of whether it counts as a holy war. Rexion: the Undeath priesthood overran the domains of the gods in the old brightheart city. Jason says building a temple of Undeath would be repugnant, as a drastic act.
119.name: The Church of Undeath

120.content: The church of the Healer is the institution through which most healing on Pallimustus is done, with its priests drawing their abilities from the god's essences and awakening stones. It is strongest in isolated areas, and its Greenstone branch is the subject of the first great church scandal in the books.
120.name: The Church of the Healer

121.content: Burning Violet is an old, elite guild based in Vitesse, tied to the Remore family and the Remore Academy. Most of Jason's friends belong to it; Jason applies in Book 12, and the application becomes entangled with a power struggle over the Remore family's control. Origin and links: "an old guild, but after Rufus' grandfather became guild leader, it became more and more associated with the Remore Academy". Its membership is Rufus's family plus allies such as Gary and Farrah. Members: most big-family graduates of the Academy do not join, so it is mostly graduates who do not come from power or money. The Academy's scouting programme gives scholarships to people with potential. Symbol: purple flames in the shape of a flower on a belt buckle. Farrah introduces herself as "Burning Violet guild, although I don't have a guild pin on me". Induction: Miles Cotezee says Jason's team has been "inducted into the Burning Violet". By Book 11 all of Team Biscuit are members except Jason and Taika.
121.name: The Burning Violet Guild

key: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
122.comment: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
122.content: During a monster surge the Adventure Society assigns every adventurer a minimum action quota, and runs a contribution board as an incentive on top. Guilds are given the bulk of the quotas and compete for the board's non-material rewards. Action quotas: after clearance an adventurer is "assigned an action quota" and must report regularly to the jobs hall for contracts. "Action quotas are the minimum requirements every adventurer has to fulfil during the monster surge". The contribution board: contracts taken beyond the quota carry contribution point values, tallied on weekly and overall leaderboards, with rewards each week and major rewards at the end of the surge. A large leaderboard in the jobs hall shows the top hundred contributors by action quota. Who pays for the rewards: societies, associations and governments give out hefty rewards; in return the Adventure Society "assigns high contribution point values to the contracts that provide that protection". What guilds want: the big guilds monopolise the top of the board, but want "access to civic services" and organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society and Alchemy Association, not material rewards. Material rewards are the lower-rung prizes, which small guilds and independents can reach.
keys: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board
122.name: Guild Quotas and the Contribution Board

123.content: The Sapphire Crown is the royal guild of Rimaros: a guild that works directly for the royal family, whose members rotate through the royal guard. It carries real power, and is held to the same surge quotas as any other guild. Purpose: in many places the role of guard had become ceremonial; "in Rimaros, the solution came in the form of a guild". Royal support: it is one of the most powerful guilds in Rimaros because of the support of the royal family, many of whom are among its most capable members; in return all non-royal members "were required to periodically serve within the royal guard". Membership: stringent, mostly from guild families; loyalty is paramount. All members are examined quarterly, rising to monthly or weekly while serving in the guard. Quotas: the royal family does not shield it from the guilds' activity quotas. Trenchant Moore, a human gold-ranker in a guild of celestines, carries a good portion. Liberty: even its gold-rankers have "a rich amount of liberty", an exception to the usual monitoring of gold-rankers. Standing: Liara is "a figure of accomplishment and respect in the Sapphire Crown", where power, not legacy, is the ultimate authority. Operations: it joins Amouz family members in sweeping the Builder cult's hideouts, watches over a familiar ritual, and uses the duelling arena as a training hall.
123.name: The Sapphire Crown Guild

key: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
124.comment: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
124.content: Team Shining Scabbard is the adventuring team of Prince Valdis of the Mirror Kingdom, built around the healer Sigrid Freyn. The text calls it a royal-backed team, not a guild; the plan's "backers" are the Mirror King's family and the kingdom's resources. This file records what is stated. Origin: Jason says Valdis, "Prince of the Mirror Kingdom", is "the reason their team exists". Humphrey says its members "were being prepared for Valdis's team before any of them ever received an essence". Structure: "their team is built around their healer, Sigrid. She facilitates and directs strategy"; the strategic core is Sigrid and the political core is Valdis. The match: in the mirage chamber fight Jason's team defeats it by going for Sigrid while feinting at Valdis. Team Biscuit's friends: Team Shining Scabbard came through the Reaper trials and trained with Jason's team at iron rank, and Sigrid is Valdis's wife. Royal backing: the Mirror King's own portal specialist portals the team to Yaresh, and Valdis says "the kingdom's thick with princes and princesses", so the King will take a good adventurer over any of his children. The team has royalty in the group, "less impressive with the Mirror Kingdom's surplus of princes and princesses". Administration: Valdis assembles the arena event in under two days, admired by the duke.
keys: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing
124.name: Team Shining Scabbard and the Mirror Kingdom's Backing

125.content: House Amouz is a Rimaros noble house that controls or has a share in more than half of the mining operations in the Sea of Storms. Its heir is captured by the Builder cult in Book 8, and the family sends its people in numbers to the cleanup in Book 9. Business: House Amouz "controls or has an interest in more than half of the mining operations in the Sea of Storms, including the bulk of high-rank mineral acquisition". Ties to the royals: Liara's husband married out of House Amouz into the royal family, but remains a high-level manager in the family's business interests. Heir: Gibson Amouz is "son of Lord Cassin Amouz and heir to the seat of House Amouz". He is captured by the cult, which wants the family's secrets. Lord Cassin: a gold-ranker with a goatee, who confronts Liara over his son's capture. Liara suspects the son was targeted because of what he would be told on becoming gold rank and ready to assume his seat. Volunteers: the Amouz family volunteers in numbers that surprise even Liara in the sweep of the hideouts.
125.name: House Amouz

126.content: The Davones are a Greenstone family with close ties to the Mercers who were, in effect, servants of that family for years. Neil Davone is their best-known member, and by Book 12 the family's standing has changed. Mercer ties: "the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers" sent their boys to the Mercer compound, where Neil spent time as a boy. Teaming: the Davone and Mercer families "colluded to team him with Thadwick Mercer at a young age". Servants to the Mercers: Neil's family had been "stuck as what amounts to servants to the Mercers for years" but now the most powerful people in the city must show them respect. House Davone: in Book 12 Neil escorts three of House Davone's young scions, his nieces and nephews.
126.name: House Davone

127.content: The Gellers are an adventuring dynasty with branches across the world and a seat at an estate in the Greenstone delta. They hold only a small provincial title, train their young hard in Greenstone, and are the richest family in the city. The estate: the Geller family estate sits behind a thick high wall, so vast that monsters are as likely to be inside as out; household guards are iron-rank essence users. The seat is "a sprawling estate in the delta", landscaped on secure ground with artful waterways and decades of defences. Standing: "The Geller family stood at the peak of Greenstone society, and their local power was just a fragment of their world-spanning influence". The family "sprawled across continents", and branch families exist: one patriarch leads a branch family. Training: Geller family tradition is to supply scions with enough awakening stones to get started, while the rest must be earned. The family trains its young at "the south end of nowhere" so they can make their own mistakes, with facilities including a mirage chamber and arena. Why Greenstone: other Greenstone families envy the influence the Gellers hold elsewhere and want outside connections. Some families "simply wanted the next adventure", as the Gellers do. The academy annex: the Remore Academy's Greenstone annex is a joint venture with the Gellers, with an internal Geller faction opposed to the agreement.
127.name: House Geller

128.content: House Headingway is one of Estercost's pre-eminent families, with its title from Cyrion, the heart of civilisation. It is humbled in Book 12 when family members clash with Jason. Standing: Garret Headingway is "an upper-echelon member of House Headingway, one of Estercost's pre-eminent families". Percival Headingway is the patriarch and Duke, "holder of the family's highest title", which "came from Cyrion", unlike the claimed titles of rural city-state aristocrats; he serves under the throne but his power "dwarfed even the most prestigious of theirs". Power: "the true power of House Headingway came from their adventurers"; adventurer training had been mandatory in the family when Percival was young. Ben: Benjamin Headingway is the family's top gold-ranker and represents the noble houses of Cyrion when they ask to speak to Jason. Factions: one faction, "the pure politicians", wants a proportional political reply; Percival knows they are wrong. Mariska Headingway manages business affairs. Pressure: the Sky Link Company decides whether "continuing a relationship with House Headingway is appropriate". The affair: the Dominion church keeps the captured family members from genuine danger.
128.name: House Headingway

129.content: The Ketterings are a Greenstone family tied to the Mercers who send their sons to the Mercer compound. They have people in Old City and supply adventurers, including Dustin and Hudson Kettering. Mercer ties: the Davone and Kettering families have "close ties to the Mercers" and send their boys to Thadwick. Adventurers: Hudson Kettering is on Beth Cavendish's team. Dustin Kettering, a local, takes Jonah's defender role in Rick's team. Old City: "The Ketterings have people in Old City"; Danielle coordinates with the Kettering family to mobilise them. Dustin: a friend of Neil's from Thadwick's team. His family obliged him to work with the Mercers.
129.name: House Kettering

130.content: The Mercers are a very powerful Greenstone family, tied to the Duke through marriage, who run spirit coin farms and shape the city's other families through their patronage. Thadwick Mercer is their heir; Cassandra is his sister. Power: "Thadwick's Mercer family was very powerful in Greenstone", and more so when "the Duke of Greenstone's brother, Thadwick's father, married into it". The family ranks above many others, especially those without aristocratic title. Residence: their main residence is a manor on the Island, five towers set in a ring connected by glass walkways, "a feat of magical engineering". Numbers: no family can match the Gellers' numbers, but the Mercers "still made an impressive showing". Farms: Humphrey says most of the spirit coin farms are operated by his family or the Mercers, under Magic Society regulation. The Mercers do not offer part ownership as the Gellers do. Household: the household staff are "raked over the coals" when Thadwick is provoked. Patronage: "Thadwick had needed friends his own age and the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers, had frequently sent their own boys over". Neil Davone grew up at the Mercer compound. Obligation: Neil and Dustin were forced to train and work with Thadwick through their families' obligation to the Mercers. The Mercer family gave Neil training, facilities and resources "that only the Gellers could match". The Mercer family is large and Thadwick was raised mainly by his father.
130.name: House Mercer

key: House Remore and the Remore Academy
131.comment: House Remore and the Remore Academy
131.content: The Remores are a family of educators and adventurers in Vitesse who hold no title but run the Remore Academy, one of the most respected adventurer schools in the world. Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker, is arch-chancellor; Rufus is the heir. The Academy: the family "operates the Remore Academy, which is a big deal everywhere, not just Vitesse". It runs a Greenstone training annex built with the Gellers. Roland: "Although Roland Remore was rarely spotted on the Remore Academy campus, the presence of the diamond-rank arch-chancellor was always felt". Rufus as heir: Rufus "was the prince of Remore Academy, the talented heir-apparent to the power and prestige of his family legacy". Graduates: an academy graduate should have better control of her aura, so students have standing among adventurers. No title: the Remore family has no aristocratic title; the family's prestige comes from "generations of accomplishment", not their name. Like other prestige families they are offered titles and refuse. Scholarships: Rufus's grandfather set up a scouting programme for people with potential, with scholarships and dormitories. Students: scions of international mercantile guilds, adventuring families, aristocrats and royalty, taught by methodology studied from across the globe. The family nurtured Rufus's talent with carefully engineered opportunities. Guild influence: some in the Burning Violet guild think the Academy has too much influence over guild affairs.
keys: House Remore and the Remore Academy
131.name: House Remore and the Remore Academy

key: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
132.comment: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
132.content: The royal family of Rimaros rules the sky-island city and its kingdom under a Storm King. It has its own guild (the Sapphire Crown), marries into the engineering and mining houses for stability, and carries sapphire hair and eyes. The guild: the royal family supports the Sapphire Crown, and many of its own are among its most capable members. See Sapphire_Crown.md. Marriage politics: Zara, a princess, is matched with a member of House Irios, the pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering. The union would have created political stability before the surge. Liara's husband was born into House Amouz. Family traits: Zareen has "the iconic sapphire hair and eyes". Liara: a gold-rank member of the royal house, in charge of screening adventurers for Builder cultists. Zara: although she left the royal family for political reasons, "the Storm King did not stop caring for his daughter".
keys: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)
132.name: House Rimaros (the Royal House of Rimaros)

133.content: Cyrion is the capital of Estercost and, even discounting its farmland, the largest city in the world. From the air it stretches to the horizon in every direction; "Cyrion looked like Tokyo by way of the Emerald City of Oz" from the air, with massive lakes and whole forests inside the urban sprawl. Book 7 calls it home to the Adventure Society's continental council, though Book 6 puts that council in Vitesse. Seat of the Estercost crown and, in Book 7, the Adventure Society's continental council. Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families, and house guards were technically a form of indentured servitude. Very well-paid servitude"; many noble houses use that power to keep guards from leaving. Before the series: the capital of Estercost. Book 6: the Society's analytical office tracks events involving Jason from here. Book 12: Jason visits to prepare for the return to Earth, studying more than a decade of Clive's work on restoring the bridge between Pallimustus and Earth; the Cyrion branch director is Jacinta Adeline. The noble houses' abuse of indenture law triggers the System withdrawal.
133.name: Cyrion

134.content: Jason's domains are territories that his soul's power fills: the zones he claimed on Earth and Pallimustus, his soul realm and astral kingdom, and the places he has made permanent. This file gathers the rules the text gives for living in them and for being his enemy in them. For what each place looks like, see the individual place files. The file is level 3 because it includes Book 12-13 rules.
134.name: Jason's Domains: The Rules

135.content: Greenstone is a colony city at the mouth of a river delta in the low-magic far south of the Africa-like continent. It is the first city Jason knows on Pallimustus and the setting of most of Books 1-3. It was founded because its conditions suit low-end spirit coin farms: stable low magic, in a place that is also livable and close to the desert. It is a place of green marble, walled harbours, crime lords with gentlemanly manners, and a Society full of ambitious, mid-ranked people who use monster cores rather than fight for their ranks. Colonial status: the city began as a colony from the wider kingdom. The Adventure Society is a major force, but the isolation makes the local branch dependent on local powers; Rufus's remark to the village mayor is that "compromises must be made."; The Adventure Society branch is directed by Elspeth Arella. Vincent Trenslow runs assessments and assigns contracts. The Magic Society branch is directed by Lucian Lamprey, a silver-ranker who watches Fortress fights from a viewing box. His deputy is Pochard Finn, whose son Cassowary serves as Lucian's dogsbody. The Big Three of the underworld: Clarissa Ventress (mansion in the canal district), Cole Silva (obsessed with Sophie) and Adris Dorgan. They keep the underworld running and avoid gang war because it draws the attention of the Island authorities.
135.name: Greenstone

136.content: For each place that changes, this file says what state it is in during each of the seven playable eras defined in Era_Selection.md. Use it to avoid placing a destroyed city on the map or a ruined one in its prime. A place missing from an era is simply not shown there in the lines read. The file is level 3 because it includes Book 12-13 outcomes.
136.name: Locations by Era

137.content: The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, founded by Soramir Rimaros, a diamond-ranker who was its first king. Its principal city, Rimaros, spans three islands and is protected by storm accumulators. Its monarch, the Storm King, must be gold-rank; the successor is chosen by the previous king after a contest. Its royal guard is supplied by the Sapphire Crown guild, whose members are examined quarterly, and more often in the guard. It is the first place Jason lands when he returns to Pallimustus in Book 7, just as a monster surge begins. The royal family: Soramir Rimaros (founding king, a diamond-ranker with emerald hair who prefers disguise), Liara Rimaros (gold princess; husband Baseph), their children (Dara, the eldest, and Zara, the "Hurricane Princess"). The Sapphire Crown: the royal guild; non-royals serve in the royal guard and take quarterly exams. Commander of the royal guard: Trenchant Moore, introduced as "Commander Trenchant Moore of the royal guard" and called "the siege sword". House Irios: "the pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering" whose defences protect Rimaros and many fortress towns; the family is "known as the shield of" the kingdom. The text of its founder being Soramir's "brother" is not checked here. The Magic Society holds the second-largest sky island in Rimaros, after the palace. The Adventure Society in Rimaros registers Jason and Farrah and questions the irregularities in his record.
137.name: Rimaros (the Storm Kingdom)

138.content: Vitesse, in the kingdom of Estercost, is the City of Flowers, "located in what Jason Asano would know as the French Riviera". Its skyline is made of the garden towers: huge towers with flowering vines spilling down the exterior, "most had every third or fourth floor dedicated to gardens using water, light and plant magic", which are residences for the wealthy elite and headquarters of key organisations. It is a high-magic, wealthy city (the social programmes and labour laws described below are not confirmed in the lines read). It is the home of Remore Academy and of Burning Violet, and the place Rufus, Gary and Farrah come from. Governed within the kingdom of Estercost. The books disagree on where the Adventure Society's continental council sits: Book 6 says "the continental council for the Adventure Society sat in Vitesse, rather than the capital city, Cyrion", while Book 7 calls Cyrion "home to the Adventure Society's continental council". Remore family influence is pervasive: Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker who took over Burning Violet long ago, is the Academy's arch-chancellor and Rufus's grandfather. Burning Violet is the Remore family's elite guild. Strong labour protections and social programmes mean an unusually large comfortable middle class.
138.name: Vitesse

139.content: Yaresh is a rainforest city with "only a few tens of thousands" of people, spread over "the footprint of a much larger centre" because its design deeply accommodates the natural environment. Its walls are "a line of massive trees with walls of glossy black stone filling the gaps", with tunnels through the trunks. It is the centre of the Battle of Yaresh in Book 9 and the gateway to the natural array beneath it. Ruled by a duke, who attends the arena and sends representatives with Adventure and Magic Society convoys. The Aristocratic Faction, a bloc of wealthy aristocrats and merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, is the dominant political force in the region; see 05_Organisations/Guilds_and_Houses.md. Two diamond-rank adventurers live here: Allayeth and Charist, both elves. Hana Shavar is "the High Priestess of the Church of the Healer for the city of Yaresh"; she runs relief for refugees, and after the messenger attack much of Yaresh's population is homeless and housed at Jason's cloud palace. Adventure Society presence is strong; Rufus stays in Yaresh during part of Book 9. Before the series: the natural array and the Smoulder city of Cardinas lie beneath Yaresh. Book 8: Jason's team learns of Yaresh while dealing with Builder and messenger activity.
139.name: Yaresh

140.content: An ancient, circular, overgrown city in an astral space with a sea around it, entered through the drowned fortress at Sky Scar Lake. It is the site of Emir Bahadir's contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, a trial gauntlet that tests wisdom, courage, capability, intellect and resolve.
140.name: The City of Fallen Echoes (Book 2)

141.content: A water-and-islands astral space reached from the desert by a submerged aperture. A large Greenstone expedition goes in at the climax of Book 1 to find what is disrupting it. They are ambushed by a construct army.
141.name: The Desert Astral Space (Book 1)

142.content: An artificial astral space that turns out to be a giant Builder boarding vessel. The Order of the Reaper repurposed its delivery system into a portal system powered by Jason-like power. The team enters it around the middle of Book 3.
142.name: The Reaper-Trials Boarding Vessel (Book 3)

key: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
143.comment: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
143.content: Jason's personal space grows over the series: a dimensional inventory that only he can physically enter becomes the Spirit Vault, which those who trust him completely can enter, then a spirit domain, a soul realm that travels along the world link, and finally an astral kingdom once he possesses an astral throne and gate. Places inside it are described below.
keys: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom
143.name: Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom

144.content: A transformation zone is a sealed dome or sphere in which a place is rewritten; the Kostroma sphere extends underground and completely encapsulates the city. Inside is a genesis space: a landscape of anomalies, territories and cores. The wiki's phrase for zones, "scabs over dimensional ulcers", was not found in the book text; the later Book 13 briefing speaks of removing reality cores making "scabs on wounds in the universe" only in earlier notes. In Book 5 Dawn names the danger "dimensional ulceration" and says the worst case is that the dimensional membrane rapidly collapses and the world is annihilated, tearing a chunk out of reality; it is more likely contained to the planet or at least the solar system. She adds that "in the best case it will establish a second source of magic that will start feeding into this world".
144.name: Transformation Zones and Genesis Space

145.content: Dimensional Artefact Site One, called the artefact city, is "a small city" in outback Australia, with "nine thousand or so workers" before an evacuation, built around the standing stones where Jason and Farrah left Earth. It is run by a multinational coalition and is where the Earth end of the Earth-Pallimustus bridge sits. Director of Operations: Lenora Coleman, Director of Operations for Dimensional Artefact Site One; she was a graduate stuck for two years in a monitoring station when the site was "little more than some pre-fab buildings", and is a bureaucrat and a core-user. Deputy: Barry, "what amounted to mayor of the artefact city"; assistant Cassie; Security Commander Higgins. Sub-Commander Keene leads a security team under Director Lenora Coleman. The original director was Gordon Truffett, who chose the site's name and is now the Australian Prime Minister; he came to power "through fearmongering over magical gender transitions during rank-up". Gold-rankers on the rotating roster are mostly American and Chinese, which is why Lenora does not have the command her title suggests. A bomber attack leaves the standing stones unharmed.
145.name: Dimensional Artefact Site One (Australia)

146.content: Casselton Beach is Jason's hometown, a tourist beach town on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales where he was born. It is where he wakes in Book 4 after dying on Pallimustus, and it is the model for the head-shaped fortress he later builds in a transformation zone. Asano Village is the family compound on clifftop land nearby, built by the family after the magic arrives. Book 4: Jason wakes in the hospital; contacts uncle Hiro through the Stone Wall bar in Sydney's Kings Cross; reveals magic to his niece Emi, then to the family. Books 5-6: the family evacuates to Asano Village when the Grid is sabotaged. Book 11: the clan lives in Jason's astral domains in Europe. Book 12: the Australian government seizes Asano Village and the stone-circle land and gives them to Noriko's Japanese-line "true Asano clan", allied to the Network (Noriko says the System link is "utter nonsense"). Book 13 (2038): after negotiation the Australian government declares Asano Village and the surrounding area a special-interest territory, "similar to the standing stones", to be managed by a multinational organisation with Lenora Coleman in charge; Jason says his family built it with their own money and toil, and Prime Minister Truffett is named as the one who suggested the seizure.
146.name: Casselton and Asano Village

key: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
147.comment: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
147.content: An incursion is a proto-astral space that opens on Earth and spills monsters into the surrounding area. Spaces are rated by category and last "forty-three hours, as a baseline". This file records the sites where the story takes place.
keys: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)
147.name: Incursion Sites (Dorrigo, Makassar, Broken Hill and others)

148.content: Nitra, in western Slovakia, is a city that became "a major centre for the Network after the organization had been pushed out of Bratislava by vampires". It is too small to host ancient vampires but large enough to warrant Network protection. At the end of Book 5 a transformation zone forms there; in Book 6 Jason claims it and it becomes his first Earth spirit domain.
148.name: Nitra (Slovakia)

149.content: Saint-Étienne, France, is the site of the Dimensional Fortress, a permanent astral space found by the Network's Lyon branch in 1948. In Book 4 Jason frees Farrah from it; in Book 6 it becomes a second transformation zone, which Jason claims and later turns into a whimsical cloud city of refugees.
149.name: Saint-Étienne (France)

150.content: Arcazitlan is a fortress town dug into the wall of a rocky gorge in jungle country, where Jason arrives alone at the start of the surge and fights bone feasters. Its region is not named in the lines checked. Book 7: Jason lands nearby after dropping from the sky, reaches the fort during a night attack by bone feasters (emaciated, eyeless humanoid monsters with large mouths) and helps defend it; he leaves by road with Shade as a land skimmer.
150.name: Arcazitlan

151.content: Boko is an old desert city of academics and artists to the north of Greenstone, with a native population, a Duke, an Adventure Society branch and a Magic Society presence. Jason first arrives there by portal at the end of the Ustei expedition. In Book 12 it is destroyed when he is assassinated there. The scholars: "Scholars of the arts. Painting, poetry, sculpture, dance"; people travel from across the continent to visit its theatres. People: almost entirely human and very dark-skinned, with local fashion loose and breathable, calmer than the Ustei's. Rule: a Duke of Boko, a silver-ranker through cores, as is normal for political leaders; noble houses exist. Adventurers: the Adventure Society has a branch, but Boko "was not a strong adventuring city". Trouble: a movement against intellectuals among low-rankers began in Boko proper before it spread out; officials suspect more sinister backing and a power base shift to Greenstone and Boko. Book 1: the Adventure Society returns the Ustei captives to Boko, where Jason arrives through Hester's portal; he, Gary and Rufus explore it. Book 12: Li Li Mei lives in Boko and is being hunted. After the assassination the city is evacuated, the blast containment zone gives out and the city is gone; most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated. They shelter in Jason's astral kingdom. The crater becomes a harbour, and Jason names the astral city New Water, not Boko.
151.name: Boko

152.content: Cartise was a river city and the major hub of trade and travel in its area, destroyed just before the great surge when the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space and a diamond-rank monster then overwhelmed the city. Jason's team clears monsters from its ruins in Book 9. Before: "the river city of Cartise", the major hub for trade and travel in the area. It had many adventurers who now protect the fortress towns. The fall: the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space, which separated from the world with widespread destruction; a diamond-rank monster manifested shortly after and overwhelmed the city; most people were evacuated to towns along the river. After: the ruins look like London after the Blitz, with blocks reduced to fist-sized rubble. Refugees overpopulate the surrounding towns and the loss strains logistics. Clearing the ruins: Jason's team sweeps a route guided by an Adventure Society functionary named Vestine, as one of several teams.
152.name: Cartise

153.content: Casallini is a small border city of Girlano, close to the coast where Girlano comes nearest to the Sea of Storms. It is where Sophie's Book 8 delivery contract leads, and where a gang is hired to ambush her on behalf of Purity loyalists. Gangs and cartels: the surrounding country is run by cartels producing heavily controlled or banned substances from rare plants and minerals. The eight men who ambush Sophie are members of a small gang from the nearby city, one of many satellite groups to the local cartel, mostly strongmen who keep low-end officials in line. Hired muscle: they are silver-rank in their forties, "raw garbage" with no training and reeking of cores, hired by Purity loyalists to bring Sophie in. Adventure Society presence: the Society ignores borders and keeps monsters out of population centres; its neutrality is why Sophie heads this way, and Liara says "we have a large force in Casallini because it's a border city". Smuggler's paths: semi-hidden paths through jungle-covered hills avoid border checkpoints, which have no patrols during the surge. Character: "a lawless town full of crappy guys" in Sophie's words.
153.name: Casallini

154.content: The Dragon Lands are the Pallimustus version of Antarctica: an island continent that is not icy but volcanic, the native land of the draconians. Jason's sky ship passes over it in Book 12. Peoples: draconians; they are called isolationist and are not welcoming to strangers, and trade through proxies outside their lands. Trade: agricultural products are the second-largest trade through Greenstone's port, after low-rank spirit coins. Most nations tariff the goods heavily over political issues, which makes them a luxury food.
154.name: The Dragon Lands

155.content: Girlano is a landlocked inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom, ostensibly a kingdom but controlled by cartels that produce heavily controlled or banned substances, with a puppet government. It is a smuggling region on the Storm Kingdom's border. Cartels: the illicit leadership keeps its position through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up the puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression. Trade: the rare plants and minerals of the region are what the cartels exploit, and strong public sanctions and border controls surround the nation. Adventure Society: it ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with. Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers"; Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" and tempting. Book 8: Sophie heads toward Girlano and Casallini on a specialised delivery. Book 9: the team turns east at the coast, not south toward Girlano.
155.name: Girlano

156.content: Hornis is a port city on the coast south and around from Greenstone, reached overland through the delta, the veldt and then south. It is Greenstone's nearest rival port, used for smuggling and escapes, and a stop on the team's route home in Book 9. Adventure Society: Hornis has a branch that mounts large searches. Magic Society: Hornis has its own Magic Society people and a mirage chamber that Danielle helped rebuild and maintains. Underworld: the Big Three's influence is a factor in Greenstone; Sophie plans to buy her way past it in Hornis. Book 1: Sophie plans to flee through the delta and the veldt to Hornis with the spirit coin vault's money. Book 2: smuggled materials are traced to shipments into Hornis before being moved to private vessels; Jonah's team is found in Hornis on a boat bound for distant shores. Book 3: Lucian Lamprey hopes to escape to Hornis through a contact. Book 9: the team's route home runs south, across the Great Southern Continent, then north to Hornis on the way to Greenstone, Vitesse and Cyrion. Book 12: a Greenstone resident says Hornis is the furthest south he has been.
156.name: Hornis

157.content: Isart is named once: a city on Jason's procession south where Emir asks to meet him to discuss a job and bring the person who made the cloud flasks. Emir says there is "a city called Isart that you should arrive at on your procession south", will meet Jason there when the detour is done, will arrive in about two weeks and bring the maker of the cloud flasks. No later scene in the chapter files shows Jason reaching Isart, and nothing describes the city.
157.name: Isart

158.content: Jayapura is a port on the northern coast of Pranay, the large southern land equivalent to Sri Lanka, and the birthplace of Hester. Jason's team stays several days after the Reaper trial to awaken abilities, summon familiars and get tattoos. Mirage Chamber Association: owns the complex, has close ties to the Magic Society, Adventure Society and local government and holds significant power. Entertainment: essence users fight one another or illusions for a paying audience.
158.name: Jayapura

159.content: Kazlahk is a wealthy coastal city on the eastern border of Estercost, surrounded by desert and used for spirit coin farms, with a famously scalding climate. Wealth: its spirit coins and sea trade; as with Greenstone, the empty desert is a premium site for spirit coin farms, but the higher magic makes for more valuable denominations. Kazlahk University of Medicine: the most notable beach institution; healing studies focus on essence and ritual magic over alchemy because the Magic Society and Adventure Society fund them, with some money from the Healer's church. Its School of Alchemical Efficiency appears in a disclaimer.
159.name: Kazlahk

160.content: Kurdansk is a river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil and Sophie Wexler's birthplace. It has a busy skyport, an entertainment quarter in a former warehouse district, many dark-skinned, silver-haired celestines and prisons that hold criminals for years. For the culture see../../04_Peoples_and_Cultures/Kurdansk_Culture.md. Peoples: celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common. Law: the city locks criminals up for years, and a Book 12 speaker asks about the operating costs of such places. Book 6: Emir tells Sophie she was born in Kurdansk; the team searches the city, and Marta Fries, a silver-rank celestine and friend of Melody Jain, escapes through a hidden panel Melody once used to fake her death, about two decades earlier. Book 9: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk about twenty-five years before; she and Sophie's father were both secret members of organisations, the Order of the Reaper among them.
160.name: Kurdansk

161.content: Leust is one of the largest and richest towns in the delta, with paved roads and stone buildings instead of mud brick. Jason stays there while investigating a fergax contract in the nearby lumber region. Industry: lumber; the land rights are heavily regulated, and the lumber region is one of the few places in the delta where lumber-worthy trees grow. Mill owners: Kyle Lindover, a leonid larger than Gary, owns the Lindover Lumber Mill and shut it after repeated fergax sightings; his family stays with her parents in Greenstone.
161.name: Leust

162.content: Two neighbouring lumber properties in the eastern delta, near Leust: Kyle Lindover's idle mill and the busy, ostentatious property of Eustace Clementson. In Book 1 a "fergax" sighting contract Jason takes turns out to be a land-grab staged by Thadwick Mercer, and the properties are where he finds the summoner behind it.
162.name: The Lindover and Clementson Properties

163.content: Oleyu is an unremarkable border city on a river, "pleasant, prosperous, and moderately sized", built on river trade with a mid-range level of magic. Position: Clive's route follows a river to "the border city of Oleyu", where the Rakesh Magic Society branch's area of influence ends. Standing: not as big or important as Rakesh or Vitesse, or unusual like Greenstone. Magic Society building: Clive lodges a protest here over his treatment by the Rakesh branch, without optimism.
163.name: Oleyu

164.content: Palisaros is a small laid-back town on the island of Arnote in the Storm Kingdom, arranged along a lagoon and the clifftop above it, where Jason settles his cloud house. Residents: mostly normals, irons and bronzes using cores, with a few silver and gold auras, and many caramel-skinned celestines. Pace: small-town, with none of the residents in a rush, calmer than busy Livaros. Mayor: Pelli, a member of the royal family but separate from them, living a relatively humble life as a core user. Guide: Argy shows visitors the saloon, eateries and market. Book 7: Jason meets Argy and Pelli in the town and settles there; during the surge only Jason and Pelli remain to defend it, and Jason leaves shortly after his team. Book 8: Vidal rides into the lagoon to find Wexler's team staying in a house by the waterfall.
164.name: Palisaros

165.content: Rakesh is a populous, caste-divided city on the north coast of the Africa-like continent, home of the Adventure Society's continental council and of the continent's largest Magic Society and Adventure Society strongholds. It is where the Magic Society holds Clive in all but name and where Danielle meets Carlivexistrix. Caste system: society is divided into castes, and the caste system justifies holding someone seen as lowly against their will; it dismisses Belinda as unimportant. Culture: busy but quiet streets, a local culture that values calm decorum, most people on foot or in animal-drawn carriages. The Magic Society branch: one of the most powerful on the continent; officials there have power and connections, so consequences come from the Adventure Society, not other branches. The campus prevents portals outside designated zones. The Adventure Society: the continental council sits here. Vitesse is also described as the seat of a continental council; the text reads most simply as one council per continent, with Rakesh serving the Africa-like continent and Vitesse the continent of Estercost, but it never states this.
165.name: Rakesh

166.content: Sadi Andali is "a little dirtball country", famously almost lawless, where slave markets sell unusual and restricted goods and the Adventure Society keeps no branch. It matters in Book 12 because the System's withdrawal from slave-holding regions turns attention on it. Law: "famous for being almost lawless"; the Adventure Society has no branch and only sends people in to sweep for illegal research and restricted essences, finding plenty of both. Slave trade: unusual products move through its slave markets; Ben asks whether destroying the Sadi Andali slave trade is Jason's price. Reach: events "all across Sadi Andali" are set against the great and noble houses of Cyrion. Book 12: Garret and Patterson wake in suppression collars in Sadi Andali; Garret's experience there may have knocked some sense into him, according to Percival.
166.name: Sadi Andali

167.content: Zartos is a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines, and the home of the diamond-rank smith Virid, Gary's mentor. It is named early as a celestine centre and appears on the page only when Gary and Virid reforge Jason's sword there. Peoples: "Zartos has a large celestine community"; the city is "largely populated by celestines". No ruler or institution is named in the lines checked. Book 1: Gary and Farrah mention Zartos on the road; Rufus has not been there, though his brother recommended it. Book 7: after Jason's death the team waits in Zartos while Gary and Virid examine and reforge Dread Salvation, a collaboration that Jason's soul-bond guides; the sword returns as Hegemon's Will.
167.name: Zartos

168.content: The continent that Jason would call Africa holds Greenstone, where Books 1-3 are set. In the text it is separate from Eurasia (see the World Primer), is far more populous in the north than the south, and has its continental Adventure Society and Magic Society strongholds at Rakesh on the north coast. This file sets out the places the compendium already files here, from south to north.
168.name: The Africa-like Continent

169.content: Estercost is the kingdom whose capital Cyrion is the largest city in the world and whose Vitesse sits on the equivalent of the French Riviera. The text places it on the Europe-like continent and calls it the home of Greenstone's founders.
