It is the setting of most of Books 6 and 11 and the base of Remore Academy and the Burning Violet guild.
169.name: Estercost and Its Continent

170.content: The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, the Caribbean analogue, founded by Soramir Rimaros. Its best-known city, Rimaros, spans three public islands; its largest and most populous city is Jaitari. Beyond the islands lies Girlano, the cartel country along its southern border.
170.name: The Storm Kingdom's Islands

171.content: The Network's Lyon Operations Director, who imprisons Farrah in the dimensional fortress, rises to be the second "Mr East" and later follows Gerling. Operations Director of the Network's Lyon branch, working out of the black site; one of the secretive staff who knew of and worked in the dimensional fortress, and has been cultivating loyalists. He leaves the dimensional space by another aperture just before it is sealed, alone, with no EOA and no prisoner. In Book 5 he takes the seat of Mr East, speaking of "the previous Mr East" and of vetting his people. Mr North says his own minions were disappointing before Barbou came along. Anna says Barbou is not hers to give; Farrah says "Barbou belongs to me". Gerling hits him and demands help reaching the Saint-Étienne dimensional space. In the zone he is the only one not attacked by the soul attacks and Jason declines to take him. In 2038 Farrah recalls him as the man behind her incarceration and tells Anna to retire the "bad apple" excuse. Jason brought him out of the zone alive; Mr North asked for a quick death and Jason left the decision to Farrah, who describes disposing of bodies without denying what she did, so Anna concludes "Barbou isn't alive". In Book 6 Anna did not know his fate.
171.name: Adrien Barbou

172.content: Adris Dorgan is an elf crime lord of Old City, the last of the Big Three, who keeps his daughter Elspeth Arella's parentage secret and seeks legitimacy. By Book 12 he is the mayor of Old City and a happy man. Patient and measured: "Your mistake was your need to feel in control". Protective father: "A father's wish for his child to go further than he". Quietly threatening: "Don't forget who my daughter is". Content with legitimacy: "Once a powerful crime lord, he found that legitimacy sat very well with him". His aura senses are less trained than Thalia Mercer's. He keeps his word, chasing down materials Clive listed. By Book 6 Humphrey says "Adris Dorgan's goal is legitimacy". Last of the Big Three crime lords, later mayor of Old City. Jason: Jason tells him "Nothing will happen to your daughter from my people".
172.name: Adris Dorgan

173.content: Akari Asano is a silver-rank swordswoman of the Japanese Asano clan, daughter of its patriarch, who is sent to Asano Village in Book 5. She spars with Jason, rides with Kaito's helicopter team and chases through the slums alongside him. By Book 13 she carries a gold-rank sword forged for her by Valdis Volaire, her sparring partner for a decade. Reserved and formal: after joining the Network team, "her reserve that Jason had cracked open went back in place". Ritualist: she meditates on a mat with a stitched ritual circle, a monster core in her hands. Horror at Jason's methods: she watches leeches drain a monster and melt into blood in Jason's hand. Duty-minded: she tells her escort to inform her father of a change in plan. Essences sword, adept and magic, a master confluence; she carries a genuine chokuto and has a blinking teleport that leaves exploding after-images. Silver-rank speed and strength outstrip Dawn's, but Dawn's perfect positioning turns her hits into near misses. She and Jason started sparring evenly matched; she was a specialised swordswoman caught up in human fighting styles. By Book 13 she wears a rare gold-rank sword Valdis forged using other-world techniques. Her father is the silver-rank patriarch of the Asano clan, named Shiro like Ken and Hiro's older brother. Her grandmother claims her for a hug and wonders what Jason wants from them. Jason: sparring partner and relative.
173.name: Akari Asano

174.content: Allayeth is one of Yaresh's two diamond-rank elves, the more reclusive of the pair. She is Charist's rival and sometime partner, trains the all-female team Moon's Edge, and is the most powerful person in the room at Jason's Yaresh meetings. She comes to respect Jason's restraint. Playful but exact: she tries to put Jason at ease "with some playful teasing". Learns to read power: she realises that pushing Jason as hard as Charist advocated "could have greater repercussions". Unrepentant: she turns on the dead envoys without guilt. Understanding of burden: she nods at Jason's account of power and responsibility. Diamond rank, the most powerful at the meeting, in the front row. She moves in a blur to stand before Jason. She works with a silver priestess when they find an incongruity in the ruins. Resident of Yaresh; "the more reclusive Lady Allayeth". She raised Team Moon's Edge, the all-female team led by Miriam Vance. Charist: fellow diamond and rival; he looks like a child caught doing something stupid when they talk. Jason: she learns to respect his concessions. Team Moon's Edge: trained by her.
174.name: Allayeth

175.content: A gold-rank adventurer with a soul-damaged aura who teaches Jason aura and soul techniques and is lost to an orb in Cardinas. Trenchant asks whether anyone has worked with Amos Pensinata. Dawn names him as a gold-ranker whose experiences with soul trauma left him with a more capable aura than most; she has convinced him to travel with Jason to teach soul manipulation. Jason knows him by reputation as the man who defeated the same forces that had forced Jason to flee the underwater complex. Jason later learns from him how to combine auras into a single force and about controlling aspects of the soul in isolation, which helped him expand perception without a beacon-like aura. Clive turns on him at the Yaresh camp: "You were brought on to help Jason, not make things worse. But your baggage...". He debriefs a Rimaros team in Cardinas and is among the few able to resist the zone's corruption. In Book 11 he grows troubled, does not flee with the other gold-rankers but goes into the water orb, and Jason promises to try to get him back. His nephew is Orin Pensinata; he joins Jason's journey partly because Orin insisted on coming. Jason extracts him from his attempted "suicide-by-messenger" and the gold-rankers escape into Jason's soul realm. After the zone he takes Orin and the scout Rosa back to Rimaros.
175.name: Amos Pensinata

176.content: Amy Asano is Kaito's wife and Jason's childhood best friend from next door. She and Jason had a fraught romance that ended badly; in Book 4 she meets the changed Jason, in Book 5 she acts as village mayor, and in Book 13 she is a protective widow with two daughters. Steady and perceptive: her face is stricken as she catalogues the changes from the boy she remembered. Protective: she stands ahead of her daughters at the Book 13 meeting. Wary of Jason emotionally, not physically: she knows he is an emotional threat to her children. Amy has seen essences before; Book 4 marks her first time holding one. She is the village's "de facto mayor" and acts as mayor in the Book 5 evacuation. The girl next door and Jason's best friend; she had a crush on Kaito from early on. Her parents retired to Tasmania and sold her the house next door. The notes add that she is mayor of the Casselton Regional Council. Kaito: husband; widowed in Book 5. Jason: history "like London fog".
176.name: Amy Asano

177.content: Anisa Lasalle is a zealous elf priestess of Purity from the Lasalle family who guides Rufus's party in Book 1, is thrown out for killing a captive, and dies serving the Builder's cult alliance in Book 3. Cold, righteous and quick to anger, she treats mercy as weakness. Zealous: Rufus calls her "Zealous girl. Dangerously committed". Ruthless: Farrah says "Anisa killed him before he could get a word out". Defiant of correction: Gary tells her "You don't get a say in what we do anymore, Anisa... You're out". In the Book 3 fight she is "something of a perfect weapon against Jason's powers", able to protect herself and cleanse afflictions. A temporary addition to Rufus's party at the start of the books. After Purity is implicated in the cult she vanishes with the archbishop and much of the Lasalle family. Rufus and Farrah: former party leaders. Nicolas Hendren: her archbishop.
177.name: Anisa Lasalle

178.content: Anna Tilden is a Network director who first meets Jason on Earth in Book 4, becomes a member of its steering committee, serves as the Asano clan's UN liaison, and by Book 11 is Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations Office of Supernatural Affairs. She is Jason's most trusted political contact on Earth. Roles: Director of the Network's Sydney operation, a government-faceless "suit" who hunts magic events from a helicopter, addressed as "Director" by Ketevan Arziani; on the Steering Committee of old family Network members in Book 5; UN Liaison to the Asano clan in Book 6; Under-Secretary-General of the Office of Supernatural Affairs by Book 11, an ex-Network official who knew Jason with "trust and scared". Family: wife Susan; brother Terrance, the Network's media director. Habits: Nigel Thornton's team is most often contracted by her, and Nigel says he came to Rexion on her job. In Book 13 she sets up a meeting in Canberra for ambassadors and officials of the nations whose people were displaced; that she works with Boris Ket Lundi is from notes, Book 13.
178.name: Annabeth "Anna" Tilden

179.content: Arabelle Remore is Rufus's mother, a gold-rank member of the Church of the Healer who specialises in mental health and trauma recovery. She helps Jason recover from captivity, drains life from enemies in battle, and keeps a firm hand on her son, her old teammate Callum and Jason's team. Wry and perceptive: she tells a bureaucrat she can only assume he is eager to step through a portal, in a pointed tone that Allayeth enjoys. Firm: "The amusement passed from Arabelle's face and the flint in the tone of her next words arrested his attention". Cares for her patients: she helps Jason explore traumatic memories and teaches him how to recover. Family-minded: "I think it's time for another child, husband. A daughter, this time". Healer and therapist: a member of the Church of the Healer specialising in mental health and trauma recovery. Life drain: she moves "through like a breeze, the enemies she touched with her hand collapsing to withered husks", each death leaving an urn of life force to fuel her other powers. In Book 10 she drains the magic from the undead, leaving them inert. Medical advice: she and Carlos conclude Jason should use his mana as much as he can tolerate. Administration: she organises procurement lists in the cloud palace's offices. Old team: she, her husband Gabriel, Callum Morse and Emir were a team. Never sent deep: as a valuable healer she was never sent deeper into the city than the surface during the Book 7 crisis.
179.name: Arabelle Remore

180.content: Argy (Emmett Dillivan) is a fruit grower in Palisaros who takes Jason, Rufus and Farrah into town and to the mayor, Pelli. Easygoing and proud of his town, he treats visitors as guests. Laconic: Jason "happily fell into Argy's laconic pace". Hospitable: he greets everyone he passes in the sealed streets. Friendly nickname: "Emmett Dillivan, but folks just call me Argy". Not an essence user in the lines read; his family has grown the fruit "longer than most can remember". Named for the fruit he is eating, which looks like a large tangerine. Pelli: local mayor; he says "You'll want to talk to Pelli". Jason: calls Palisaros "a genuine paradise".
180.name: Argy

181.content: Asya Karadeniz is a school friend of Jason's from the Mid North Coast who works in Network magitech administration. She joins Jason's side in Book 4, crews Kaito's helicopter with Greg, enters Jason's spirit vault as their relationship deepens, and dies in the Berlin attack in Book 5. Her family stays in the Asano clan afterwards. Dry about herself: "I was always fancy". Modest about her job: "I'm just an administrator there... My job is to keep the people doing the actual work happy and funded". Deliberate in contact: she asked for the Sydney slot because she went to school with Jason. Shaken by the gap between boy and man: the recording of Jason's power unnerved her, set against "the boy she had known" with his "sexy, impish grin". An executive-level Network administrator given an essence to reach category one, without monster cores. She operates the helicopter's weapons when a winged lizard enters her sights. Went to school with Jason and Greg. Her mother Rabia sits on the Asano Village committee for the non-Asano families and helps introduce the village to magic. Her cousin is Lina Karadeniz, who is also Emi's friend. Jason: old school friend; she enters his spirit vault "as her relationship with Jason deepened". Greg and Kaito: teammates. Anna: "The bastards killed Asya". Rabia and the Karadeniz family: mother and relatives.
181.name: Asya Karadeniz

182.content: Audrey Blaine is a Network committee member ("Mrs South") who survives a failed secret programme in a cloned body and later directs the Asano clan's energy-vampire research. Dry, practical and unsentimental, she has lived with the consequences of her own research. Pressed by colleagues: Mr North and Mrs West press her to go along with them. Composed about her condition: Jason says she has learned to manage the state left by her old programme. She is the clan's energy-vampire research director. She woke in a body that had been in stasis for more than a dozen years, the last remnant of a secret programme whose progenitors she had killed. She ran a sketchy joint programme between the magical factions decades ago and has lived in a magic city for a decade among vampires. Mr North: former committee colleague. Jason: brings her down to meet Team Biscuit and vouches for her.
182.name: Audrey Blaine

183.content: Liara Rimaros's husband and their three silver-rank children. Baseph is Liara's husband, silver rank, met leaving her townhouse. In Book 8 he hammers a pipe to draw raiders, fears what lies below because it is people who died because of what he did and is saved by Jason. He holds Liara's hand under the table. Dara is the eldest, a one-star adventurer happy to hunt monsters, with Liara's height and Baseph's dark copper hair and eyes, a muscular frontline combatant. Zareen is the middle child, physically smaller, with the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes, a politics enthusiast close to Vesper and a three-star adventurer. Joseph is the youngest and only son, an administrative official with the Amouz family business interests like his father; he wants to meet the man who saved his father. Dara's later remark about "the one from up north" with the elf twins refers to Rick.
183.name: Baseph, Dara, Zareen and Joseph

184.content: Beaufort is the gold-rank elf who leads the Cult of the Builder's forces in Cardinas, an uneasy ally of the brighthearts and then of Jason's expedition. He gave up his essence powers for a star seed and a war form of metal, and his loyalty to the Builder is tested when Jason removes the star seeds in Book 11. He shares his name with Thadwick Mercer's father (Beaufort Mercer) but is not him. Who he is: "the head of the Cult of the Builder's forces and their uneasy ally"; the gold-ranker "had given up his essence powers and was some manner of semi-artificial" being. War form: his body contains too much metal for his elven frame; when not in war form most of it sits in a dimensional space created by his star seed. He would stay in his fifteen-foot metal skeleton war form if diplomacy allowed. He has two extra arms, longer than his legs, wielding magically enhanced weapons swapped through his internal portal. His view of himself: his true form is "so much more perfect than his old elf body, which now served as little more than a disguise". Alliance: "Come now, Lorenn. The choice may be hard, but the calculation is easy"; he urges the brighthearts to abandon the cult's uneasy alliance if they must. They keep it. Jason: he calls Jason "the Defier", "perhaps, the greatest enemy of my Lord Builder on this planet".
184.name: Beaufort (Builder Cult Commander)

185.content: Belinda "Lindy" Callahan is Sophie's oldest friend, a thief from Greenstone's Old City who becomes Clive's assistant and, in time, the team's planner, infiltrator and master of shapeshifting. Essences: Magic, Trap and Adept, which she traded for in Book 2, producing the Charlatan confluence. Abilities: Echo Spirit is her first charlatan ability; Bait and Switch, Rune Trap, Force Tether, Lightning Tether and Pit of the Reaper; shapeshifting. Disguises: she infiltrates the Order of Redeeming Light as "Keth Gino" and, in the jungle territory of the transformation zone, passes as the silver messenger "Relia Vin Vala". Aura disguise: her power gives her an edge in learning aura disguises, which she teaches Jason. Storage: a personal storage space that even the Magic Society cannot peek into "without killing her first". Familiars: Shimmer, a summoned astral lantern, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.
185.name: Belinda Callahan

186.content: Benella is a servant of the messengers who works as Zolit's aide, brings Jason to the messengers' attention and is given one chance to prove herself valuable. Careful, watchful and afraid, she hides what she thinks behind a servant's neutrality. Neutral by necessity: she is relieved but not fool enough to thank the messenger, as showing that his consideration mattered would get her punished. Self-possessed: "Benella," she corrected with an annoyed shake of her head. Uncertain under scrutiny: she is unsure why Kaal is interested in her thought process. Not an essence user in the lines read; she is Zolit's aide, silent until the priest leaves. Her master is Fal Vin Garath; he scolds her and demands she explain the servant races' different way. Fal Vin Garath: her abusive master. Jes Fin Kaal: the Voice she presents to. Zolit: the fighter she aids.
186.name: Benella

187.content: Beth Cavendish is a bronze-rank Greenstone adventurer and water healer who leads a team in the Ustei campaign and the City of Fallen Echoes. Competent and brisk, she gives orders without ceremony. Brisk: "We're going to move on the sand barge". Encouraging: "Welcome to the path to bronze rank". Compared with Cassandra's brother: Cassandra says the way Jason describes his brother reminds her of Beth. Water healer; Jason envies her affliction-blanketing powers. Struck down by the thorn fountain's retributive damage in the Fallen Echoes fight. Introduces herself to Jason at the Adventure Society as Beth Cavendish, meeting her cousin Mose. The Cavendish family names a Greenstone district. Hudson, Niko, Emily, Mose: team members.
187.name: Beth Cavendish

188.content: Boris Ket Lundi, who goes by Boris Ketland on Earth, is a messenger from Earth who is secretly one of the Unorthodoxy. He appears in Book 10, helps Jason's alliance in Cardinas, takes Rufus and Taika to Earth in Book 11, and is a leader of the Cabal in Book 13. A messenger with no indoctrination, from Earth, who says "I'm from Earth, Asano" and that he has been on Earth "for a lot longer than you"; the television detail is from notes, Book 10. Unorthodoxy messengers hid on Earth since before hominids; Earth was chosen because of the Builder sanction scandal; the Council of Kings avoids it. He is Unorthodoxy secretly, serving under Vesta Carmis Zell, who hired him for his elemental powers; what she knows of astral kings outside the Council is from notes, Book 11. The Cabal's "angelic founders" were messengers, and a database lists Boris Ketland as a Cabal executive; that he is a founder is from notes, Book 10. In Book 13 he contemplates events from the Cabal's main headquarters in what was the Democratic Republic of the Congo. He worked with the founder's familiar to betray the Network's founder to the early societies. Messengers can hide their wings and shrink their size; Boris has long been comfortable with human proportions and once spent several millennia as a celestine research assistant.
188.name: Boris Ket Lundi (Boris Ketland)

189.content: A gold-rank stealth assassin, former teammate of Emir and of Rufus's parents, whose long hunt for Sophie's mother Melody Jain drives his later scenes. Introduced by Emir as a gold-ranker who, if he does not want to be seen, cannot be seen by anyone short of diamond rank. Described as "the gold-ranked assassination specialist" and the group's best scout; his attacks on a gold-rank priest land strongly but do not kill at once. He, Gabriel and Arabelle Remore have been companions for decades. Emir, Arabelle, Gabriel and Callum were an old team. An avid monster-hunter, he is one of the few gold-rankers who obsessively raise their strength. He stops Sophie and Humphrey from running off after the Order of the Reaper: "I'm stopping you until you are ready. Hate me if you like", and explains the order split from the cult and became self-serving assassins. His fixation on Melody Jain, Sophie's mother, is because he is connected to her: she kept him as her only real connection to the order; he lost track of her and has searched ever since. Jason avoids his petitions to see Melody, and finds his aura dangerously unstable even after things are in the open. In Book 13 he conjures rats to track a creature through a pipe.
189.name: Callum Morse

190.content: Carlos Quilido is a gold-rank priest of the Healer and the world's leading specialist in soul damage, star seeds and aura conditions. He helps Jason recover from the Builder's attack, leads a healing team, studies Purity's Flames of Redemption on Melody Jain, and later develops the Quilido Procedure that removes monster-core taint. Priest first: "First and foremost, though I am a priest of the Healer. Before anything else, I'm here to help you, not for you to help me". Uneasy at society events: Arabelle plays guide to "Carlos, a priest of the Healer who was not comfortable at fancy social events". Dogged: he once harangued Jason to be an experimental subject when Jason had barely woken from a coma, and Jason threw him across the room with his aura; Carlos backing down since is called "considerable progress". Protective of patients: in a lab coat and a glare he looks "like a doctor shooing people away from his harried patient". Specialty: "Finding and dealing with soul influences is his specialty; he's at the top of his field. From star seeds to vampirism to plain soul trauma, he's the best there is". Star seeds: the Healer's church took over extracting star seeds from Purity: "we, the church of the Healer, have taken over that task"; he warns that extraction can be lethal without continuous healing. Rituals: gold-rank soul-projection ritual lamps and circles.
190.name: Carlos Quilido

191.content: Cassandra Mercer is Thalia's daughter and Thadwick's older sister, an adventurer who becomes Jason's first romance on Pallimustus, ends it when her family wants a reliable match, and reunites with the changed Jason in Book 12. She leads her own team in Greenstone. Sweet and sharp: she investigates Jason's background and kisses him back forcefully. Drawn to rescue: she thinks of a hot shower after bog monsters. Bound by family: Neil explains that she dumped Jason "not because she wanted to, but because her family decided he wasn't going to amount to anything". Bronze rank with a hidden aura in Book 1; by Book 12 her team fights silver-rank bog monsters. Thalia oversaw her training personally. Four years older than Neil, who had a crush on her. Her brother tried to kill Jason. Jason: first romance, ended by her family. Thalia and Thadwick: mother and brother.
191.name: Cassandra Mercer

192.content: Charist is one of Yaresh's two resident diamond-rank elves, the more social of the pair, who dislikes the responsibilities of his power. He is Allayeth's rival and partner in Jason's Yaresh diplomacy and pushes the harder line against Jason. Sociable: "Lord Charist was the more social of the two". Courtly: "Your father is known to me. Convey my regards". Reluctant: he "dislikes many of the responsibilities that come with his level of power". Sheepish: he looks like a child caught doing something stupid when Allayeth calls out his approach. Diamond-rank; no silver-ranker can open a portal that diamond-rankers can use. He eavesdrops on Jason and Allayeth's talks. Resident of Yaresh; he and Allayeth stay in the city because its people love Hana Shavar. Jason: opposed then wary; Jason tells Allayeth "you know your friend Charist is listening".
192.name: Charist

193.content: Cheryl Asano is Jason's mother, from a large Australian farming and mining family. She is the one in the family fascinated with Japan, a strong-willed realtor who shows up in Book 4 stunned at her dead son's return. Strong-willed: she flashes "a well-recognised look of dissatisfaction" at Jason's poke but calms herself. Stern: Jason jokes "Mum is quite stern". Grieving: she looks at Jason "like she'd seen a ghost" and hugs him tightly once she steels her nerve. Overworked: she hasn't been into the office in two days, unlike her. She is "the pre-eminent upscale realtor in the Greater Casselton area". She is non-essence in the lines read; portal travel sickens her. Her family are "miners and farmers, tracing their bloodline back through bushrangers, convicts, and indigenous Australians"; she was the one fascinated with Japan. Her brother is Robert; her mother makes a miraculous recovery. Jason is told his parents divorced a year ago and that his mother moved to Castle Reach. Erika and Kaito: other children. Amy: puts a restraining hand on Cheryl's arm.
193.name: Cheryl Asano

194.content: Chloe Baudrillard is a French epidemiologist with Doctors Without Borders whom Jason befriends in Book 5 while healing patients in a quarantine tent. She is later sheltered by the Asano clan with her family and works on magical healing. Wry: "My biggest enemy beat me out for the good parking space at the hospital where I used to work". Awed but steady: she watches Jason calm the ward "in disbelief". Friendly: Jason calls her "a good egg". A medical scientist, not an essence user in the lines read; by Book 13 she works with healers on magical healing. French; a Doctors Without Borders epidemiologist. In Book 11 she and her family are displaced by the vampire occupation and taken in by the clan. Ian: works with him on healing. Vincent Baudrillard: same family.
194.name: Chloe Baudrillard

195.content: Clarissa Ventress is one of the crime lords of Old City and holds Sophie's indenture. She uses Sophie to provoke the rash Cole Silva and learns what Lucian Lamprey wants in order to control him. Calculating: "The key to controlling a person was finding what they wanted". Amused: she is "happily imagining the look on Silva's face" as she watches Sophie's match. Irritated by independence: she is less happy with Sophie's friend Belinda. Rank is not stated in the lines read; she travels with a huge leonid bodyguard. Lives in a sprawling manor in Old City's canal district, which has its own internal city wall. Her arrangement with Sophie: Sophie would help her provoke Silva into the kind of rash action his father would have prevented. Sophie: indentured servant. Cole Silva: rival, newest of the Big Three. Lucian Lamprey: someone she plans to control.
195.name: Clarissa Ventress

196.content: Clive Standish is a tall, lanky Magic Society researcher in Greenstone, raised on an eel farm, who becomes Jason's team's ritualist and astral-magic scholar. He explains the cosmos to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup, identifies the Reaper-trial astral space as a Builder vessel, and builds the open-access Magical Research Association. A lecturer who loses the thread and apologises; he wants dumpling soup in the middle of his own lecture on the cosmos. He says he venerates, not worships, the Celestial Book: "There's a difference"; an archbishop asks "You admit to being a heretic?" and Clive answers that he "could be considered a heretic". He jokes about his background: "I'm the son of eel farmers". A stranger accuses him of sleeping with a wife he says he does not have, which becomes a running gag. Essences: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. A rune essence came to him as "an epic four-star essence". Abilities: Wrath of the Magister, a rune circle that triggers effects when attacked, the damage-reflecting buff Mantle of Retribution and the zone ability Eye of Karma; Mana Equilibrium. Racial gift: a blessing from the Celestial Book changed his human Special Attack Affinity into a spell affinity. Familiar: Onslow, a rune tortoise who sits at the prow of the airboat, carries Clive, and becomes a runic tattoo on his torso when called back. Ritual and astral magic: he leads the team's rituals and bridge research.
196.name: Clive Standish

197.content: Cole Silva is the newest of Old City's Big Three crime lords, who inherits his father's operation and, with Lucian Lamprey, orchestrates Jason's kidnapping and star seed implantation. Arrested in Book 3, his organisation falls into chaos. Rash: Clarissa plans to provoke him "into the kind of rash action that his father always kept him from making". Predatory: his father's protection of Sophie is gone and he watches her match from a viewing box. His father had a small operation catering to nobles with low tastes, with the money and connections to arrange expensive cleansings. The father died in his sleep "a couple of months ago"; the son stepped up. Cole's father killed a man who tried to rob him. Clarissa Ventress: rival crime lord. Lucian Lamprey: partner in the kidnapping.
197.name: Cole Silva

198.content: Constance is Emir Bahadir's chief of staff and later his wife. She runs his cloud palace and treasure-hunting organisation, steadies Jason's social events, and leaves to train under Callum Morse until she reaches gold rank. From Book 6 she is a gold-ranker and a fixture of Emir's team. Steadying: she subtly indicates which guests will not respond well to Jason's social graces. Detail-oriented: "the detail-oriented half of the pairing, which sometimes made her closer to a babysitter than she would admit to liking". Dry and firm with Emir: she gives her husband "a stern look"; Jason checks with her rather than him. Pragmatic: "What we missed doesn't matter. What we do now does". Silver rank in Book 2; she holds off three enemies in the island battle, one the construct that killed Farrah. Gold rank by Book 9, only for a couple of years when Jason hides his aura from her. She is part of the reformed gold-rank team for the Cardinas mission. Emir's chief of staff, "the object of his affections"; she took leave and went with Callum Morse, intending not to return until she reached gold rank. Emir and Constance had moved around each other for years with a power imbalance between employer and employee, gold and silver. Emir: employer, then husband; "Emir's wife" and chief of staff. Callum: her trainer, who puts a calming hand on her arm. Sophie and Humphrey: she warns Humphrey she will tell his mother.
198.name: Constance

199.content: Craig Vermillion is a vampire of seventy years' standing and the Cabal's front man in Sydney. He explains the magical world to Jason, becomes his friend and political counsel, and rises to gold rank by feeding on risen vampire lords in the war against them. He plays up the mysterious vampire act only for the "normals". Casual behind the mystique: "Craig is fine when I'm not on the job. I have to play it sinister and mysterious around the normals". Helpful: Jason thanks him for the information. Wry: "I say roll with it... You built this place for melodrama, right?". Troubled: he worries about the sane vampires' future. Vampire for seventy years; every aura in the room trembles at the name Vermillion. By Book 12 he has accelerated to gold rank by feeding on several risen vampire lords, though he lacked the power to defeat a lord himself. Jason developed his blend-into-crowds technique by studying Craig's aura. The Cabal's Sydney front man. Explains the magical world's three dominant forces and that a new magic appeared five centuries ago. Hiro: Jason asks him to fetch Hiro. Susan: "Craig Vermillion was always so nice".
199.name: Craig Vermillion

200.content: Cressida Vane is the matriarch of the blood-cult family that holds Jason and his friends in Book 1. Beautiful, haughty and weary of her family's ambitions, she insists they are "a nice, traditional blood cult family" and she is killed in the confrontation. Haughty: "I am Lady Cressida Vane"; Jason mocks her high-priestess name. Traditional: "This is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way". Dismissive of her husband: "I don't care what my stupid husband thinks; he married into the family". Leader of the blood cult family's rituals. Complained that astral beings were "the death" of her son. Mother of Landemere Vane; she asks what Landemere was trying to summon. Darryl: the high priest beside her.
200.name: Cressida Vane

201.content: Danielle Geller is Humphrey's mother and the head of the Geller family's household in Greenstone. She is a silver-ranker at the start of the series who looks much younger than she is, later a gold-ranker with dimension and time powers, and Jason's political adviser on Earth. Time: a time confluence, with only forward time travel possible; in Book 3 she outpaces Lucian Lamprey in a fight, teleporting behind him and cutting his neck. She is called "Time Witch of Vitesse". Dimension: a dimension essence, as Emir says, with gold rank from the notes; she teleports behind Lamprey in a fight. Estate and training: the Geller estate's mirage chamber can run at bronze rank only "for limited periods" because Greenstone's magic is low, and at iron rank Danielle offers it to Rufus; a family member from the generation that first settled the region may still be alive. The diamond-rank ancestor in the earlier notes was not found. Rank: silver in Book 1, gold by Book 7.
201.name: Danielle Geller

202.content: Dawn is the World-Phoenix's First Servant, the head of its cult and its primary vessel. She guides Jason through Books 4-8 as a mentor and agent: she paints, takes avatar bodies, reveals the invasion plan, negotiates with the Builder and brings Jason's friends to Rimaros. Role: First Servant of the World-Phoenix, head of its cult and the primary vessel of the great astral being. Diamond-rank vessels of great astral beings can withstand the strain and keep their selves, and former vessels end up as peak existences. One intervention: the Hierophant is allowed to intervene in Pallimustus a single time; in Book 7 she says she will use one full-power intervention, and she destroys a Builder rolling city with a phoenix. Art: the paintings by "Dawn" that Jason buys show two planets with four pillars and "The Invasion of Pallimustus". Home: Interstice, the city-universe at the cosmos's centre.
202.name: Dawn

203.content: Durrum is a massive earth-aspect brightheart, one of two leaders who claim territory in Jason's unified battlefield. Conservative and plain-spoken, he leads his followers from the front, chooses to trust Neil's plan, and ends up the leader of the brightheart territories after Lorus is ruled out. Leader from the front: his messengers "had inherited the toughness of the massive brightheart Durrum, who led them from the front"; Lorus pushes aggressively while Durrum is "more conservative". Origins of his territory: he and Lorus arrived after claiming other territories and looking to expand; their standoff lasted so long that the Undeath priests and the Builder cult forced the issue. Anti-cult but practical: he "hated the Builder cult as much as every other brightheart, yet had been willing to abide by their alliance" and tries to reconcile the cult and the brighthearts. In battle: his earth powers leave him unobstructed by mud, strong enough to hurl enemy messengers and undead aside as he fights his way to Lorus. Confronting Lorus: "LORUS! Are you betraying us?" and "Every second we spend arguing or fighting the cultists takes us closer to defeat. You're killing us". He warns Lorus not to give a lightning-wielding Neil a reason to make him the demonstration. Wall and talks: his protective wall, with Dustin's, keeps the cultists from attacking the brighthearts on sight so that all sides agree to talk.
203.name: Durrum

204.content: An ice-armoured defender from the Kettering family who starts as one of Thadwick Mercer's offsiders, joins Rick's team in Book 2 and later fights beside Neil in Cardinas. One of Thadwick Mercer's two offsiders with Neil: he protects the group with his powers while Neil heals them. The Davone and Kettering families have close ties to the Mercers, which is how the boys came to Thadwick's side. He and Neil are relieved to be free, having been known as Thadwick's flunkeys. A local who fills Jonah Geller's defender role on Rick's team: "a classic defender, not very mobile but very hard to go around or through", clad in armour forged entirely of ice. His cousin Hudson Kettering is his counterpart on Beth Cavendish's team. In Book 7 he is a friend of Neil's from their time on Thadwick's team; by Book 9 he is the only non-local on Rick's team, picked up after Jonah's death. In Book 11 he is dropped into the same territory as Neil, gives the party a frontline and healer pairing and helps hold a protective wall between brighthearts and Builder cultists.
204.name: Dustin Kettering

205.content: Elizabeth is the gold-rank leader of the vampires who take Europe, a blood-ritual specialist who establishes a détente with the world and later trades with Jason's side. She is tired of being asked whether she is Elizabeth Báthory. Dangerous when asked her name: those around her stopped asking if she was Báthory once she started "immediately eating anyone who did". Pragmatic: her edicts about treating humans better were not compassion; they bought sustainability. Primus inter pares: Jason says "You clearly have primacy amongst them" about the other vampires. A gold-ranker and "a master of luring groups into traps set out using blood rituals". She and Mr North pair their ritual magics for defence; her five ritual circles send out red tentacles that extend and snake round corners to squeeze the vorger. Humanity tried to kill her with a nuclear device flooding Rome with magical sunlight, modified from a design Travis made for Jason. Under her, the vampires establish a détente: every major city still hides vampires, and bombings in Europe are answered by assassinations in Beijing, Washington, Moscow and London. She rests in a vault in Venice that was once a bank. Mr North: ally in ritual defence. Jason: he asks her to settle the other vampires, acknowledging her primacy.
205.name: Elizabeth

206.content: Elspeth Arella is the elf director of the Greenstone branch of the Adventure Society and the secret daughter of Old City crime lord Dorgan. A failed expedition and its investigation undo her career, trapping her in a post meant as a stepping stone. Twenty years later she is still there to receive Jason's return. Controlling: Dorgan tells her "Your mistake was your need to feel in control". Wary of Jason: she asks "What is it you want in return for silence?". Resentful: "she felt trapped" while her father felt elevated. Unwilling to forget: she recalls lifting "some jumped up iron-ranker by the throat" on the spot where he returns. She can lift a person by the throat with her powers. She is flanked by her deputy, Genevieve. Director of the Greenstone branch. Raised in secret by her mother, with clandestine visits to her father Dorgan. Her backroom dealings and her status as "daughter of an Old City crime lord" were dragged into the light after the disastrous expedition. Her father rose from last of the Big Three crime lords to legitimate mayor of Old City. Jason: antagonist turned polite acquaintance. Lucian Lamprey: the power she bargained with.
206.name: Elspeth Arella

207.content: Emi Evans-Asano is Jason's niece, the daughter of Erika and Ian Evans, whom Jason calls "Moppet". She is twelve when he comes home in Book 4 and learns the truth about magic from him. She trains in ritual magic under Farrah, decides at thirteen that she does not want to fight as he does, and takes her essences at about sixteen under Rufus. By Book 13 she is an upper-silver ritualist and researcher, and Vincent Baudrillard's partner. The System names her as the contact "Emi Evans-Asano" when Jason returns, and he senses her aura with Erika's and Ian's. Her father says she has always been hard to parent: "You thought you were smarter than me by age seven, and by age nine, you were right.". Jason's remark on her at twelve is "twelve going on forty". Erika says Emi took his death hard and that Erika's own conspiracy-theory phase did not help. Her cousins are Hana and Jace, Kaito and Amy's daughters; her great-grandmother Yumi is "Nana Yumi" to her. By Book 11 she is described as "the princess of the Asano clan". At twelve she stands up to a group of boys picking on another student at Jason's old school, which Jason watches through Shade.
207.name: Emi Evans-Asano

208.content: Emir Bahadir is a gold-rank treasure hunter, patron of the Reaper contest and owner of a cloud ship and palace that becomes Jason's team's base. Elegant, ageless and wanderlustful, he has hunted the remnants of the Order of the Reaper for years, uses his wealth and staff for large schemes, and marries his chief of staff, Constance. Likes grand entrances: "I'm hosting a grand event. It requires grandeur". He announces a competition and a grand-prize cloud palace in a speech that throws the crowd into turmoil. Warm and wry: he tells Rufus "Comrades behind her, enemies in front of her and friends beside her" of Farrah's apparent death and sighs "world-weary" when Jason storms off. Cautious in accusation: "Making that kind of accusation against a church is no small matter and even I'm not completely convinced yet". Not used to being the responsible one: that is Constance's job, but he is the older and higher-ranked man. Essences: he has "staff, might, magic and mystic". Cloud ship and palace: a cloud ship the size of an ocean liner that morphs into a palace. His preferred design is a five-towered castle. Staff and speed: he conjures copies of his staff under every construct, smashing the iron and bronze ones and tossing the silvers and catches Danielle before she can lunge. Aura mastery: he can block the senses of others, normally taught only to gold-rankers.
208.name: Emir Bahadir

209.content: Erigo Fin Desca is the Builder's new prime vessel, a former messenger of the Unorthodoxy heavily modified by the Builder after Shako was taken by the Sundered Throne. Insistent on names: "His name is the Builder... He is not one of our kind anymore". Corrects titles: he corrects Jamis's usage of the Builder's name. Supervisory: he warns that the planet goes nowhere unless civility is kept. Prime vessel of the Builder; the avatars gather around him on the dimensional ship. Originally a messenger of the Unorthodoxy, he says he has moved on from it. Became prime vessel after the Sundered Throne took Shako. Jamis Fran Muskar: an astral king whose avatar he corrects. The Builder: the god he serves.
209.name: Erigo Fin Desca

210.content: Erika Asano is Jason's older sister, a television presenter living in Melbourne, married to Ian Evans, mother of Emi. Sharp-tongued, loving and protective, she is the family member who reels in Jason's impulsiveness, mourns Kaito, and argues with the clan over her daughter's safety. Strict-rules household: she and Jason "had grown up with their mother's strict rules about not bringing conflict to the dinner table". Protective and blunt: she storms into her daughter's bedroom when Jason, Emi and Taika are playing a rhythm game. A professional: "being the experienced media personality, she had attached herself to the tour" of the hospital, wanting to "reel in her brother's impulsive nature". Frank about fear: "I'm her mother and I don't like her going out and risking her life. Is that so hard to understand?". By Book 11 she is the food logistics director for the whole clan. She wants Emi to use monster cores like her parents, and Emi's refusal sours their relationship. She lives in Melbourne with Ian and Emi; her series films in Melbourne and she misses "her big parties in Melbourne" after moving north. She is Jason's elder sister, with Kaito among her brothers. Ian Evans: her husband, a doctor. Emi: her daughter, whom she tries to keep from combat. Jason: "Erika clinging to him like she was afraid he'd disappear again"; she shares his look when he wants a topic changed. Kaito: she mourns him with Emi.
210.name: Erika Asano

211.content: Estella Warnock is a Livaros spy and urban scout with fourfold senses who works for Jason's team and later marries Belinda. Cautious and observant, she prefers not to be noticed. Hard to surprise, prefers anonymity: she tells a contact she says of someone "I don't think he knows who I am and I'd rather keep it that way". Nervous in waiting: she fails to concentrate on a book on a rooftop while a monster manifestation is expected. Fourfold senses: Jason says they make her "even better than I am" at spotting messenger agents; she maps messenger agents in the city. She "made a career out of being a spy and urban scout in Livaros" and knows the island's streets, alleys and rooftops.
211.name: Estella Warnock

212.content: Fal Vin Garath is a silver-rank messenger master who is abusive but within the bounds his peers accept. He detests acting at the behest of Jes Fin Kaal and launches a soul attack on Jason in Book 9. Imperious: he scowls at Benella and demands answers in a voice "like a command from the heavens". Resentful of command: he "detested being forced to act at the behest of the Voice of the Will" and sneers at his commander, astral king's Voice and Asano. Silver rank; he launches a soul attack on Jason through his connection to Shade and is surprised when Jason fends it off and retaliates. He seizes Shade and squeezes while Shade drains his mana, until Shade's body is destroyed. Benella's master, "abusive but not outside the bounds of acceptability to his fellow messengers", free to treat the servant races as he pleased so long as it did not impinge on other messengers. Jes Fin Kaal: his commander. Hess Jor Nasala: sits with him at Kaal's meeting.
212.name: Fal Vin Garath

key: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
213.comment: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
213.content: A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning. Jason has three, each very different, and Humphrey has one.
keys: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
213.name: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash

214.content: Farrah Hurin (also spelt Huren) is a small, pale, strawberry-blonde ritual magician from Vitesse. She is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, teaches him aura control, perception and meditation, and treats him as an equal. She dies in Book 1, is brought back by the Reaper, and reappears on Earth in Book 4. Essences: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence; she explains this herself in Book 1. Abilities: lava cannon, a magma golem, lava streams and fire orbs, obsidian domes, shards and columns, and obsidian armour. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and builds the infrastructure of Asano Village and the Grid repairs. Aura teaching: perception and memory games, meditation and aura control. Rank: silver in Book 4 or 5; in Book 12 she is offered the choice of becoming a Voice of the Will or a Defier of the Will; she accepts and becomes the Defier, immortal and "still a step or two from gold".
214.name: Farrah Hurin

215.content: Gabriel Remore is Rufus's father, a gold-rank fire-and-sword adventurer and academy teacher who reforms his old team with Emir and Arabelle when Jason needs gold-rankers in Book 10. Brisk and capable, he fights beside his wife and trusts his son's friends once they have earned it. Wry: "I'm her husband!" and "Is it just me, or is this messenger a little bit odd?". Practical about interrogation: "it's not easy to get a gold-ranker to talk. We can all hold up to a lot of pain". Deflates when his son is surly: "That's fine!... Understood, son". Wary of suspicious allies: "If the messengers have people that can go down there... what do they need us for?". Gold rank with fire powers; his ash cloud carries him and Arabelle and his sword glows yellow-white like molten steel. He flies a flame-trailing airship down from the sky. Aura control is among the best Jason had sensed at gold rank. Old team: Emir, Gabriel, Arabelle and Callum; they stopped adventuring while raising their son, and Gabriel started teaching at the academy. Danielle Geller investigates Jason at his request. Arabelle: wife, field partner. Emir, Callum: old teammates; Callum was swapped out.
215.name: Gabriel Remore

216.content: Gabrielle Pellin is an acolyte of Knowledge who begins as Humphrey's girlfriend, becomes a stern and strikingly beautiful priestess, and ends as Travis Noble's wife. She is often at odds with Jason and uneasy about his aura, but is devoted to her goddess and her husband. Stern and accusing: "Where did you learn to use your aura like a messenger?"; "You move like a messenger". Does not rise to bait: she glowers but doesn't answer teasing. Hostile to Jason: their dislike was a factor in ending her relationship with Humphrey. Quiet when separated from her goddess: she is still getting used to the absence of Knowledge. A silver-rank priestess of the Church of Knowledge. Jason's spirit domain cuts her off from her goddess, which makes her look like she bit a lemon. Introduces herself as "just an acolyte, not a full priestess". Humphrey's girlfriend, until he breaks up with her in Book 2. Knowledge assigns her to shadow Travis and later attach her to his and Farrah's project. Travis Noble: nervous around her at first; later her husband. Jason: mutual friction; Jason enjoys baiting her.
216.name: Gabrielle Pellin

217.content: Garth Larosse is the High Priest of Undeath, a nine-foot skeletal undead built from the skeletons of a dozen monsters, who leads the undead host against Jason in the Book 10 and 11 campaign. Cold and strategic: he leaves the mindless hordes clawing at the wall until defences break. Resentful of Death's interference: Death drives back the territory Undeath claimed. Cautious in command: he directs his undead "with care and subtlety" so failed commands hide his purpose. Higher-order undead leader; priests of Undeath range from ordinary essence users to undead mockeries, including vampires commanding ghoul armies and liches. He designates a priest to control the avatar while he handles Asano. Leader of the priests of Undeath; most who knew his nature are already slain and turned into his puppets or parts of his body. Jason: his opponent, who answers him flippantly.
217.name: Garth Larosse

218.content: Gareth "Gary" Xandier is an enormous leonid smith and warrior from Vitesse. He makes Jason's first sword, Dread Salvation. In Book 10 he drinks the Cup of Heroes and becomes a demigod; in Book 11 he dies; in Book 12 a new leonid, Gary Sharpton, appears who carries his reincarnated soul. Summon: a foundry golem, a roughly three-metre black-iron figure with a molten mouth that drips molten metal. Equipment: conjured full-body dark-steel plate armour; the notes add a hammer and shield and the runes. Smithing: he forges Dread Salvation; he reforges it with his mentor Virid Martine as Hegemon's Will. Rank: bronze at the start; "almost silver" by Book 3; silver after using a core. Demigod: Hero's power makes him a demigod, "a vision of physical might, wreathed in divine power".
218.name: Gary (Gareth Xandier) and Gary Sharpton

219.content: Jack Gerling is a US Network category-four (gold-rank) essence user with an explosion-based power set, who kills Jason's brother, lover and best friend in Book 5, fights beside and against Jason in Book 6, becomes the vampire queen Elizabeth's blood slave, and is freed and turned by McKean into a nearly immortal agent. Jason kills him in Book 13. Gruff, bellowing and friendly to those who are kind to him: "You're alright, Cleary... My last handler would have thrown me the chicken like I was a monster in a pit. Most people are scared of me". Pugnacious: "I don't mind kicking their asses back and forth a little"; he is annoyed by being managed and "not entirely at peace" with joining Jason's push. Cynical about his handlers: category fours "were beholden to whoever could provide the coins to keep them alive", and a handler is easier to replace. Essences: might, potent and vast, producing the onslaught confluence; the potent essence is rare, the vast essence "so unheard of" the Network checked records hundreds of years old. He could down a plane and everyone in it with a snap. Explosion flight: periodic explosions throw him through the air faster than a helicopter. Explosive fist: a broad wave of force when he hits, "devastating" with an explosive fist power. Aura and recovery: he extends his aura to shield his men from Jason's suppression, and his gold-rank recovery closes wounds and purges poison fast.
219.name: Gerling (Jack Gerling)

220.content: Gilbert "Bert" Bertinelli is a Greenstone tailor who sells Jason his combat robe and later his suits. Courtly, theatrical and sharp about quality, he does not hide his rivalry with his brothers. Theatrical: he runs "Gilbert's Resilient Attire For the Discerning Gentleman" and invites customers to call him Bert. Competitive with his brothers: one of octuplets named after Berts, including the "handsome" Bertrand. Cloth essence abilities at bronze; he reached iron rank late. He makes the trap-weaver-silk and leather combat attire haggled by Gary and priced in bronze coins, unusual for iron-rank gear. Jason's combat robe is "custom made for him by Gilbert Bertinelli"; Gilbert supplied his armour. His brothers: he is "loath" to refer Jason to his brother.
220.name: Gilbert Bertinelli

221.content: Gormanston Bynes is a gold-rank elf, leader of Yaresh's Aristocratic Faction and head of its civic administration, who is outmanoeuvred by Marcus Xenoria and Jason. Proud, controlled and shrewd, he conceals contempt behind careful politeness. Proud and controlled: the faction's chief standard bearer and new lead representative of the Yaresh civic administration. Foresighted: he fears the elite's neglect of the foundations of their power and wanted a different crisis than the invasion he got. Ruthless: Allayeth says he hates weakness, squeezes value from enemies and would use or ally with Jason. Allayeth: "one of the most prominent members of a powerful political faction"; his son Calcifer is the man Jason sent running. His niece Juniper, twenty-two, reached silver during the surge. Allayeth: informant about him.
221.name: Gormanston Bynes

222.content: Greg is an old school friend of Jason's who joins the Network defectors on Kaito's helicopter crew and is killed in Book 5. His family is taken into Asano Village afterward. He is nerdy, self-deprecating and braver than he believed. Self-deprecating: he was "never much more than an adequate lawyer" and had been pushed out of his father's practice. Enjoys small comforts: he holds a mug of hot chocolate on a chalet balcony. Teased by Asya: "If all your friends are cool, what does that say about you?". Sensitive to portals: he fights portal sickness on Erika's floor. Bronze rank by Book 5; his body "could easily endure the cold". He crews Kaito's helicopter with Asya. School friend of Jason and Asya who roped Jason and Amy into hours-long board games. He says he had lived more in six months of magic than in six years before. Asya: friend and fellow crew member.
222.name: Greg

223.content: Gwydion Remore is Rufus's older brother and a priest of Hero. He is the family's softer edge: easygoing, card-playing and quietly devout. Easygoing: he brings Danielle a fresh drink at her table. Curious: "I'm looking forward to meeting this Asano". Family man: he worries about his family underground during the Cardinas expedition. Sheepish before his mother: Arabelle watches him with raised eyebrows. Priest of Hero; he tells Gary that Hero has decided to sanction himself. Danielle Geller: tablemate.
223.name: Gwydion Remore

224.content: Hana Shavar is the elf High Priestess of the Church of the Healer for Yaresh. She personally runs the camp for rescued refugees, oversees operations from Jason's cloud palace and goes with the gold-rank force to Cardinas. She is warm, devout and plain about danger. Hands-on: she personally takes charge when people start arriving rescued from towns across the southern region. Assessing and unimpressed: she runs "another assessing look over the infuriating man" and concludes the eyes are "the most honest thing in his appearance". Dissatisfied: she looks Jason up and down before going back downstairs. Quiet in a tense room: she is oddly quiet when Undeath priests are questioned. Gold rank: one of the remaining gold-rank participants with Amos and Carlos. She senses enemy forces massing near the city walls. "The High Priestess of the Healer for the city-state of Yaresh". Her operations gradually changed Jason's cloud palace from a triage hospital into a larger base. Jason: friction and respect. Arabelle: orders her to rest. Amos and Carlos: fellow gold-ranker members of the expedition.
224.name: Hana Shavar

225.content: Twin elf sisters on Rick Geller's team: Hannah the archer and Claire the healer. The elf twins Hannah and Claire Adeah are the archer and the team healer, with Claire the most important member to protect. Hannah's arrows pin trap weavers to trees; Claire cleanses afflictions and cuts a team mate from a web with her wand. In the Book 1 mock battle against Jason, Claire's body is left floating in the water after she focused her healing on the others, and they swear revenge. Claire resented Jason's tactics in the mock battle the most. By Book 10 Hannah is Rick's girlfriend and then fiancée; by Book 12 his wife. In Book 13 Claire Adeah is on the expedition with Arabelle and Sigrid and says the vampires have too much magic for the cure to be safe.
225.name: Hannah and Claire Adeah

226.content: Hassan Dukhtar is a Pakistani doctor praised for courageous medical work in a vampire war zone, whose name Jason turns into a running joke. Patient and earnest: he introduces himself as Hassan Dukhtar and keeps correcting Jason's mishearing. A doctor who did courageous medic work the week before in a vampire war zone, which saved many lives. Jason hears "Handsome Doctor" instead of Hassan Dukhtar and repeats it. Jason: delivers the running joke. Rufus, Clive, Lorelei: table companions.
226.name: Hassan Dukhtar

227.content: Helsveth is a draconian World-Phoenix servant being groomed to become First Sister as Dawn moves to the Hierophants. Formal, deferential and earnest, she is still learning initiative; by Book 11 she is the current prime vessel. Reverent: she says serving the World-Phoenix is a fulfilling life and the communion the greatest thrill and honour of her life. Earnest: Dawn rebukes her for challenges that were all designed for her. A servant of the World-Phoenix and its prime vessel by Book 11. Dawn says Helsveth will become First Sister while Dawn joins the Hierophants. Dawn: mentor and predecessor.
227.name: Helsveth

228.content: Henrietta Geller is Humphrey's older sister, a bronze-rank summoning specialist who takes her sibling role seriously. She trains the team, helps defend Greenstone in the Book 3 surge, and by Book 12 is an adventurer on Cassandra's team. Protective and critical: she makes clear Humphrey's teammates are yet to meet her approval and appoints herself to look after him and his team. Coaching: "It's not enough to be a distraction for your damage dealer". Summoning specialist, "something of a one-woman team"; one summon is an angelic messenger with healing powers. Bronze rank for almost two years in Book 2; the senior adventurer at twenty-one in Book 3. Daughter of Danielle and Keith; Humphrey's older sister. Returned to Greenstone with her father ahead of the monster surge. Humphrey: younger brother.
228.name: Henrietta Geller

229.content: Hess Jor Nasala is a silver-rank messenger, dark-skinned and silver-haired, who serves as Jes Fin Kaal's chief assistant and mouthpiece. Deferential and careful, he relays the messengers' objections and counsels caution. Cautious: "We cannot base our activities on doubts and assumptions". Discreet: he does not respond, knowing better than to talk for the sake of it. Honest about danger: he admits he would not fight Jason. Silver rank, subordinate to Kaal, who is gold rank and a Voice of the Will. Kaal's chief assistant and mouthpiece. Jes Fin Kaal: his superior. Fal Vin Garath: a fellow messenger present at the meeting.
229.name: Hess Jor Nasala

230.content: Hester Maharala is Emir's portal user and head of logistics, born in Jayapura in Pranay. Warm, travelled and practical, she gets people where they need to be and keeps Emir's operations running. Warm and practical: Jason compares her portal range to his own shadow portals. Respected: "Hester was one of Emir's most important staff members". Portal user: she traces a circle in the air to open a portal; she can only open portals to places she has visited and the time before her next use depends on range. She portals Clive back to the city. Born in Jayapura, a port city of Pranay. Has a clifftop house with grotto rooms and a swim-access bar. A shopkeeper calls her "Hester Maharala... The lady with the house on the hill".
230.name: Hester Maharala

231.content: Hiro Asano is Jason's uncle, a Sydney crime figure and the family's black sheep, who knew about hidden magic and the factions around it before Jason returned. He is bought out by the EOA at Jason's insistence, stays in the family circle through the whole series, and shares Jason's dry humour. Wary: he compares the dangerous Vermillion with the returned Jason and "knew that fear" in how Ari reacted. Black sheep: "Hiro's criminal connections had made him a black sheep of the family". Long-suffering and jokey: he teases at the family gathering that "There have been many cultures where it's acceptable to marry your brother". Does not like fuss: he rubs a hand over his face unsure where to start. He leads a Sydney criminal organisation and meets its leaders. He is not an essence user in the lines read. Hiro's contacts in the magical world, including the EOA's pressure on Sydney, are why Jason gets him out of the way. Jason's uncle; Ken Asano is his brother. He and Taika hold the Sydney operation and watch Shade warily. Jason: nephew; Hiro stands beside him at the family gathering on his return. Taika: his employee and friend. Ken: brother, who slings a possessive arm over his son.
231.name: Hiro Asano

232.content: Holly Macrossan succeeds Anna Tilden as Under-Secretary-General of the UN Office of Supernatural Affairs. After the position is lost she becomes Australia's liaison to the Multinational Supernatural Response Taskforce. Dry, careful and practical, she believes only what she can verify. Sceptical: she maintains a sceptical mindset despite two decades of magic. Wary of cores: she did not want to see reality cores return, remembering secret wars over cores. Tolerant within limits: Anna knew she tolerated wild events "but there were always limits". Hit by loss: losing her nephew hit her hard. Not an essence user in the lines read; she is a high-level bureaucrat and diplomat. Anna kept an eye on her while running the Network's Sydney branch. Anna Tilden: predecessor and sponsor. Sophie: a first impression.
232.name: Holly Macrossan

233.content: Hudson Kettering is the huge earth-essence front-liner of Beth Cavendish's team and cousin of Dustin Kettering. He is a stone-shielding bruiser who meets Jason on the sand barge assault, fights Humphrey in a Geller-versus-Cavendish contest, and joins the Reaper trial expedition. Size: "One of the members of Beth's team was a huge human named Hudson. He looked like Humphrey with twenty percent bonus person, to the point of being almost as large as Gary". First meeting: he tells Jason "You don't seem evil". Team role: Beth puts him "front and centre" in the assault on the sand barge, and a large flat block of sandstone rises under the team to carry them forward like a raft. In the fight: a bronze-rank captain's charge shatters his stone shield and sends him staggering; he ploughs up the ramp "crashing into the people inside and making space for the others". Beth tells him "No slacking". Family: he is cousin to Dustin, "the only one I can think of who could stack up to Jonah" among defenders, and cannot be pried from Beth's team. Dustin sits beside him with their teams around them. Humphrey's offer: Jason brings Humphrey to talk to Hudson about his cousin joining a Geller team; Hudson says a Geller name is good "but so was Mercer", and the family wants real adventurers for Dustin after Thadwick. Memorial: his team attends the memorial because "Her standing strong is the reason my team all got out alive".
233.name: Hudson Kettering

234.content: Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller is the leader of Team Biscuit, a tall, broad-shouldered, handsome young man from a family that has been adventuring for sixteen generations. He begins the series a shy teenager and becomes a steady leader and one of the team's strongest fighters. Formal in a crisis: in Book 3, facing the Builder's forces, he announces "My name is Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller. My family have been adventurers for sixteen generations. We aren't alchemists or weaponsmiths on the side... For hundreds of years we have done one thing, and one thing only: protect our world from people like you". Shy in personal matters: when Jason asks in front of his mother whether he has spoken to Gabrielle, he turns white and shakes his head. Moral voice: in Book 1 he confronts Jason about the cruelty of the mirage-arena ambush. He later advises against elaborate plans: "We tried that fifteen years ago and we only got from Rimaros to Yaresh". Essences: the dragon confluence, reached through the might and wing essences. Abilities include dragon wings and a flaming dragon-wing sword, a Dragon's Might aura that turns fire into dragon fire, teleporting, and the ability Spartoi, which at gold rank calls up a hundred dragon-tooth bone-golem warriors in blue and gold armour. Racial gift: his human gift Special Attack Affinity evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon and later into Hero's Drive, with the racial gift Hero's Sacrifice.
234.name: Humphrey Geller

235.content: Ian Evans (Evans-Asano) is Jason's brother-in-law, Erika's husband and Emi's father. A doctor when he learned about magic, he becomes a healer with two decades of experience on the confluence of medicine and magic. Steady and humane, he is one of the few outside Jason's blood who can enter his spirit vault. Easy-going at home: dressed like it was laundry day with Hiro and Erika at the family mansion. Frank about Emi: he understates his daughter's stubbornness. Trusts Jason: "I've known Jason since he was twelve years old". He and Erika were midway through iron, having taken cores regularly. He is a doctor whose two decades of experience cover the confluence of medicine and magic. Erika's husband and Emi's father. Moved out of the family house after their daughter did. Jason: brother-in-law; one of the few outside blood relatives who can enter his spirit vault. Rufus: walks with him over Emi's training.
235.name: Ian Evans

236.content: Itsuki Tiwari is a young Japanese essence user from the Tiwari clan, an admirer of Jason with a doom confluence. He joins the Asano combat team in Book 5, avoids battle after the Berlin deaths, and in 2038 is a gold-ranker affliction specialist protected by Nigel's nine-person unit. He is Akari Asano's husband, though in Book 13 he moves out. Nervous and polite: "I apologise for being the one to meet you"; his aura shudders with anxiety. Admiring: "my essences are dark, blood and omen, with a doom confluence" because he followed Jason's exploits. Honest in pain: he says his wife's life "doesn't have room for me anymore". Regretful: he turned to monster cores out of fear and trauma, then came to regret it. Essences dark, blood and omen forming a doom confluence. Stealthy scout in Book 5, a poor fit for the combat team. New to gold rank in 2038; a traditional backline affliction specialist who can "blanket massive areas in death" faster and more reliably than Jason. One of the first to have his monster core taint purged. Son of Koya, the youngest of three Tiwari elders; Denji is patriarch and Souta the middle brother. After the deaths of Asya, Greg and Kaito he avoided regular battle and turned to monster cores. Koya and the Tiwari elders: his father and uncles. Jason: idol turned colleague. Nigel: commander in the vampire war.
236.name: Itsuki Tiwari

237.content: Jameela is a priestess of Undeath, Garth Larosse's most trusted subordinate, tall and elegant, capable and quick to learn. She helps lead the undead army in Cardinas and the desert, and dies fighting Taika when the priesthood collapses. First impression: a "tall, beautiful woman" with long legs, whose addition to Garth's group left him "almost sad to have given up his flesh"; "capable and intelligent, eager and quick to learn", the opposite of another priest he was forced to bring. Dress: an elegant combat robe and heavy boots. Garth's feelings: Garth feels a longing for her despite his unliving body but never acts on it, "not allowing himself such a lack of discipline". Knowledge of Hero: she says she has "never seen anyone who has drunk from the Cup of Heroes" and reads it as Hero's miracle at the brink of defeat. Before the god: she and Garth drop to their knees when Undeath appears as a living man in black robes with empty sockets and a crimson spark, and she bows to Undeath and then Garth. In battle: she silences a skeleton's communication magic, watches the divine giants clash and points out that crushing the undead at the wall will cost time to replenish. Perception: she warns "He's not bluffing, High Priest... The world feels wrong, somehow. Like standing on a frozen lake as the ice starts to crack". Intelligence work: she extracts what she can about Asano from prisoners, who say his aura is like a gold-ranker's in strength and coverage.
237.name: Jameela

238.content: Jamis Fran Muskar is an astral king whose avatar attends the Builder's observation scene, berates defiant messengers and, in Book 13, advises Jason on McKean with condescension. He rules from a sleek spaceship-like dimension ship. Vain and sharp when crossed: he snarls at defiant messengers that they directly defied the Council of Kings. Dismissive of lesser threats: Farrah says "Muskar might not think McKean is dangerous". Rules a sleek dimension ship that looks out of place on Pallimustus. Says when the task is complete "the price is paid. Zithis Carrow Vayel will have fulfilled his debt to us". One of the Council of Kings. Zithis Carrow Vayel: a debtor to the kings. Jason: Jason says Muskar sees danger only for those he cares about, namely Jason himself.
238.name: Jamis Fran Muskar

239.content: Jason Asano is the series' protagonist: an Australian from the coastal town of Casselton Beach who, at twenty-three, is pulled across the cosmos to Pallimustus by a failed summoning. He becomes an affliction specialist, a bronze-, silver- and gold-rank adventurer, a king of his own astral kingdom, and finally the administrator of the System that every essence user in the cosmos sees. Humour and references: he jokes constantly and quotes films and television. He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart"; he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine. He says "G'day" and "mate". Self-deprecation: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities". He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway". Essences: Dark, Blood, Sin and the Doom confluence. His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence). Weapons: a sword, Dread Salvation, an iron-rank growth item of legendary rarity made by Gary, later reforged by Gary with his mentor Virid and with Jason's soul-bond guiding the work, becoming the sword [Hegemon's Will] with the scabbard Hegemon's Dominion; Virid's surname Martine is Book 6, Ch47 L270. Way of the Reaper martial arts. The set Regalia of the Dark Hegemon includes the Amulet of the Dark Guardian.
239.name: Jason Asano

240.content: Jeni Kavaloa is the gold-rank leader of the mixed-force surge expedition in Book 7. She is irritated by the roster, suspects Vesper Rimaros of assembling it, and enlists Jason's astral magic to seal the astral aperture. Impatient: unhappy about being "saddled with the mixed group". Suspicious of politics: the roster is like "a mad alchemist throwing volatile ingredients in a pot". Practical: she plans for the worst and does not slow when she senses the clearing's oddity. Gold rank; she senses Jason's defences pop an opponent's aura like a soap bubble. Sets up a device to seal the astral aperture, roping in Jason as astral specialist. She knows Orin Pensinata chiefly through his famous uncle Amos. Vesper Rimaros: suspected of rigging the roster. Jason: recruited for his astral skill.
240.name: Jeni Kavaloa

241.content: Jes Fin Kaal is a gold-rank messenger ritualist and Voice of the Will who leads the messengers' dealings with Yaresh. Quiet, exact and unreadable, she lets others speak and listens for what they leave out. Formal: "I am Voice Kaal, and you may address me as such". Probing: she reads Benella's emotions with her aura. Keeps things back: Jason says she played things mostly straight but kept things from them. Gold rank ritualist; a Voice of the Will. Boris says she believed Destruction wanted a massive explosion once the messengers claimed the soul forge. "Relatively new to the stronghold" and "referred to by the other messengers as Voice Kaal". Benella: servant she questions. Fal Vin Garath and Hess Jor Nasala: subordinates.
241.name: Jes Fin Kaal

242.content: Jonah Geller is a heavy-armoured Geller family fighter on Rick's team who is captured by the Builder cult and dies when the star seed is extracted. Brash and loyal, he learns too late what the family name cannot protect him from. Brash: "I'm going to show this little no-name weed what it means to fight a Geller". Loud in battle: he shouts to draw out monsters. Resistant to help: Danielle must seek legal permission from his family to have him examined for a star seed, as he refuses. The team's bulwark in heavy armour and shield. Humphrey says Jonah had quit Rick's team and was found with a new team in Hornis. Danielle Geller: family elder who sought his examination. Dustin Kettering: replacement on the team.
242.name: Jonah Geller

243.content: Jory Tillman is Greenstone's gentle alchemist and clinic-runner, Jason's first friend, and later Belinda's boyfriend. Passionate about making alchemy affordable, he becomes a Healer-backed teacher spreading his methods around the world. Idealist: "If I can make alchemical products affordable to everyone, not only can it help a huge number of people, but it will open up huge new markets". Honest about himself: technically an adventurer, he is "the first to admit he rarely went on adventures"; his "true calling was alchemy". Gentle: he tells Jason "You have a good day" to a guard and nurses patients with Healer priests. Passionate teacher: "He lit up when talking about his alchemy, and his passion for helping people was wildly appealing". Alchemy: he brews potions and elixirs from materials he gathers in towns and villages and runs an alchemy lab and medical clinic, the Broad Street Clinic. Miracle potion: his facility produces the first batch of lesser miracle potions, a thank-you to Jason who funded it. In a fight: floating clear orbs and materials from his pockets and belts in the Reaper trials and quick to throw enemies overboard on a skyship. Teaching: in Book 11 he lectures a group of students on a stage in a hazy hall. Member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association. The Healer makes his clinic a sanctuary and the church backs him; "The Church of the Healer gave him a mandate and funding to spread his methods around the world".
243.name: Jory Tillman

244.content: Jota Withers is a gold-rank dimension ship captain in a pirate admiral's service who is sent to Earth in Book 12. Weary, proud and cautious, he has always been one rung short of what he was promised. Weary and proud: he reflects that the universe-city of Interstice is "for most practical purposes, the centre of the cosmos". Self-aware: arrogance cost him opportunities. Cautious: he watches Jason float towards him, noting the impenetrable aura and the scars probably not affectations. Gold rank; his vessel is a rarity, only gold rank, which suits certain jobs. Born in a feeder realm, he fell short of Interstice at gold rank and ended up serving "a self-styled cosmic admiral" who was a pirate lord. Noriko Asano: his host on Earth.
244.name: Jota Withers

245.content: Kaito Asano is Jason's older brother, a year his senior, married to Amy, with two daughters, Hana and Jace. Easy-going and socially skilled, he is the "well-received original" Jason grew up in the shadow of. In Book 4 he reconnects with Jason, in Book 5 he flies a helicopter with Network defectors against the vampires, and he dies in Berlin. Socially adroit: Jason says he never had "Kaito's skill for getting along". The favourite: their parents "got Kaito, so they were willing to put up with me". Casual: he greets the family meeting with "G'day... We're arrived for the mysterious family meeting". Dry on pop culture: his knowledge of classic pop culture "appeared to begin and end with Miami Vice". Warm with his children: he leads Hana by the hand and carries Jace. After Jason's return he joins the Network-defector combat team with Asya and Greg. He flies drones to sweep the ruins of a town and owns the helicopter Jason and Akari ride in. A year older than Jason; the "well-received original" at school, so Jason felt like "a disappointing rehash". He and Amy bought her parents' house next door to Jason's family. He and Amy's relationship caused the fallout that left Jason dropping out of university; Jason did not want details. Jason: brother; Jason says Kaito made his own choice to stand up for his world and that Amy knows it. Amy: wife, with daughters Hana and Jace. Erika: sister who keeps the family together.
245.name: Kaito Asano

246.content: Kalif is a member of Team Storm Shredder who has "bad blood" with Jason from their first meeting, and who ends up on his side in the war against the undead and messengers.
