He is blunt, sulky and loyal to his team leader Korinne. Hot-headed: Korinne tells her "still-angry team member" to let go of a quarrel, "You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata". History with Jason: he first met Jason "at a bad time", at the height of Jason's volatility. They worked together on the underwater rescue under Korinne, after which Kalif "wanted nothing more to do with Asano" and was relieved he would leave Rimaros. He then learned their team was going with him. Agreeing to go: "Of course we go. That doesn't mean we go blindly, and you know that Asano and I have bad blood". He eventually shakes Jason's hand. Team Storm Shredder: he names the team to Jason and thinks being watched by Jason's guard dog is "unsettling. Makes it hard to relax". Driving: left behind to drive the team's new vehicle, he is "starting to get a handle on it" and has hit few other craft. Vitesse approach: he sums up Humphrey's idea as "the Vitesse approach, but scaled up". Complaints: he grumbles that his team will work for two weeks while Jason is "knocking boots with the cute pink-haired woman". Opinions on afflictions: he says of area specialists, "No iron-rank monster is tough enough to make afflictions worthwhile".
246.name: Kalif

247.content: Kasper Irios is a peak-bronze heir of House Irios whom Jason meets at a tailor's shop after the Zara marriage scandal. By Book 12 he is an adventurer on a team with Orin Pensinata. Shaken: his movements are "oddly stumbling" and he freezes when he sees Jason. Eager to please: shocked when Jason names himself the dead man. Nervous: his friends pick up on his nervousness. A peak-level bronze-ranker, close to silver like his three young friends. Zara's intended match was "a member of the Irios family". Vesper engineered Jason's meeting with him for political reasons, and Jason's overture to the family was not taken up. Jason: unwilling companion.
247.name: Kasper Irios

248.content: Keith Geller is Danielle Geller's husband and Humphrey and Henrietta's father. The text shows him mostly in groups; he is the quiet, reliable counterpoint to Danielle. Solid and reliable: "Compared to Danielle, her husband, Keith, was more akin to their son: a solid and reliable counterpoint to her domineering charms". Father of Henrietta, who takes her role as Humphrey's older sister seriously. Humphrey and Henrietta: son and daughter.
248.name: Keith Geller

249.content: Ken Asano is Jason's father, a Japanese-born Australian landscape architect who embraces the Australian lifestyle with convert's zeal. He catches Jason in a huge hug when Jason returns, joins the Asano Village family, learns a skirmish confluence and by Book 13 is a regular companion on Jason's walks. Convert's zeal: "Proving there is no zealot like a convert, Ken was all about the Australian lifestyle, from pub rock to footy matches and weekend barbecues". Warm and undemanding: Jason finds "his father's warm and undemanding support was a balm". Emotional: he goes still, then "exploded forward" to hug Jason. Straightforward: he asks whether Jason has gone "a little far" with his domain. Has the skirmish confluence, which suits running battles; many powers trip up the enemy. Born in Japan, raised in Australia from a very young age. The middle brother: Shiro was the favourite, Hiro the disappointment, "your father laid low in the middle".
249.name: Ken Asano

250.content: Ketevan Arziani is an analytical Network officer in Sydney, Anna Tilden's assistant, who later becomes Yumi Asano's chief of staff. Brisk and sceptical, she tests leaps of logic. Analytical: Anna places a lot of trust in her analytical abilities. Sceptical: in Book 11 she doubts Jason's plans while Yumi has faith. Formal title: Assistant to the Director of Operations, Sydney branch. Investigates a hospital event up the coast. Jason saves her life with one of Shade's bodies forming a parachute. She leads the Network defectors' intake and sits on calls with the Sydney branch. After the Network's Australian branch breaks up, Yumi hires her for her administrative skill. Anna Tilden: her director. Yumi Asano: her new principal.
250.name: Ketevan Arziani

251.content: Killian Laurent is Cole Silva's right-hand man and the leader of Silva's bronze-rankers. He works with the Builder cult, uses a star seed, flees Greenstone with Silva's wealth and is later captured and chained by Jason's team. Unctuous and without limits: he ushers in guests. Merciless: he argues that a man who can defy the star seed's power cannot be left alive. Exploitative: in Book 8 he is described as dangerous for how he wormed into corners, exploiting and betraying those he works with. Not given a rank in the lines read; Laront says his real name isn't Laurent, he "chose that to annoy me". He uses a star seed for the cult. "Of the bronze rankers under Silva, Killian was the unquestionable leader" and he runs the secret site. He had worked behind the scenes to plunder the Silva family while Jason distracted Silva. Cole Silva: employer he betrays.
251.name: Killian Laurent

252.content: Knowledge is the goddess of Knowledge. Jason meets her in Book 1 on arriving at her temple, and for twelve books she charms and manipulates him. In Book 13 he learns she has prepared for half a millennium to invade Earth and has used him as a key part of the plan.
252.name: Knowledge

253.content: Korinne Pescos leads a Rimaros guild-elite team, later called Storm Shredder, that fights beside Jason in the surge, travels with him in Book 9 and joins the Cardinas campaign. In Book 11 she survives the Undeath siege dazed and morose after losing a friend. Efficient: she relays orders swiftly, her efficiency "only enhanced by Jason's communication power". Loyal: "he's our asshole, and we don't turn on our own assholes". Peacemaker: "Let it go, Kalif... You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata". Guarded then curious: she visits Jason's cabin guarded about his methods and takes a slice of baked goods thoughtfully. Leader of a silver-rank guild team of six; they were star performers, clearing enemies faster than the other teams, with two high-damage members and the rest built around them. Her team "operated alone through most of the surge". She feels Jason's aura as "the cold anger of an icy hell". Leader of Orin and Kalif's team, who coordinated the underwater complex rescue. Her team eschewed the yacht for their own vehicle during travel. Rosa, Orin, Kalif, Zara: team members. Jetta: a friend, dead as a puppet. Jason: she guesses he will lecture on Rimaros-style versus Vitesse-style adventuring.
253.name: Korinne Pescos

254.content: Landemere Vane is the Vane heir whose failed summoning pulls Jason to Pallimustus. He is the first person Jason meets and the first he kills, which leaves Jason shaken for weeks. Ambitious and out of his depth: Dougall says Landemere summoned "one of them entities from beyond the void". Traditional family: his mother says "this is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way". Clive explains that Landemere's summoning went wrong, possibly because he reached beyond his ability or a dimensional event interfered. He was holding more than a thousand coins when killed. His mother, who looks no older than her son, is among the cultists who greet Jason. The Vane family treats the summoning as a family matter: "This is my manor, my family". Familiar: Jason's first encounter with a native creature was Vane's familiar, which tried to avenge him and fell victim to aging masonry. Cressida Vane: his mother, who calls him "poor Landemere".
254.name: Landemere Vane

255.content: Lenora Coleman is the bureaucrat who runs the dimensional artefact site in Australia. She was recruited from university, spends her working life in a monitoring station, and by Book 12 directs a bunker operation against pirates arriving via Jason's domain. Disillusioned: "her excitement had been well and truly killed off". Composed: she pinches the bridge of her nose, breathes out and schools her expression. Dry: Anna says she will "play this objectively". A core user and not a fighter. She directs operations from the command-and-control room, the bunker's most restricted zone. Excited to join the program out of university, then a year in the monitoring room drained that. Worked there for "almost her entire adult life". Her deputy Barry is mayor of the artefact city.
255.name: Lenora Coleman

256.content: Li Li Mei is a Chinese silver-ranker and daughter of Li Ning who deals with Jason on Earth in Books 4-6, ends up in Pallimustus and is found hiding in Boko, and becomes a political figure in Book 13. Controlled and watchful, she adapts quickly to a new world's rules. Diplomatic: she hopes for a "more modest collaboration in the future". Adaptive: one of the few with political experience in both worlds. Silver rank in Books 4-6; Jason uses her as a test subject for refining his control of the System. Daughter of Li Ning; her gold-rank uncle is Li Chen. Has lived in Boko for years. Li Ning and Li Chen: father and uncle. Jason: acquaintance and test subject.
256.name: Li Li Mei

257.content: Liara Rimaros is a gold-rank Adventure Society special-operations officer and a lesser member of the Rimaros royal house. She screens adventurers for Builder cultists in Book 7, leads the Book 8 expedition into the Builder's complex, handles Jason for the royal family and stays a brisk, protective ally. Brisk and official: she is working without rest as the city fills with adventurers to be filtered for cultists. Wary of politics: she "disdained" the politics she "could never seem to escape". Self-critical but resolute: after Gibson Amouz's capture she "allowed shame to flash over her expression before schooling it"; she stands up to his father, "Get out of my office, Lord Amouz". Protective: "Don't even think about it", she tells Zareen of Jason. Rank: a gold-ranker, leader of the Book 8 expedition with her former teammate Jana Costi as second. Investigator: her search for the cult's portal users is a process of elimination through portal schedules, market tracking and field reports. Not for rescues: she understands why she was told not to take part personally in the mining-complex rescue: "Her abilities were ill-suited to the task and her emotional investment would not be an asset". Royal branch: "from one of the more remote branches of the royal family", not close enough to be called a princess, but entitled to a home on the royal sky island and to take part in the contests for the throne in her youth.
257.name: Liara Rimaros

258.content: Lorelei Grantham is a researcher who becomes Vice-Dean and later Vice Chancellor of astral magic research, recruits Clive, covers for his escape from Rakesh and becomes his partner in Book 13. Polite, administrative and quietly decisive, she defers to Clive's research and protects him from officials. Protective: she shields Clive from Lady Ajus and stalls Lady Ajus without asking what he was doing. Deferential to research: she later studies the notes he left. Vice-Dean of the astral magic research department in Rakesh; Vice Chancellor of the Magic Research Association by Book 12. She introduces herself as a researcher assigned to the Adventure Society's Continental Council when recruiting Jason's team's help against the Builder cult. She recruited Clive out of Greenstone; Clive thinks she was misled too.
258.name: Lorelei Grantham

259.content: Lorenn is the last councilwoman of the brighthearts of Cardinas and, after Jason's intervention, the leader of her people. An ash-aspect brightheart who fought a war she could not win, she accepts surface allies she dislikes, hands her territories to Jason and leads her people into the new subterranean realm he builds. Last of the council: the brighthearts had a ruling council of nine, "three elected from the gold-rankers, three from the normal-rankers and three from the guilds"; only Lorenn remains, the others "having sacrificed everything to keep the rest of us alive". She is addressed as Councilwoman. Appearance: an ash aspect, with "smoky greys" that she thinks far less appealing than the forge-glow of her fire-aspect friend Marla. War room: she stands alone in the old council chamber, now a war room, before a live model of the city drawn from the natural array and mostly covered in the sickly green of the elemental messengers' tree. Marla: Marla urges evacuating a number of people they can feed; Lorenn breaks down, then accepts the comfort. Beaufort: she keeps the alliance with the Builder cult's commander despite loathing the cultists, "Our alliance stands". Later she tells the adventurers that accepting them "was not an easy choice" because "we are not warriors". Suspicion of the surface: she cannot bring herself to be happy at the prospect of more surface invaders.
259.name: Lorenn

260.content: Lorus is a fire-aspect brightheart who claims a territory in the unified battlefield and wants all the power. Ambitious, impatient and proud, he refuses to hand over his territory, is out-argued by Neil and Durrum, and loses his followers' support. Fire aspect: "Lorus, a fire-aspect brightheart whose messengers were likewise possessed of flame powers", each shrouded in steam as they evaporated the rain. Aggressive: he pushes aggressively "in spite of casualties" while Durrum is more conservative, and he has no intention of stopping his offensive against the cult. Betrayal charge: Durrum shouts "Are you betraying us?" and "You're killing us". Defiance of Neil: the brighthearts around him yell that they would never let the undead go, and Lorus grandstands once Neil has left the cage. His case: "I will not hand over my power on their say-so. Those cultist abominations invaded our city. They were the beginning of the end for our entire people!". Power grab: "Then give the territories to me. Once everyone actually obeys, I will make us stronger as we go... Our messengers are stronger than theirs". Neil's read: Neil gambles that Lorus is "a volatile mix of ambition, impatience and pride, with an unearned sense of entitlement", and says his actions show he likes "having command of all these messengers". Losing support: Lorus looks around and finds even his followers will not meet his eyes, "their faces showing disgust, disdain or disappointment".
260.name: Lorus

261.content: Lucian Lamprey is the corrupt director of Greenstone's Magic Society branch, an elf with a fighter's physique "banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties". He treats the Fortress as his office, orchestrates Jason's kidnapping with Cole Silva, and is cut down by Danielle Geller and imprisoned. Smug and indulgent: he arrives at his viewing room "with a contented sigh". Handsy: he strokes his fingers over a face in the viewing window. Quick to blame: his fury threatens to erupt when pressed. Danielle outpaces him in a duel and cuts him. His handling of a star seed for the Church of Purity comes under scrutiny. "Banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties"; he is not a member of the local elf community. His deputy Pochard maintains the city campus so he can use the Fortress as his office. Pochard Finn: deputy and friend. Cole Silva: co-conspirator. Danielle Geller: opponent.
261.name: Lucian Lamprey

262.content: Marcus Hargrave Xenoria is a massive leonid troubleshooter for the Adventure Society's continental council, sent to Yaresh to break the aristocrats' hold. Booming, cheerful and blunt, his bluster hides a politician's skill with leverage. Cheerful and blunt: "an adventurer and the man the Adventure Society saw fit to deploy to your city". Wry: he wonders if a familiar picked Team Biscuit's name. Confrontational: "I was warned that you might give me trouble" to Gormanston Bynes. Accommodating to Jason: which unsettles Jason's allies. "A high-level agent of the Adventure Society's continental council, Marcus was a troubleshooter and enforcer". His arrival and the support he wins from figures such as Gormanston leave the aristocrats scattered. Gormanston Bynes: opponent turned supporter.
262.name: Marcus Hargrave Xenoria

263.content: Marek Nior Vargas is a gold-rank messenger commander who leads the breach force over Yaresh's entertainment district in Book 9. Held captive inside Jason's astral kingdom, he slowly questions the indoctrination every messenger undergoes and becomes the leader of the free messengers. Arrogant, then honest: confident in his superiority over "servant races", but he learns that "when pushed, even the least of sapient species would push back". Respects craft: he appreciates "a power used well over one that was mindlessly strong" and wants to face Humphrey in battle. Disaffected from the Voice: he hates Jes Fin Kaal and avoids politics. Quietly longing for freedom: freedom from astral kings "was what he had always hoped for and never believed possible". Gold-rank commander; he blocks a projectile with his wing without effort. He spent far longer than Tera's lifetime working free of the conditioning every messenger goes through. Messengers' soul spaces are blank concrete utilitarian landscapes; Marek compares them with Jali's vibrant realm. Tera Jun Casta: young messenger whose identity rests on the indoctrination; Marek sits beside her with concern. Jason: his captor; Marek senses Jason looks "for reasons not to kill them". Jes Fin Kaal: he hates the Voice. Humphrey: a respected enemy.
263.name: Marek Nior Vargas

264.content: Marie Finnegan is the recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch who ran a secret programme working with Elizabeth and Simon McKean. Controlling and secretive, she thinks she is running a tight operation; Jason takes her to talk and says he will hand her over to the Network afterwards. Controlling and secretive: she thinks she is running a tight operation. Professional: she answers a call as "Finnegan". She uses earth-shaping powers to create a basin at a rocky shore. She runs video conferencing with feeds from Pakistan and a grid system. The recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch, fleeing with Elizabeth. The leadership council kept the vampire programme contained at her insistence; her contacts with Elizabeth and McKean were critical. Her backers called using Elizabeth the smart choice. She worked directly with Elizabeth, "intimately" according to Remy. Elizabeth: her vampire partner. Jason: interviews her at his estate, "this part is best done by me".
264.name: Marie Finnegan

265.content: Marla is a fire-aspect brightheart who commands the brightheart military defending Cardinas. Commanding and practical, she answers loss with order. Comforting: she comforts Lorenn, the city's leader, when she breaks down. Practical: she briefs Jason on the citadel's defences, the children in the growth chambers and the messengers' failed attempts to cross the death chamber. Commander of the brightheart military; she commands the citadel's response when Gary drinks from the Cup of Heroes and coordinates reinforcements. Leader of the brightheart military in Cardinas. Lorenn: the city's leader whom she comforts. Jason and Gary: allies in the defence.
265.name: Marla

266.content: Melody Jain is Sophie's mother, who faked her death twenty years before Book 6 and then led the Order of Redeeming Light in the Storm Kingdom, brainwashed into fanaticism by the order's god. Jason's team captures her in Book 8; she is held, treated and slowly softens, ending as a loving mother in Book 13. Fanatical and sharp: "sharp, fanatical and brainwashed" when Jason met her. Clean habits: she likes showers and is "ever at the ready" in her marred armour. Commanding: she silences her second with a gesture. Softening later: after therapy with her daughter she is "less hostile and manipulative". An essence user responsible for a fort holding out without supplies. A sword fighter fast enough to dance with Jason's blade. Shackled, she still runs and hides through a cloud-stuff palace. Faked her death twenty years before Book 6, using a wall panel in Marta Fries's house in Kurdansk. Arabelle dates the story to "around a quarter of a century ago". The Order of Redeeming Light is a creation of the god Disguise masquerading as Purity; its Flames of Redemption are a modification of lesser vampirism. Arabelle: helps look after her. Jason: his team holds her captive; by Book 13 she gives him a motherly smile.
266.name: Melody Jain

267.content: General Michael Mills of the United States Army is the operational commander of the EDJI's largest military action to date, the war against the vampires in Book 13. A career soldier who rebuilt infantry doctrine for the magical age, he is trusted to handle Jason, and is chosen as spokesperson for the EDJI member states. Past posting: he was stationed at Saint-Étienne "two decades and several ranks ago", before the Asano Clan took over. Seen the horrors: he has seen "with his own eyes the power of the vampire lords and the land of horrors they had made" and believes the stories of Asano reclaiming his territory. The EDJI: he had never thought it would happen and was there for the negotiations when China and Russia demanded more influence; the US almost derailed it over the spelling of "defense". He does not approve of the troops calling it "edgy". Doctrine: he commanded the Infantry Reimplementation Program, redefining infantry doctrine as augmented soldiers with magitech weapons returned infantry to the forefront. Command: with his doctrine knowledge and experience fighting vampires, he is placed "in operational command of the EDJI's largest military action to date". Observations of the base: he is met by a saluting EDJI lieutenant in a US Army-marked uniform; the tarmac holds augmented infantry and Cabal contingents, and he finds a "wild amount of diversity" in Asano Clan territory.
267.name: General Michael Mills

268.content: Miles Cotezee is a senior Vitesse Adventure Society administrator whose silver rank comes entirely from cores and who supervises missions in the Book 7 surge. A harried, courteous official, he runs paperwork and logistics. Harried: he stumbles out of his chair and hurries around the table when Clive arrives. Frank about orders: "This contract didn't come down through normal channels. It came down from on high". Reputation-minded: "Reputation is everything in this town". Silver rank "entirely from cores", with paper, knowledge, rune and scribe essences. Senior administrator at the Vitesse Adventure Society. Humphrey and Clive: officials he briefs and warns.
268.name: Miles Cotezee

269.content: The gold-rank leader of Team Moon's Edge and Tactical Commander of the Cardinas expedition, who shares overall command with Jason. Introduced as "the leader of Team Moon's Edge, Miriam Vance". Moon's Edge is a team of six women, all gold rank, raised and supervised by Allayeth from early in their careers. She is the expedition's Tactical Commander and tells Jason no when he wants to add his butterflies to a messy flying battle. Her gold-rank senses read Jason's emotions through his aura. She notices how Allayeth acts around Jason, questions him about astral kings and the goddess, and argues with him over command. Death addresses her by name. She runs the withdrawal through the citadel tunnels as overall commander and sets the defensive perimeter. In Book 11 she is the zone's co-commander with Jason, directs Moon's Edge to destroy the tree crystals and protects the non-combatants in Ramona's invisibility sphere when Amos Pensinata goes into the orb. Her team "was the most powerful force on the battlefield other than the cloud buildings and the two divine entities". Jason introduces her to Gordon, his avatar of doom. A different Miriam, Miriam Coyle, heads a magitech weapons institute in Book 13.
269.name: Miriam Vance

270.content: Mr North is the true leader of the Engineers of Ascension, first among its four Cardinals, and the Network founder's former familiar Noreth. A very old rune spider turned man, he spends centuries on Earth bargaining, scheming and experimenting, ends by disabling the Grid and by leaving Jason a vault of his research, and dies in Book 6 killing Gerling to avenge his friend. Amused and mocking: "You're a smart man, Mr Asano. More or less"; he calls Jason "a parade of delights". Controlled: "He had long ago schooled himself out of dangerous curiosity and exploitable impatience". Ruthless about outcomes: with the Grid down for months he says "A wide-scale collapse of civic and social infrastructure does not obviate our objectives" and "So long as we rule". A manipulator of principles: "Be wary of your principles, Mr Asano. I might use them to be assured that you enter that astral space". Paranoid and lonely: Barbou thinks he is "older and more powerful than anyone realises", not human, and "lonely". Webs: he draws ritual circles in webbing that contain auras, sound, scent and magic. He buries himself in a cocoon before the nuclear solar rockets, and digs out afterwards. Magitech without theory: he developed magitech "with almost no knowledge of magical theory, drastically low ambient magic, and essentially zero technology", and was too paranoid to trust capable scientists; Audrey Blaine "was a buffer between North's ambitions and his paranoia".
270.name: Mr North (Noreth)

271.content: Musin Heath is the director of the Adventure Society's Yaresh branch, an elf and veteran administrator who presides over the meetings at Jason's cloud palace and brokers a possible alliance with the messenger leader. Calm: he announces a potential alliance with the messenger leader while auras erupt in consternation. Careful: he talks behind a privacy screen with Jillet, watched by the whole room. Distrustful: he presents the messenger-delivered device with distrust. His rank and core use are not stated in the lines read. An elf, as are most Yaresh locals. He is "director of the Adventure Society's Yaresh branch". Jillet: an official he consults.
271.name: Musin Heath

272.content: Natalie Park is an ASIS agent and silver-ranker assigned as Jason's liaison during the 2038 events. A junior officer in an unenviable position, she is professional and wary. Distracted by proximity: she pays half attention at the symposium after realising who is sitting next to her. Startled easily: Jason rises from her shadow. Silver-ranker trained on Farrah's and Rufus's methods. Manages the video feeds in the briefing room. A young girl at Jason's last visit. She states it has been more than four years since a confirmed trace of McKean. Jason: her assigned principal.
272.name: Natalie Park

273.content: Neil Davone is an elf of Greenstone's Island families, a healer who grows from the Mercers' hanger-on into the heart of Jason's team. He is a priest of the Healer, and by 2038 he uses his growth magic to reclaim deserts. Essences: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence: short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing. Abilities: size-growth power and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time; the Reaper's Redoubt. Summon: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit. Late: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa.
273.name: Neil Davone

274.content: Nicolas Hendren is the archbishop of the Church of Purity, a silver-rank barrier-and-force specialist who flees the inquiry and joins the Builder cult's camp before Jason's team kills him. Stiff, proud and rule-bound, he wants Purity's dignity even as it is dragged into the cult's plans. Disgruntled and proud: he is summoned to the cult camp and refuses to taint the church for "short-term power". Moral authority absent god: his god's voice is silent, making him the highest moral authority in the realm he stands in. Silver-rank barrier and force specialist: his barrier shields his group from a falling building; a force wave power; "always the true danger". Archbishop of the Church of Purity, introduced at a Greenstone meeting. One Book 3 line spells the name Hedron. The Builder cult: reluctant ally.
274.name: Nicolas Hendren

275.content: Nigel Thornton leads a nine-person mercenary unit that began as a Network tactical team. He is the first gold-ranker outside the United States to get there without cores, and in 2038 he works as a gold-ranker for hire, infiltrating vampire strongholds and clearing blood farms alongside the Asano clan. Disciplined: "We can't match up to your gear... But we have training and discipline". Direct and proud of results: "We've taken out four category threes just today". Bitter at the blood farms: "How many farms were left running while the Asanos were hiding in their magic hole?". Careful: he spends more time hiding than moving in the city and freezes when a vampire sniffs the cellar. First gold-ranker outside the US without cores; "the US had non-core training programs long before Farrah Hurin arrived". The rest of his team are silver-rank core users. His team is the same nine-person unit it was almost two decades earlier, when it belonged to the Network's secret paramilitary wing. When the Network schismed, they left, sickened by infighting and the Australian government, and became mercenaries. Jason: Jason's tutor on how teams will fail against stronger monsters. Rufus: rides back with him from the blood farms. Gladys: he is her bodyguard.
275.name: Nigel Thornton

276.content: Nik is a four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo whom Jason brought into being, unplanned, when his soul realm became a transformation zone. He curses constantly, is bleeped on the page, and calls Jason "Dad". He is the control key to the zone's network, trains at the Geller estate, reaches gold rank and acts as a team's coordinator and overwatch through drones and mapping powers. Nik first appears to Neil and Dustin in the soul realm as a "four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo", with swearing bleeped and a "bleeper" he does not recall being installed. Jason names him in a forest: "Nik. NIK, no C", from "Lehenik", a word from the language of Jason's birth world meaning "first" or "firstly", and the name Jason would give a people of which Nik is the first instance. Jason declines to name him after Kai and offers him the Asano surname if he wants it. The transformation zone created him, with the Healer's gift erasing any flaws; Jason "unconsciously brought" him into being. He says he is "six months old" and that most of what he knows is "random nonsense put in my head". He is "the key" to the network of control nodes Jason made while changing the zone, and the node's lock is broken. He and one of Shade's bodies bring Jason's friends into the soul realm as "plan B" and lead them to the objective. He calls Boris "Two-Piece Feed".
276.name: Nik Asano

277.content: Noriko Asano is the strongest member of the old Asano clan and its patriarch's mother, who takes control from her son and opposes Jason's family. By Book 12 she is matriarch of the old clan, hosting Jota Withers. Stern, brusque and proud, she measures people by strength. Contemptuous of honour: "You sound like your new white friend, Asano". Strength-first: she argues there is only shame in weakness and "only the strongest shall rise". Calculating: she tells the others not to inform Mei and Akari, so they act as a mask for the clan's own plans. The strongest member of the old Asano clan. She wrests control of the clan from her son, the former head Shiro, whose closest family settle in Asano Village. She explains the government seized land from the "upstart clan" and gave it to the "true Asano clan".
277.name: Noriko Asano

278.content: Orin Pensinata is a calm guild adventurer, Amos Pensinata's nephew, who rises to gold and survives Team Storm Shredder's losses. Stoic and slow to speak, he keeps a team steady. Impassive: he stands apart while guilders tease the independents. Restraining: "Complications. Best left alone". Steadfast: the steady one, fresh from a rank-up. Intractable about coming along: Jason had been reluctant to accept his team, but Orin had proven intractable. Silver-ranker most notable for his famous uncle; gold by Book 12. Storm Shredder is built around buffed high-damage ranged specialists. He goes on Jason's journey because his uncle insisted. First met Jason through Vesper's arranged meeting with Kasper Irios.
278.name: Orin Pensinata

279.content: Padma Parsell is an adventurer from Remore Academy and Farrah's half-disciple, who leads a Vitesse team in the City of Fallen Echoes. Keen, grieving and quick to speak her mind, she treats Jason as a rival after Farrah's death. Keen and grieving: Farrah was her idol and mentor; she lets Jason vent her frustration. Obedient to instructors: Instructor Gabriel's voice triggers conditioned obedience. Ignores interruptions: when Lance calls out under his breath, she ignores him. Leader of a Vitesse team of Rufus's juniors. Trained at Remore Academy a few years behind Rufus. She had waited for Farrah's return to Vitesse and, when Farrah died, joined Emir's call for adventurers.
279.name: Padma Parsell

280.content: Pelli is a sharp-tongued core-using gold-ranker who keeps the town of Palisaros quiet and safe, is "Aunt Pelli" to the royal family, and is a contact for Jason in the Storm Kingdom. She fights a pirate captain outside Kasilaro and organises civilians at the mining facility. Blunt: "The name's Pelli and I'll thank you to use it". Teasing and self-deprecating: "I'm just an old core user"; she shakes her head at "an abundance of experience, dear gods". Protective: she fights outside the town to spare Kasilaro's residents. A gold-ranker and core user; she fights a pirate captain outside a town. She had a magic barrier put on a cave behind the waterfall. "Aunt Pelli" to Vesper from when she was a girl. Mayor-level authority in Palisaros: Argy tells Jason "You'll want to talk to Pelli". Vesper: calls her "Aunt Pelli". Rufus: she asks about his father and the sword.
280.name: Pelli

281.content: Phoebe Geller is a distant Geller cousin of Humphrey's, Rick Geller's sister, and a pugilist on Rick's team. Blunt and curious, she asks what everyone is thinking and sits in on Sophie's training. Dry: "I suspect your mother's hand will be firmly pressed down on the scale". Relaxed: she settles happily in a chair sipping her second glass while watching Sophie. A pugilist, "a more damage-oriented version of Sophie"; she launches off Stash's palm to strike multiple enemies. Iron rank in Book 1 and with the Adventure Society for over half a year. Distant cousin of Humphrey; the two share a last name but barely any ethnicity. Rick's sister, on his team but absent for family issues at one point.
281.name: Phoebe Geller

282.content: Pochard Finn is Lucian Lamprey's long-time deputy director in Greenstone, an elf and local who does the actual work while Lamprey enjoys the title. He is practical, discreet and understands the value of discretion. Discreet: "a man who understood the value of discretion". Protective of his boss: he steps up when fury crosses Lamprey's face. Judges Humphrey fairly: he remembers the Geller son as "polite, forthright and a little lacking in confidence". He keeps the city campus running while frequently travelling to the Fortress. He arranges the lifelike water-link to Gabriel Remore. Long-time deputy who did the real work during Lamprey's famously corrupt tenure. His son Cassowary is Lamprey's dogsbody and go-between. Lucian Lamprey: friend and employer.
282.name: Pochard Finn

283.content: Raythe is the prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments, a peak diamond-ranker from beyond Pallimustus who steps in on Jason's behalf in Yaresh and stays after the great beings leave. Direct: "I am Raythe, and I have told you as much of my intentions as you need to know. Leave or die". Calm and amused: "You shall see me again when it is done. Not too soon, as you have earned your rest". Reluctant when needed: she tells Jason with a straight face that the World-Phoenix will crawl into his soul, with reluctance in her expression. Prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments; with Velius she leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft. Boris says the Keeper of Moments polices time manipulation harshly. She tells Jason only the nameless will stand with the World-Phoenix against him. After the great beings leave, she alone remains; time there is synchronised with Jason's universe. Velius: fellow peak diamond-ranker.
283.name: Raythe

284.content: Remy is a portal specialist whose range is limited. In Book 4 he and Sebastian work for Adrien Barbou, hop across Australia with a rescued agent in Kakadu and kill her; in Book 5 he helps in Makassar; in Book 13 he is Marie Finnegan's portal man, caught between Jason and the vampire queen Elizabeth. Kakadu: he and Sebastian have taken Miranda (Ellis) out of Australia; her complaint that "Twelve hundred kilometres is the best you can do? And you have to wait an hour between portals?" draws "Let's see your portal power". They are in Kakadu National Park, which Remy is scornful of her not recognising. Range: he says no essence user can portal sixteen thousand kilometres, and that the Chinese reportedly have someone near category four who can do a few thousand at a time. He notes the rule that "You cannot portal where you have never been". Barbou's men: Miranda calls Remy a failure of "the great portal master Barbou promised". After a glance, Sebastian kills her with metal hummingbirds and a kick; Remy says "A personality like that is practically a suicide note". He reports to Adrien by phone. Book 5: "Hi, I'm Remy. You two came in pretty hot", and he takes Jason and a companion through a portal to a command post near Paotere Harbour. Book 13: Finnegan's portal man: he opens a portal "About time... If any gold-rankers turned up, I was just going to bail", is careful around "that guy", and follows Marie, Gerling and the blood orb through it.
284.name: Remy

285.content: Rick Geller is a Geller cousin and team leader, a big swordsman who is the main rival of Jason's team in Greenstone. He loses his teammate Jonah Geller to a star seed, takes Dustin Kettering on, and becomes a friend and ally of Jason in Rimaros and the later wars. Earnest and wide-eyed: the 'standard Rick' expression is wide-eyed, as Jason thinks of it. Respectful of rank: he realises he is speaking to a gold-rank princess and his head dips as if yanked by a string. Loyal to his team: he does not like having his team split, and watches over Jonah in the rescue. A huge sword wielded "like a baton", with an essence ability that "temporarily ramped up his speed and power". Rank: iron-rank in Book 1, a spear-wielder by Book 10 whose team smashes messengers with Stash's help. Hunt style: put an enemy in front of him and nothing at iron rank survives. Brother of Phoebe Geller; his team includes Jonah, Henry, the Adeah twins and later Dustin Kettering. His girlfriend is Hannah Adeah, who slaps the back of his head in Book 10. Dustin: Rick's team replaced Jonah's role with Dustin, who "was a friend of Neil's". Humphrey: a close match in style. Jonah: the teammate he fails to save. Phoebe: his sister, on his team.
285.name: Rick Geller

286.content: Roland Remore is Rufus's grandfather, a diamond-rank sword master, archchancellor of Remore Academy in Vitesse and leader of Burning Violet. He rarely appears but his presence is felt, and he arrives with the diamond-rankers at the end of Book 13. Weighty and remote: his presence on the Academy campus is always felt and draws all eyes. Proud of the guild: Gabriel says "He's always treated the guild like it's his own little fiefdom". Famous: Rufus often repeats his advice. Diamond-rank sword master; his aura surges out in Book 13. He personally brought a boy from the countryside to the academy, rumoured. Archchancellor of Remore Academy; the guild Burning Violet became more associated with the Academy after he became guild leader. Rufus's grandfather; Gabriel's father. Rufus: grandson, who repeats his advice. Humphrey: friend of Rufus who knows his reputation.
286.name: Roland Remore

287.content: Rosa Liselos is the scout of Korinne's Team Storm Shredder, with the best perception on the team. Practical and comfort-loving, she backs Kalif in wanting rest, spots Jason's skulking admirer, and guides her wounded team back through enemy lines in Book 11. By Book 12 she has retired and works for the Adventure Society. Introduced as a rival: a Rimaros adventurer addresses her as "Rosa Liselos, isn't it? What do you say, Liselos? Can you do better than Asano's shadows?". Role: "Rosa Liselos, the scout from Korinne's team"; "the team scout, she had the best perception amongst them". Comfort: she says she "can definitely live with it" if working for Jason means cloud beds and giant dinner spreads, and joins Kalif in telling Korinne the monster surge is over: "This is a can for storing food, not adventurers". Insight: she names the difference "between adventuring approaches in Rimaros and Vitesse". Gossip: she bets Jason "doesn't go for those stuffy society dances". Candour about Zara: she tells a princess to get over a man who is not keen on her and senses him "skulking around". Surprise: she asks "How did you get so close? You didn't use to be this good" of someone who has improved. Book 11: the team scout guides the wounded team back to friendly lines "through the enemy throng" to the healers. Book 12: "Rosa retired. She works for the Adventure Society now".
287.name: Rosa Liselos

288.content: Rufus Remore is a bald, dark-skinned swordsman from Vitesse, grandson of the diamond-ranker Roland Remore. He is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, runs Jason's field assessment, and remains his friend for the rest of the series. He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say. He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous. After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships. The family joke, repeated by Arabelle and Rufus in Book 10, is "my family runs a school". Swordsmanship: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand; silver and golden swords. Other powers: boots that let him walk on water and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time". Kingdom of Eclipse: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation. Rank: bronze at the start of the series, and in Book 11 he is the most powerful combatant on Earth below gold rank; the chapters read do not state that he reaches gold. Teaching: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat and later teaches the Asano clan.
288.name: Rufus Remore

289.content: Sendira is Melody Jain's second in command in the Order of Redeeming Light's local enclave: a silver-rank zealot and the person Melody trusts most. She commands the Purity forces on the island in Book 8, carries the aura beacon and the clockwork kings, and holds the order's discipline together while suspecting others. Rank in the order: Melody leads the enclave and Sendira, her second, reports on what the scouts have found. The overall leadership is the same silver rank as the individual cell leaders, so there is "a constant tension". Reliability: she is "ever-reliable"; like another cell leader, Kelleigh, she is not ambitious, which places her as Melody's second. Doctrine: she tells the converted, "Only Purity is worthy of our devotion, not his servants... We are all unworthy, seeking to cleanse the taint that lingers within us", and "Distraction and frivolity taint pure dedication of purpose". Command on the island: she is "the commander of the Purity forces on the island", separating from most of her group to take a smaller team underground. Control of subordinates: she wants Fila and Ramona "under her thumb instead of causing trouble for Melody's plans". She snaps at Ramona that "What Melody wants with the target is no concern of yours. Your place is to obey, not criticise in ignorance".
289.name: Sendira

290.content: Shako is a diamond-rank servant of the Builder who kills Jason in Book 6, apparently possessed by the Builder at the moment he does it. Later he is taken by the Sundered Throne, and the Builder replaces him with Erigo Fin Desca. Impatient and proud: he sighs at his petitioners despite not needing breath for centuries. Contemptuous: he sneers when Jason tries to push back. Struck still when overridden: when the Builder speaks through him he goes stiff. Told he has no authority of his own: "You don't have any authority, do you, Shako?". Diamond-rank: his aura crushes Jason's aura and lifts him into his grip. Can enter through a window opened by the transformation event as long as he leaves before it closes. Moves faster than Jason can think; a tablet throws him back with a sonic boom. A servant of the Builder; in Book 3 he is seen in an imperial throne room with an empress. Dawn warns that killing Jason violated the compact between the Builder, the Reaper and the World-Phoenix. Jason: killer and later subject of questions.
290.name: Shako

291.content: Sigrid Freyn (Sigrid Volaire) is a celestine healer and the leader of Valdis's team, who becomes his wife. Sensible and dry, she is the grown-up on a team of enthusiasts. Apologetic for Valdis: she quietly apologises for him. Dry and practical: she tells Valdis to be more respectful of his father and king. Networking: she steers him toward making connections. Healer and team leader; "the most impactful person on the field" in the mock battle; named by the system when Jason's team defeats her. She keeps a dimensional space with cushions. Leads Team Shining Scabbard, a famously capable leader and healer whom Neil has been training with; faces Neil in a healer match. She greets Hastor, the Mirror King's portal specialist, as "Father"; the king is her father-in-law. Open question: whether Hastor is still the king's portal specialist in Book 12; the text calls the specialist only "the Mirror King's own portal specialist".
291.name: Sigrid Freyn

292.content: Simon McKean is the former head of the Earth researchers in the Network's grid workgroup. By Book 13 he works with the vampires from a research complex beneath a French castle, preparing for a decade to fight Jason, and is Jason's final earthly adversary. Obsessed with the fight: Boris warns Jason that McKean "has spent the last decade preparing for this fight. To him, battling you is not a means but an end in itself". Cunning: he baited the coalition into the fight, and no one knows why. Controlled: he watches Jason and two familiars move through his tunnels from a monitoring room. Expert in the grid: "about as expert in it as anyone but you" and understands it better than anyone other than Farrah. Created vampire-magitech abominations by mixing modern magitech with blood magic. Modified a vine to revive the undead and bound souls of vampires and minions to it. He took Gerling from the vampire queen and used him as an agent. Head of the Earth researchers, ranked only behind Farrah in the workgroup. He and Farrah repaired the grid together after the Engineers of Ascension sabotaged it. Farrah: the only one in Jason's circle who knows him personally. The vampires: he is already working with them.
292.name: Simon McKean

293.content: Sophie Wexler is a celestine fighter known as the Nightingale in the Greenstone fighting pits. She is a thief and debt-slave when Jason meets her, has her indenture taken over by Jason in Book 2, and becomes the team's fastest fighter and, later, Humphrey's fiancée. Essences: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years. Abilities: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades; Between the Raindrops; Mirage Step and Wind Blade; unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes. Racial gifts (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring, Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity, and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament. Late: in Book 13 she has spent several years purging whole cities of disease with her wind and aura.
293.name: Sophie Wexler

294.content: Soramir Rimaros is the founder of the Rimaros royal house, a diamond-rank ruler with a palindromic name, who guides Jason through the Builder crisis. His connection to Jason is why Jason is protected from political accusations. Calming and formal: his aura spreads calm that oppresses the agitated Farrah and Liara. Plain-spoken about debts: "It is undeniable that we have dragged Jason Asano into events he never asked for". Deference from others: even the Storm King defers to the founder in the private lounge. He tells Jason that the Hierophant may intervene in the world a single time. Palindromic first and last names "were assigned in adulthood rather than at birth and denoted important members of a given family". Sits with the Storm King and core royal family members in an elevated lounge. Liara: royal officer and relative. Jason: protector and uneasy debtor. Dawn: he leads her away from the crowd.
294.name: Soramir (Soramir Rimaros)

295.content: Taika is a huge Māori man who works for Hiro Asano, befriends Jason on his return to Earth and becomes one of the Asano clan's core fighters. He rockets up the ranks, takes the garuda confluence and a golden bird form, and travels to Earth with Rufus and Boris in Book 11. Easy and cheerful: "Taika, by the way. Like the director, but I don't make films"; "the numbers for letters thing is a bit naff, though, right? It's not 2004". Companionable: he sits behind a plastic drum kit while Jason and Emi play a rhythm game. He tells Jason "I don't normally like watching people's holiday videos, but they were pretty sweet". Sharp-eyed: his "narrowed eyes lingered on Boris" before he got to work. Rank: he races up through the proto-spaces and monster waves, "especially with being human as an accelerating factor". At the end of the surge his aura is "so close to breaking through to silver that it was like an egg starting to hatch". A mobility brawler: Farrah teaches him to fight "like Taika", adapting to his new abilities, and his performance helps convince the Network to grant him a place. Garuda confluence and bird form: see Taika_Power_Set.md. He is "Taika Williams", employed by Hiro in Sydney and knows the ropes of the Asano family business. When offered the renewal essence and immortal confluence Jason picked out, he chose a different combination after discussion. Hiro Asano: his boss, who rides in silence with him in Book 4.
295.name: Taika (Taika Williams)

296.content: Tera Jun Casta is a branded messenger who challenges Jason to a duel in Yaresh, is knocked out when Jason strips her seal and later works through the destruction of her sense of self. She ends as a member of the freed messenger community living with the Asano clan. Zealous: "I am Tera Jun Casta... I will be the one to kill you". Rigid and devout: a "zealous follower of the messenger orthodoxy before her forced liberation". Duellist by temperament: she chooses weapons that instil the most fear. Guarded: she listens to Jason's story "without comment or expression, but her aura was a calamity of emotions". She fights comfortably with her abilities suppressed, in an orthodox style. Her seal keeps her at silver rank; Jason removes it by working inside her soul. A messenger unable to advance beyond silver is a loose addition to the raid forces. Her soul is branded and she was raised on lies and exploited her entire life. Her old friend from "their days of enslavement" is Jali Corrik Fen. Jali Corrik Fen: old friend. Marek Nior Vargas: her commander. Jason: freed her against her will.
296.name: Tera Jun Casta

297.content: Thadwick Mercer is the arrogant heir of House Mercer, who torments his two "offsiders" Neil and Dustin, feuds with Jason, takes a Builder star seed and becomes a vessel for the Builder. The Builder's vessel is later "the worst vessel I ever possessed"; Thadwick himself ends as an energy vampire in Book 9 and returns in Book 13. Arrogant and cruel: "a fool whose arrogance and incompetence only escalated over time" and "the worst". Fixated on Jason: "Thadwick was always fixated on me. I think he might have had a sister complex", after Jason dated his sister Cassandra. Leashed: a rival greets him, "I see your mother let you out, so long as you wore your leash". Lightning, wind, potent and storm essences. He fights from behind his protectors: Dustin used his powers to protect while Neil healed him, and Thadwick "had been blasting powers". After the star seed he becomes a vessel for the Builder and later "some weird vampire". Family: his father Beaufort Mercer is the Duke of Greenstone's brother; his mother Thalia is an adventurer. Companions by obligation: Dustin, like Neil, was "forced to train and work with Thadwick through the obligation of his family to the Mercers". Sister: Cassandra Mercer is four years older than Neil and the object of his youthful affection. Neil and Dustin: his offsiders, "both stuck under Thadwick due to their families". Thalia and Beaufort: parents, one adamant about training, the other guilty. Cassandra: his sister, who dated Jason.
297.name: Thadwick Mercer

298.content: Thalia Mercer is the matriarch of the Mercer family, a silver-rank explosive adventurer and friend and teammate of Danielle Geller. She wants better training for her son Thadwick, fusses over him after the Builder-cult crisis, and by Book 13 watches her estranged daughter Cassandra from the shadows. Welcoming with an edge: "You must be the young man people are getting so curious about". Wry and diplomatic: "I daresay you're right. So, you're willing to leave Thadwick to my family?". Unhappy about her husband's decision: she tried to convince him Thadwick needed more training. Motherly under pressure: she fusses over Thadwick as he is carried through a portal. Sentimental about her daughter: she hasn't seen Cassandra "in years" and watches her from behind a tree. Silver rank with might, potent, swift and onslaught essences: "in terms of pure explosive power she was a match for any adventurer alive". She blasted Thadwick's door "to splinters with a special attack". Her Onslaught essence informs her inclinations as well as her power set. Friend and teammate of Danielle Geller. Present at the estate when Danielle witnesses Jonah Geller's gruesome end. Cassandra: daughter she hasn't seen in years. Danielle Geller: friend and teammate.
298.name: Thalia Mercer

299.content: Timos is a Builder cultist embedded in Greenstone for years who regrets going along with Thadwick's self-recruitment, kills Frank, and stands with Zato in the Vane estate ritual. He is careful, patient and horrified by amateurs. Regretful: he "quickly came to regret" Thadwick's aggressive self-recruitment. Cautious: every mistake "threatened to snowball into disaster". Compartmentalising: he facilitated the cult's insertions and ran operatives in compartmentalised groups. He kills Frank with a conjured spear. He takes part in a ritual with Zato and Dougall. "Timos had been operating in Greenstone for years". Thadwick: an inconvenient recruit.
299.name: Timos

300.content: Travis Noble is a young Californian magitech weapons engineer who becomes Jason's outworlder weapons researcher on Pallimustus, marries the Knowledge priestess Gabrielle Pellin and, by Book 13, leads weapon development against the vampires. Earnest, happy and quick to adapt, he is the person who builds Earth's new arsenal. Overworked and decent: "Travis Noble was twenty-one years old and a category two magitech weapons engineer from California. He was also having a very bad month". Clear-sighted on Network faults: "The Network has kidnapped Mr Asano twice, along with killing his friend, his girlfriend and his brother". A researcher by temperament: "an enthusiastic researcher whose expertise bled into" other fields. Devoted husband: he is happy and worried watching his wife eat. Magitech weapons engineer: a specialist in large-scale weaponry. His dimensional space is a holographic cabinet with a sliding door, from which he pulls an oversized high-tech revolver. Cross-world builder: he works with Clive, Gary and Gabrielle on the tools and artifice side of magitech. Constructs: he waves a rod and a mannequin-like construct walks out. Sky link: his sky link service carries calls by Book 12. Category-two Network engineer who becomes head of the Special Munition Stockpile Division when his supervisor goes AWOL, with a team of people who all hate him. An outworlder from Earth to Pallimustus. Gabrielle Pellin: his wife, a priestess of Knowledge. Clive and Gary: collaborators.
300.name: Travis Noble

301.content: Trenchant Moore is a gold-rank human sword specialist of the Sapphire Crown royal guard who escorts Jason's group in Rimaros. Watchful and reserved, he reads places and people for danger. Reserved: he drops to one knee before the royals. Cautious about politics: he warns that Vesper's world is political. Gold rank sword specialist who has served as a guard on and off for decades. He boards ships checking society contracts. The royal family does not shield the Sapphire Crown from surge quotas. Vesper Rimaros: the royal who gives him leave to keep his sword.
301.name: Trenchant Moore

302.content: Umber is Shade's brother, an astral being of the Reaper's kind who trapped Shade in an astral space for centuries and, in Book 13, serves Knowledge's plan against Jason. Sensuous, opportunistic and bitter, he plays games when Shade's power is limited by a vessel. Resentful of change: fixated on the idea that changing from the original state means falling from grace; he hates Shade for embracing it. Opportunistic and bitter: he plays games when Shade's power is limited by a vessel. He built the bridge anchor ritual to bind Jason's consciousness into the prime avatar; a word from Jason makes him reel. Shade says Umber told him he had Shade trapped in an astral space for centuries "to teach you a lesson about duty". Umber persuaded Shade's summoner to trap him. Astral beings are things of spirit with defined natures: Colin an avatar of hunger, Gordon a herald of annihilation, Shade "a shepherd of death".
302.name: Umber

303.content: A swordmaster prince of the Kingdom of Mirrors whom Clive meets in the City of Fallen Echoes; he is cheerful, reckless and a rival and friend to Jason's team. Introduces himself as "Valdis" and praises Clive's reputation; the system names him Valdis Volaire. A prince of the small but influential Kingdom of Mirrors, whose borders have not changed in eight centuries; his father, the Mirror King, is eight hundred years old and the kingdom is "thick with princes and princesses". A reckless enthusiast who leads his three teammates up a tower in search of treasure; he has a light-step power, a slow-fall power and a wall run. He chooses the path of courage in the trial and is the first to step forward. A sword master, mobile striker and the stronger team's leader; his team is a highly efficient cohort trained since before they had essences. His father collects him from Jason's ship, to Valdis's embarrassment; he portals in for Jason's memorial. By Book 12 he is Sigrid's husband, assembles an arena event in under two days, and fights Jason in a mirage chamber using Mind's Eye to sense the space around him.
303.name: Valdis Volaire

304.content: Velius is a tall celestine diamond-ranker, the prime vessel of the Reaper. Warm and wry in person, chilling when the Reaper speaks through him. Warm: Shako greets him warmly in the dome chamber and he waves Shako into a lounge chair. Rueful about descendants: he says he made the mistake of getting his descendants out of trouble again and again until he washed his hands of them. Earnest in work: Rufus finds him "earnest and diligent" in a role normally handled by the church of Fertility. Prime vessel of the Reaper. With Raythe he leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft. Someone who has known Velius a very long time calls him "an old friend". Raythe: fellow peak diamond-ranker.
304.name: Velius

305.content: Vesta Carmis Zell is the astral king who rules the messenger forces around Yaresh and keeps her servants capped with seals. Cold, curious and acquisitive, she treats the lives of her servants as experiments. Cold and curious: she watches servant race armies battle to the death, resurrecting them and bestowing abilities "to keep things interesting". Soul engineer: known for her fascination with soul engineering. Separate goals: she chose a separate goal from the rest of the group and is young. She feels one of her seals vanish when Jason removes it from Tera. Jason says Vesta used Tera, keeping her at silver rank. "The astral king who rules the local messenger forces" and a known practitioner of soul engineering. Marek served her until recently. Jamis Fran Muskar: fellow king.
305.name: Vesta Carmis Zell

306.content: Vincent Baudrillard is a French swordsman from Saint-Étienne whom Rufus picked out young, now an upper-silver adventurer and Emi's love interest in 2038. Anxious and earnest around Emi, he is flustered by Jason's attention and by her teasing. Anxious: pacing around a rooftop garden while Emi eats a sandwich and teases him. Driven: his drive is more valuable than his talent; the Remore teaching method gives the most time to those with motivation. Swordsman, close to gold: his aura is in the upper reaches of silver. Rufus picked him out early for his swordsmanship and self-motivation. Member of the Baudrillard family; Chloe Baudrillard, an epidemiologist Jason befriended, is of the same family. Jason has watched him grow from a boy to a man through the domain. Emi: love interest; Jason's interest is as a match for her, and rank matters for the ageing question.
306.name: Vincent Baudrillard

307.content: Vincent Trenslow is an Adventure Society official in Greenstone with a magnificent moustache, who runs Jason's field assessment and speaks to him with strict professionalism. By Book 12 he is a drooping senior official preparing for a shipload of gold-rankers. Professional: Rufus notes his manner "had been nothing but professional". Barking: "Mercer, if I see you try to use an ability on a fellow candidate again, you will fail on the spot". Disdainful of favouritism: he shows "a hint of disdain around the eyes" at Guy's division of the group. Unhappy official: he explains an administrative error "unhappily". He uses a silver-grey recording crystal during assessments. He identifies thirteen ratlings that would run to their burrows. Rufus worked closely with him during the last field assessment and called him "exactly what I expect from a Society official". He extends the director's apologies and says she is "new to the role". Rufus: worked together on the assessment. Elspeth Arella: his director.
307.name: Vincent Trenslow

308.content: Yumi Asano is Jason's paternal grandmother and the matriarch of the Asano clan. She came to magic late in life and her flesh-shaping powers restored her youth, so she looks no older than Jason. Authoritative, affectionate and unimpressed by his status, she pushes him to formalise the clan. Stern: Jason greets her "G'day, Nanna... Sorry, Grandmother" and earns a glare. Deliberate: she quietly takes in Jason's explanation, sipping tea, before responding. Scolding: she scolds Jason "in a very matronly tone". Wary: she wonders whether any of the boy she knew is still inside Jason. Forbids members going far outside the domain. Jason's paternal grandmother. Book 12 also calls a woman named Noriko "matriarch of the Asano clan"; the two descriptions are not reconciled (open question). Erika: shares contribution-point plans.
308.name: Yumi Asano

309.content: Zara is a celestine princess of the Storm Kingdom, the "Hurricane Princess". Jason meets her in a tent during the contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, when she is nineteen and he is iron-rank. Years later the scandal of her false engagement claim, her loss of the succession, and her adoption into her mother's house bring her to Team Biscuit and, in 2038, into a romance with Jason. Powers: wind and water, big storms; recovery, speed, astral and holy affinity. Rank: gold by Book 12: she stays in a suite fit for gold-rank adventurers and calls up a storm of gold-rank force; her rank when she first meets Jason is not stated in the chapters read.
309.name: Zara Rimaros (Zara Nareen)

310.content: Zareen Rimaros is Liara and Baseph's middle child: a three-star adventurer and political enthusiast with the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes. She serves as the royal family's liaison to Jason in Rimaros, is proposed as a political match, and in Book 13 is a lady in waiting to Princess Zara on the embassy to Earth. Her sister Dara and brother Joseph are covered in Baseph_and_the_Rimaros_Children.md. Family: "Dara was the eldest and, like the middle child, Zareen, had followed their mother into adventuring"; the youngest, Joseph, is an administrator. Appearance: "physically smaller" than her sister, not inheriting her mother's height, but with "the iconic sapphire hair and eyes of the royal family". Politics, not combat: she is "much more interested in politics than her mother", and was close to Vesper, "picking up her relative's taste for the politics that Liara disdained but could never seem to escape". Interest in Jason: "I'm more interested in the man himself... Is it true that his aura is as strong as a gold-ranker's?" and Liara scolds her "Don't even think about it". Jason later says he is "not looking for the entanglements a political marriage would bring". A political match: Zara notes whether Jason chooses "Zareen, myself, someone else or no one at all" is up to him; Dara and Baseph exchange looks about Zareen's absence from dinner. Rufus guesses she would be the royal choice, since her sister is "pure adventurer" without political sensibilities.
310.name: Zareen Rimaros

311.content: Zato is the silver-rank leader of the Builder cult's local forces in Book 3, a metal-bodied shapeshifter who recruits Thadwick, drives the cult's survivors to the Vane Estate and is the final opponent of Jason's team. He is competent, unfazed and sure of victory. On top of things: Jason says "He does seem pretty on top of things... I actually kind of like him" and invites him to join team "Hopelessly Outmatched". Convinced of victory: "Zato knew that his victory was imminent. He knew that the adventurers were no match for his power". Quiet in command: he stands with his back to the door, eyes lingering on Timos's neck marks, saying nothing. Recruiter: "I see your true potential". Silver rank, with a metal body of shifting abilities. Immovable in the final fight: no damage seems to impair him, even Humphrey's strikes. Trump card: after baiting out Sophie's absorb power, his body explodes into a mass of shrapnel. "The last silver-ranker left in the Builder cult's local forces"; tasked with leading the evacuation when the island stronghold was invaded, he escaped with a good number of people, though none of the other silver-rankers survived. Thadwick Mercer: his recruit. Humphrey and Sophie: opponents in the climax. Timos: his follower, whose neck he notices.
311.name: Zato

312.content: Zithis Carrow Vayel is the messenger recruited as a sixteen-year-old diamond-ranker to become the new Builder, named on the Fundamental Realm Authority Token Jason loots. He is rarely seen; his prime vessel Erigo Fin Desca is the character to use in scenes. Boris counts him among the few who can truly shake the cosmos. Jason tells Allayeth: "His name is Zithis Carrow Vayel. He was a sixteen-year-old diamond-ranker when the great astral beings recruited him to replace the old Builder"; the Builder was a messenger. Jamis says Zithis's debt to the astral kings will be paid when the task is complete. Jamis Fran Muskar: creditor astral king. Erigo Fin Desca: his prime vessel.
312.name: Zithis Carrow Vayel

313.content: Jason's first familiar: a swarm of apocalypse leeches that lives in his blood, sprays out over enemies to bite and drain them, and can take the shape of a red-eyed blood clone of Jason. Colin begins as a hungry, wriggling swarm and grows into a being who talks back, waves from his bowl of leeches and calls Jason "smarmy". Named: Jason says, "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin", and calls the swarm "Leechy" in the same fight. Lives in Jason's blood: Jason pricks his finger and the leeches crawl into his hand and vanish into his blood. His rapid regeneration only works while the familiar is in his bloodstream. Method: Jason sprays him out over a target like a fire hose and Colin crawls over armour to find flesh. Colin wiggles happily when pleased. Where he comes from: a summoned familiar is created through different means from the sanguine horror, but Clive observes it is what Jason summoned, and if Jason reached diamond his familiar would reach the full strength of a sanguine horror.
313.name: Colin

314.content: Jason's third familiar: an Avatar of Doom, a floating cloak holding a nebula in the shape of an eye, circled by blue and orange eye-orbs that fire beams. He cannot speak, but he answers questions with his orbs and has a distinct personality, and he is the key to the intrinsic-mandate magic Jason uses to work with authority. Summoned: the doom essence ability Avatar of Doom summons a familiar. At first it is unnamed, an iron-rank incorporeal familiar whose orbs make sustained beams, one of disruptive force and one of resonating force, and whose damage leaves Vulnerable. Named: asked if it wants a name, it flashes its blue orb, and Jason says, "I'm going to call you... Gordon". Orange is no and blue is yes: Gordon's orange orb flashes brightly as his signal for no. Shade relays him: "Gordon says that I should be last". Appearance: a disembodied cloak with a nebula-like cloud of blue and orange in the shape of an eye, and eyeball-patterned orbs drifting around it that fire unrelenting beams. In a fight: his beams inflict Vulnerable on a lizard; his energy dash is fast but his reflexes are sluggish, and a blow can dissipate his vessel entirely.
314.name: Gordon

315.content: Clive Standish's familiar: a rune tortoise whose shell carries runes that throw elemental attacks, and whose shell the whole team rides in, shelters in and runs the battlefield from. Onslow is gentle and a little stubborn, and Clive talks to him as "little buddy". First sight: Onslow is at the front of Clive's airboat with his head jutting forward "like a dog with its head out a car window". Clive sits on his shell with Jason beside him. Powers: he fires elemental attacks from the magic runes on his shell, which Clive recharges with his own mana. A rune dims when he takes a hit. A seat for the team: Clive picks up Stash and climbs on Onslow's shell with Neil, and the tortoise floats off the rooftop on a cushion of air. Clive drops down off him when the tower is threatened.
315.name: Onslow

316.content: Jason's shadow familiar, a formal, dry astral being who is one of the Reaper's shadows. He first appears as the keeper of the Reaper trials, becomes Jason's closest and most constant companion, and acts as his butler, driver, spy and sounding board. He says himself that he is a shepherd of death, and that he has changed more than the others of his kind. The invigilator: he appears as the shadowy figure who runs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes and offers to explain their practical dangers or their origins. He hands out vials and medallions with his shadowy hands, which are cold to the touch. A familiar before: he tells the competitors that the grandmaster who built the place was an outworlder with the dark essence like Jason, "I was his summoned familiar once". Summoned by Jason: when Jason chooses to summon a familiar after the trials, he greets Shade with "I was hoping it would be you". Bodies: he appears as three bodies that become horses for a ride or large lizards for rough terrain, and his bodies move among monsters as elusive shadowy figures. The Reaper's child: the Reaper says "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path".
316.name: Shade

317.content: Belinda Callahan's astral lantern: a small living lantern that orbits her, projects shields, fires force bolts and feeds mana to her team. It is the quietest of the team's familiars, but it is on the field in almost every battle. Summoned: the final ability of Belinda's power set is a summoned familiar, an astral lantern. Belinda names it: "How about Shimmer?". In a fight: it projects shields to protect the team and, with Gordon, beams the enemy to split their attention. The force bolts of a lantern familiar prove more dangerous to its own side against Hendren's defences.
317.name: Shimmer

318.content: Humphrey Geller's bonded familiar: a baby mirage dragon whose full name is Velitraxistaasch, who prefers "Stash". He changes shape constantly, starts as a barking lizard, a bird or a puppy and ends up large enough to crush a company of messengers, and he talks, mostly in cheerful, blunt remarks. Name: "It's short for Velitraxistaasch. He likes 'Stash,' though.". Jason works out what he is at once and Humphrey is startled. Bond: "Our mothers arranged him becoming my familiar. Or me becoming his person, depending on how you look at it". A bonded familiar is an actual magical creature that can die, unlike a summoned familiar. Shapes: a canary on Humphrey's head and a puppy, a bird that swoops from the sky and turns into a puppy in his arms, a barking lizard, and a bark lurker or a darting bird in a fight. Biscuits: Jason feeds him a biscuit and he turns into a puppy to snuffle it from Jason's hand, then yaps his agreement. Speech: "Stash chase worm! Stash chase worm!". Scouting: he leads Humphrey's party by barking in the right direction to the margolls. Special attack: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
318.name: Stash

319.content: This file gathers who is related to whom in the six family lines roleplay needs most: the Asano family (with the Evans line through Erika), the Remores, the Gellers, the Mercers and their circle, and the Rimaros royal house. It adds nothing that the character files do not already cite; its job is to put the links in one place. The file is level 3 throughout because it names deaths and Book 13 outcomes.
319.name: Family Trees

key: Knowledge States: Who Knows What, and When
320.comment: Knowledge States: Who Knows What, and When
320.content: This file tracks four things a roleplayer needs to keep straight for the core characters: whether the character knows that Jason is an outworlder from Earth, how much they know about the party interface and the later System, what they know about the Earth-Pallimustus link and Earth's magic, and what they know of Knowledge's plan. For each, it names the earliest scene where the text shows the character knowing, and the band of books that scene falls in. It is the character-by-character companion to the secrets table in Spoiler_Management.md.
keys: Knowledge States: Who Knows What, and When
320.name: Knowledge States: Who Knows What, and When

321.content: This file lists romantic ties and standing rivalries between named characters, in the order a reader meets them. Romances are given as pairs with the book they begin, change or end; rivalries are given with what each side wants. It is level 3 because it includes outcomes up to Book 13.
321.name: Romances and Rivalries

322.content: This file lists the named adventuring teams and who was on them, by era. Roster changes (deaths, departures) are noted where the text gives them. It is level 3 because rosters run to Book 13.
322.name: Teams by Era

323.content: - Jason left Earth in late November and returned in early June, a year and a half later. - His birthday is 1 April ("April Fool's Day"); he has just turned 26 in Book 5.
323.name: Master Timeline

324.content: Boko is destroyed on the day an assassin spears Jason's avatar there. Jason uses his aura to lift the city's people out and drop them in the desert, holds his draining power while the containment ritual is built, and dies in the blast. A messenger army then descends on the survivors until Jason's ghost-fire phoenix form rises from the crater. The survivors are sheltered in his astral kingdom.
324.name: The Boko Evacuation (Book 12)

325.content: The messenger war is the long conflict between the winged servants of the astral kings and the people of Pallimustus, with Jason caught between them as a would-be astral king. It begins with the invasion of the south in Book 9, includes the Battle of Yaresh and the Cardinas expedition, and ends with the reprisal at Boko and an uneasy peace in Books 12-13. This file sets out the sequence; the Battle of Yaresh and the Cardinas expedition have their own era guides.
325.name: The Messenger War (Books 7-13)

key: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
326.comment: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
326.content: During the Rimaros monster surge, the Builder cult sends mobile cities against the Storm Kingdom: a ground city that walks south, an underwater city and a flying fortress-city that appears over Livaros. The adventurers answer with six diamond-rankers, gods' miracles and a single true bomb carried into the flying city. The war is later called the War of Four Cities or the One Day War.
keys: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)
326.name: The One Day War (War of Four Cities)

327.content: The Earth vampire war runs in two phases: a first war that "ended without conclusion" when both sides were exhausted and the vampires got nuclear weapons, then a renewed war that was in full swing again by the Book 13 symposium and ends at McKean's castle. This file collects the duration statements. For the events, see../Era_Guides/Earth_Vampire_War.md.
327.name: The Vampire War (Books 5-13)

key: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh
328.comment: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
328.content: After a four-month journey south from Rimaros, Jason's convoy reaches the rainforest elf city of Yaresh as messengers besiege it. The Church of Knowledge gathers an army in the background, the messengers use apocalypse beasts and world-taker worms as weapons, and the battle ends with a breach the messengers' commander Marek has to concede. Jason's identity as an astral king comes out, and Marek and Tera become his captives. Messenger agents in the city: Benella presents Jason to Kaal as a threat; Fal Vin Garath calls Shade "Reaper spawn". Apocalypse beasts and worms: Carlos suspects a heat-consuming parasite with a swarm hive mind; "[Inexorable Doom] on [World-Taker Worm]"; the messengers know the apocalypse beasts and use them as weapons. Defence plans: the two cloud palaces are reconfigured into defence bunkers; Hana directs the clergy away from Jason's bunker.
