The trigger: an Adventure Society functionary hides his anger behind an aura mask; a naga egg is triggered in the city. The breach: Marek Nior Vargas leads the breach force over the entertainment district; the breach is a trap. Eilaf Hayel commands the defence of the entertainment district. Intervention: Raythe tells Schaat "Leave Asano be. Turn around and leave this city"; Schaat is found dead. The duel: Tera Jun Casta challenges Jason; Jason's last word stops her dead.
keys: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)
Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh
328.name: Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)

key: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone
329.comment: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
329.content: For about a year after the Reaper trials, a hidden cult of the Builder works inside Greenstone's aristocracy and through the church of Purity. It implants star seeds, suborns Thadwick Mercer and others, and prepares to claim an astral space. Jason's team learns of it in Book 2 and breaks it in Book 3, ending in the astral space the cult built and the death of Jason.
keys: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)
Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone
329.name: Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)

key: Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone (Books 10-11)
Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone
330.comment: Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone (Books 10-11)
330.content: A descending expedition goes beneath Yaresh to stop the messengers' device from turning the city's natural array into a soul forge. In Book 10 the allies reach the brightheart city of Cardinas, face the Church of Undeath and Hero's divine power; in Book 11 the failed forge becomes a transformation zone that Jason must claim territory by territory. It ends with Jason holding the astral throne, gate and soul forge, and with Rufus and Taika leaving for Earth.
keys: Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone (Books 10-11)
Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone
330.name: Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone (Books 10-11)

key: Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War (Books 5-13)
Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War
331.comment: Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War (Books 5-13)
331.content: When transformation events release reality cores, ancient vampires wake and feed on blood infused with core energy. They take most of Europe and Russia under a queen, Elizabeth, then fight the Network and the Earth powers for two decades, with Jason cleaning their domain in Book 12 and the Earth forces storming Belgrade and Simon McKean's castle in Book 13. This guide follows the war across the series.
keys: Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War (Books 5-13)
Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War
331.name: Era Guide: The Earth Vampire War (Books 5-13)

key: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves
332.comment: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
332.content: Jason wakes on Earth in early June, a year and a half after he left. Earth's magic is rising; the Network, the Cabal and the Engineers of Ascension fight for influence, monsters arrive in waves, vampires rise, and Jason builds a family compound, a clan and his first Earth domains. The era ends with Jason leaving Earth, in a warm French autumn.
keys: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)
Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves
332.name: Era Guide: Earth and the Monster Waves (Books 4-6)

333.content: After Farrah's death, Emir Bahadir opens an astral space in the delta and invites iron-rank teams to compete for the legacy of the Order of the Reaper. The City of Fallen Echoes holds the trials, a shipful of time-displaced priests and a Reaper-run test of virtue. Jason's team wins a set of rewards, and the tale of the Order's survival becomes a live question. Launch: iron-rankers board the cloud ship once the palace has resumed its shape; adventurers spread across Sky Scar Lake by every means. The zone is "City of Fallen Echoes (Gate Tower Three)". Shade's account: the legacy goes to whoever embodies the ideals of the Order; the last grandmaster sent all the initiates into the city; the vorger do not kill, and the initiates were turned into abominations. The city: siege golems and flesh abominations adapt to how they are fought. Imran Keane joins Jason's party. A blood root vine is hit with Inexorable Doom. Rival teams: Padma's team is the last to join, and Beth's team stays put beside Jason's near the end. Before the trials Beth's and Rick's teams had met in the mirage chamber contest. All reach the city centre, where Humphrey's team staggers in ragged. The final day: Shade announces that the second trial ends in one day and warns of nightmare hags, diamond-rank astral entities. Rewards include a True Light, Summoner's Die: Form and an Immortal Crest.
333.name: Era Guide: The Reaper Trials (Book 2)

334.content: Jason returns to Pallimustus at the standing stones in a cyclone, just as a long-delayed monster surge begins. In the Storm Kingdom he meets its royal family, settles at Palisaros, helps defeat the Builder's invasion in the One Day War, and then faces the Order of Redeeming Light, a mining complex rescue and the birth of his astral kingdom. The era ends with the Builder withdrawing and Jason technically an astral king.
334.name: Era Guide: The Rimaros Surge (Books 7-8)

key: Era Guide: The Return and the Bridge (Books 12-13)
Era Guide: The Return and the Bridge
335.comment: Era Guide: The Return and the Bridge (Books 12-13)
335.content: After roughly fifteen years away, Jason returns to Pallimustus' cities, destroys Boko by accident of assassination, meets the Council of Kings, triggers the System's withdrawal from regions that keep indenture, and then sails with his friends to Earth to build the bridge. In 2038 he tells the world about the great astral beings and Knowledge's plan, ends the vampire war with his allies, and stands at the bridge anchor site.

Era Guide: The Return and the Bridge
335.name: Era Guide: The Return and the Bridge (Books 12-13)

336.content: Single-use stones that awaken an essence ability, found, traded and rewarded by rank and rarity. What they do: "An awakening stone that unlocks the power of consumption... Effect: Awakens an essence ability", requiring an unawakened essence ability. The stone melts into the user's hand "with little fanfare". Why they matter: Rufus tells Jason he cannot "properly progress towards bronze rank until you awaken every essence ability you have. That's all twenty". Naming and rarity: stones are "unranked" and carry a rarity, such as the Awakening Stone of the Feast, of Adventure, of the Stars and of the Reaper. Affinity: the Reaper stone "sharing affinity with the Reaper" is used in Jason's awakening ritual with the Reaper token, and it gives Humphrey, a human, a special attack. Divine awakening stones: a god-made stone is "transcendent rank, epic" and bestows a specific aura power. Sources: looting an awakening stone or essence can pay better than the contract to kill the monster; the Adventure Society gives stones for exceptional service, "although rarely", and some open contracts offer them as rewards; otherwise stones are bought through brokers, almost always at auction, at exorbitant prices. Brokers in a small city hold the valuable stuff, like essences and stones, for big auctions. Family supply: the Gellers traditionally supply their scions with enough stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
336.name: Awakening Stones

337.content: The badge as an object: how an Adventure Society badge is made, tied to its wearer, tracked, altered and replaced, and what a guild membership adds on top. The organisation file explains what the Society does with badges; this file is about the item and the ways it fails. Who makes it: the Adventure Society manages the badges but the Magic Society creates them, taking an aura imprint from the new member inside a magic circle in about a minute. What it carries: every badge is paired with a tracking stone that tells the Society whether the member is alive or dead and finds them if they go missing. Members claim adventure notices with it and hold it against a security screen to close a contract. The wallet: the badge is a circular iron medallion embossed with a sword and rod crossed over a shield, carried in a leather wallet. Stars are on the metal: an official taps a wedge-shaped stone to the badge and a star is added, or removed. It tracks the badge, not the person: the tracking stones trace the badges, so a discarded badge hides its owner. A change of aura leaves the imprint on the badge unmatched, so the wearer cannot be tracked until a new badge is issued. When the Society wanted people's auras re-examined, their badges were also to be replaced. Jason's case: the stone cannot track his aura imprint, and Farrah says some people have abilities that block magical tracking.
337.name: Badges and Guild Membership

338.content: Emir's cloud ship and palace, and Jason's own cloud houses, yachts and palaces made from his Cloud Flask. Emir's cloud ship: it arrives at the Greenstone dock and a walkway of cloud connects to the shore as a hole opens in its side. Moored, it morphs over about ten minutes into a palace of clouds floating on the water. Emir's cloud palace: floating just offshore on the north side of the Island, "fully exposed to the waves and currents, yet remained as immovable as solid ground", with wings and towers in blue, purple, orange and gold. Walls, floors and ceilings glow with absorbed sunlight the palace stores and distributes, and the floors have a bouncy-castle spring. Low-magic limits: out of Greenstone the ship's full functionality is restored when Emir's cloud ship floats above Kurdansk. Team base: Jason's team move into Emir's palace after the contest. Jason's Cloud Flask: it creates buildings and vehicles of cloud, with forms limited by rank, iron cloud houses, bronze cloud vehicles and silver cloud palaces; items inside a returned construct are stored in a dimensional space until another is formed. Disguised constructs: in Venice his family and Dawn stay in a cloud palace disguised as a yacht.
338.name: Cloud Constructs and Cloud Palaces

key: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
339.comment: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
339.content: Single-use and crafting items: the City of Fallen Echoes rewards, clockwork cores, reality cores and star seeds. Lesser Miracle Potion: "iron rank, legendary", "Salvation in a bottle", it fully restores health, mana and stamina but only works on normal and iron-rank people, and its lingering magic delays other recovery. Medallion of Escape: "silver rank, uncommon", evacuates the holder from the astral space when their aura is projected into it, and only works inside the City of Fallen Echoes. Immortal Crest: "iron rank, rare", lets a mystical tattooist draw out a soul crest and only works on an iron-rank essence user. Summoner's Die: Form: "iron rank [growth], legendary", it randomly alters the form of an iron-rank summon. Clockwork Core: "iron rank, rare", the core of an artificial monster that simplifies the materials and processes of a construct creature; clockwork cores are made by clockwork kings. Star seeds: great astral beings, not gods, "can send their followers star seeds"; once implanted and germinated the body transforms, "minor or major". Reality cores: roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg, dark crystal glowing with transcendent light; one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it. They are the source of the transformation zones' treasures and are common in node space.
keys: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
339.name: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials

key: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
340.comment: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
340.content: The vehicles that cross the desert around Greenstone: the sand skimmers and sand barges Emir Bahadir's people run, the carriages that move expeditions to relay stations, and the monstrous Ustei war barge. Emir's cloud ship is covered in Cloud_Constructs_and_Palaces.md. Sand skimmers: small desert vehicles that carry a party across the sand. Emir leaves skimmers waiting at Boko to carry the team into the desert. Pushed past their limits: one of Emir's people specialises in magical tools and can periodically push the skimmers to speeds beyond their normal capability, so the whole vehicle vibrates. Their limits: skimmers cannot go through an astral-space aperture, so the party continues on foot. Requisitioned skimmers: expeditions requisition extra skimmers from the city and return them afterwards. Sand barges: larger vessels that move people and supplies overland. After Emir's ship sails south down the coast and into shore at an unremarkable patch of desert, his people unload three sand barges that carry the whole group inland to Sky Scar Lake. The trip takes hours more, into the night. Expedition transport: an expedition leaving Greenstone uses carriages to reach desert relay stations, then the captured Ustei barge and smaller barges supplied by the Magic Society.
keys: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
340.name: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges

341.content: How things and people are carried across a world without carts or roads: storage spaces that hold a person's goods, dimensional bags that expand them, and portal abilities that move people between places they have seen. Jason's own inventory and shadow gates are the best-documented examples, and the rest of the world treats both as everyday professional tools with hard limits. Jason's inventory is "a video-game inventory only Jason could see", unlike Clive's storage, which is opened by making a circle of floating runes with a portal inside. Dimensional bags are items with a rank. They add slots to an inventory in proportion to their rank, and at iron rank one bag slot is available and holds only iron-rank bags. Bags come in novelty shapes, such as a pair of boots. Storage as a profession: adventurers carry their possessions in dimensional bags or dimensional space abilities and travel light. Some portal workers "aren't even adventurers and do storage space transport for a living". Loot goes straight in: looted coins appear in the storage abilities of Clive, Humphrey and Jason, and Jason keeps a ledger of how much belongs to whom. Storage can be looted: Jason could have taken the items from Farrah's storage space by looting her body like a monster, and neither man suggested such a defilement. Limits on contents: it is "almost impossible to place living material inside dimensional storage", with only a few carefully chosen plants viable.
341.name: Dimensional Storage and Portals

342.content: The reforged form of Jason's sword Dread Salvation and the scabbard that was made with it. Hegemon's Will is the weapon and Hegemon's Dominion is the scabbard; the game treats them as one item. The scabbard stores afflictions that land on Jason and turns them against the next enemy he cuts. Soul_Bound_Items_and_Regalia.md covers where the sword came from; this file covers what the two pieces do. Hegemon's Dominion: "silver rank [growth], legendary", "the scabbard to Hegemon's Will" and "the embodiment of hegemonic control, representing the hegemon's mastery of his domain". Bound to Jason: it cannot be used by anyone else, shares his ability to ignore rank disparity, and is "treated as the same item" as the sword for all magical effects. What the scabbard does: afflictions affecting the wielder are periodically moved to it, which removes their effects from him but is not a cleansing effect. The rate depends on the effects' rank relative to the wielder; suppressing the originator's aura speeds the transfer and being aura suppressed slows it. If the sword is sheathed, all afflictions pass to the weapon and affect the next enemy struck. Anything the target resists or is immune to is negated and cannot be passed to another target. Growth: its growth is no longer capped by rank, but the upgrade materials are ones Jason has never heard of and are presumably gold rank.
342.name: Hegemon's Will and Hegemon's Dominion

343.content: Jason's combat robes are the flowing, tailored armour that gives him his dark, shadowy look. The first is the Trap Weaver Battle Robe, bought from Gilbert Bertinelli in Book 1; it is replaced at each rank by a new robe made by Gilbert from monster materials Jason supplies. The robes are armour in a robe's cut, stored in his inventory and swapped on by the outfits tab.
343.name: Jason's Combat Robes

344.content: Reality cores are egg-sized crystals of concentrated power found at transformation events on Earth. Factions fight over them, vampires use them to power their blood, and Jason's work shuts the supply off. Genesis cores are different: Jason loots them from anomalies in the zones to expand his spirit domain.
344.name: Reality Cores and Genesis Cores

key: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
345.comment: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
345.content: Jason's three soul-bound growth items, joined in Book 6 into the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon by the Soul-Imprinting Triune, plus the Robes of the Astral Verdict. Dread Salvation: a sword "crafted with gratitude, in hope it would be of the greatest use in the moment of greatest need"; "iron rank [growth], legendary"; when an affliction special attack meets a physical immunity it gains Stone Cutter, and for a magical immunity Spell Breaker. Gary made it, as a gift. Dread Salvation in Book 6: bronze rank, bound to Jason and sharing his ability to ignore rank disparity; it can be imbued with aura for damage at an ongoing mana cost; "The original creator must demonstrate his growth and reforge the weapon". The window says it "must be reforged by the original craftsperson in order to advance further". The reforged sword is named Hegemon's Will on its item screen, with its scabbard Hegemon's Dominion treated as the same item; Gary gives it to Jason in Book 7. The reforging by Gary and Virid is Book 7, Ch2 L73-74. Cloud Flask: iron rank growth item that Jason binds in Book 2; it creates cloud buildings and vehicles, with forms limited by rank. By Book 6 it is silver rank, with the cloud house at iron, cloud vehicle at bronze and cloud palace at silver. Its maker is "some unknown diamond-rank craftsman".
keys: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
345.name: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon

346.content: A soul forge is the third part, with the astral throne and astral gate, of a full astral kingdom; it is used for soul engineering. Every astral king has one except Jason until Book 11. The messengers' attempt to turn the Cardinas natural array into one corrupts the array into a birthing tree; Jason separates the three and claims the forge in his own soul realm.
346.name: The Soul Forge

key: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
347.comment: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
347.content: The Builder's astral door, the Fundament Gate that Jason absorbs, and how they let him work in the fundamental realm. The door: Mr North tells Jason "It's not a literal door... It's an astral construct with the power to manifest in physical reality in the form of a portal", and that Jason must absorb it so it cannot be taken from him. Jason notes "This door is an object of the Builder". The Fundament Gate: a ring of rough marble standing stones in a dell, "transcendent rank, legendary", whose window lets Jason incorporate it into his Spirit Vault, purging the Builder's influence. It improves his sense of Builder items and adds to Path of Shadows the ability to open a portal to the Fundamental Realm. Consequences: Jason used the Builder's door when he flooded himself with magic and later "accidentally trashed it for parts"; "the magic of the Builder's door that Jason had absorbed" is distinct from the soul-attack trick he learned from the star seed. Builder's view: in Book 6 Shako says that without the Fundament Gate the Builder forged, Jason could not have remade the zone, and Dawn asks for the designs so the World-Phoenix can create a complementary item to anchor the bridge. Later items: the Fundamental Realm Authority Token and the Firmamental Bridge Anchor are looted from the destroyed artefacts; see Tokens_Stones_and_Relics.md.
keys: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate
347.name: The Builder's Door and the Fundament Gate

348.content: Transcendent-rank items that mark the favour or authority of great astral beings and gods: astral blessing tokens, divine awakening stones, the Fundamental Realm Authority Token and the Cup of Heroes. Astral blessing tokens: Clive says they are "something great astral beings give out to bestow blessings, as signs of approval"; they trigger racial gift evolutions, and are harmless, unlike star seeds. World-Phoenix Token: Jason finds it in his starting inventory, "transcendent rank, legendary", "Uses remaining: 1/1" with unreadable effects. It is consumed in Book 3. Reaper Token: an obsidian square engraved with a silver scythe, "transcendent rank, legendary". Jason takes the Scythe of the Reaper by placing his inventory window behind it, and the token is added. It is melded into his body with the awakening stone of the Reaper in Clive's ritual and consumed. Knowledge's token: a small stone square like the World-Phoenix Token but washed-out blue, offered with two awakening stones; Jason is told it would take him home and wonders whether to trust it.
348.name: Tokens, Stones and Relics
